meta.author_uz: Lev Nikolayevich Tolstoy (1828–1910) — rus yozuvchisi, «Urush va tinchlik» va «Anna Karenina» muallifi. 1870-yillar oxiridagi ma'naviy inqirozdan keyin u axloq va din masalalariga bag'ishlangan asarlar yozdi; «Ivan Ilichning o'limi» (1886) shu davrning eng mashhur asari.

chapters.title: I. The news of a death

paras.en: Inside the great building of the Law Courts, during the interval in the hearing of the Melvinsky case, the members of the judicial council and the public prosecutor were gathered together in the private room of Ivan Yegorovitch Shebek, and the conversation turned upon the celebrated Krasovsky case. Fyodor Vassilievitch hotly maintained that the case was not in the jurisdiction of the court. Yegor Ivanovitch stood up for his own view; but from the first Pyotr Ivanovitch, who had not entered into the discussion, took no interest in it, but was looking through the newspapers which had just been brought in.
paras.uz: Sud saroyining ulkan binosida, Melvinskiy ishi tinglovidagi tanaffus paytida, sud kengashi a'zolari va prokuror Ivan Yegorovich Shebekning shaxsiy xonasiga yig'ilishgan edi va gap mashhur Krasovskiy ishiga borib taqaldi. Fyodor Vasilyevich ish bu sudning vakolatiga kirmaydi, deb qizg'in turib oldi. Yegor Ivanovich o'z fikrini himoya qildi; Pyotr Ivanovich esa munozaraga boshidanoq qo'shilmay, unga qiziqmay, endigina olib kelingan gazetalarni varaqlab o'tirardi.

paras.en: “Gentlemen!” he said, “Ivan Ilyitch is dead!”
paras.uz: — Janoblar! — dedi u. — Ivan Ilich o'libdi!

paras.en: “You don’t say so!”
paras.uz: — Nahotki!

paras.en: “Here, read it,” he said to Fyodor Vassilievitch, handing him the fresh still damp-smelling paper.
paras.uz: — Mana, o'qing, — dedi u Fyodor Vasilyevichga hali bo'yog'ining namligi hidi ketmagan yangi gazetani uzatib.

paras.en: Within a black margin was printed: “Praskovya Fyodorovna Golovin with heartfelt affliction informs friends and relatives of the decease of her beloved husband, member of the Court of Justice, Ivan Ilyitch Golovin, who passed away on the 4th of February. The funeral will take place on Thursday at one o’clock.”
paras.uz: Qora hoshiya ichida shunday bosilgan edi: «Praskovya Fyodorovna Golovina chuqur qayg'u bilan do'stlar va qarindoshlarga sevimli eri, Sud palatasi a'zosi Ivan Ilich Golovinning 4-fevralda vafot etganini ma'lum qiladi. Dafn marosimi payshanba kuni soat birda bo'ladi.»

paras.en: Ivan Ilyitch was a colleague of the gentlemen present, and all liked him. It was some weeks now since he had been taken ill; his illness had been said to be incurable. His post had been kept open for him, but it had been thought that in case of his death Alexyeev might receive his appointment, and either Vinnikov or Shtabel would succeed to Alexyeev’s. So that on hearing of Ivan Ilyitch’s death, the first thought of each of the gentlemen in the room was of the effect this death might have on the transfer or promotion of themselves or their friends.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich bu yerda o'tirgan janoblarning hamkasbi edi va hammasi uni yaxshi ko'rardi. U kasal bo'lib yotganiga bir necha hafta bo'lgan edi; kasalligi davosiz, deyishardi. Uning lavozimi saqlab turilgan edi, lekin u vafot etsa, o'rniga Alekseyev tayinlanishi, Alekseyevning o'rniga esa yo Vinnikov, yo Shtabel o'tishi mumkin, deb o'ylanardi. Shuning uchun Ivan Ilichning o'limini eshitgan zahoti xonadagi har bir janobning birinchi o'yi bu o'lim o'zining yoki tanishlarining boshqa joyga o'tishi yoki lavozimi oshishiga qanday ta'sir qilishi haqida bo'ldi.

paras.en: “Now I am sure of getting Shtabel’s place or Vinnikov’s,” thought Fyodor Vassilievitch. “It was promised me long ago, and the promotion means eight hundred roubles additional income, besides the grants for office expenses.”
paras.uz: «Endi Shtabelning yoki Vinnikovning o'rni menga tegishi aniq, — deb o'yladi Fyodor Vasilyevich. — Bu menga allaqachon va'da qilingan, lavozim oshishi esa idora xarajatlari uchun beriladigan pullardan tashqari yiliga sakkiz yuz rubl qo'shimcha daromad degani.»

paras.en: “Now I shall have to petition for my brother-in-law to be transferred from Kaluga,” thought Pyotr Ivanovitch. “My wife will be very glad. She won’t be able to say now that I’ve never done anything for her family.”
paras.uz: «Endi qaynog'amni Kalugadan bu yerga o'tkazish uchun ariza berishim kerak bo'ladi, — deb o'yladi Pyotr Ivanovich. — Xotinim juda xursand bo'ladi. Endi u men uning qarindoshlari uchun hech narsa qilmaganman, deya olmaydi.»

paras.en: “I thought somehow that he’d never get up from his bed again,” Pyotr Ivanovitch said aloud. “I’m sorry!”
paras.uz: — Negadir u to'shakdan boshqa turmaydi, deb o'ylagan edim, — dedi Pyotr Ivanovich ovoz chiqarib. — Achinarli!

paras.en: “But what was it exactly that was wrong with him?”
paras.uz: — Unga aslida nima bo'lgan edi o'zi?

paras.en: “The doctors could not decide. That’s to say, they did decide, but differently. When I saw him last, I thought he would get over it.”
paras.uz: — Doktorlar aniqlay olishmadi. Ya'ni aniqlashdi-yu, har xil aniqlashdi. Uni oxirgi marta ko'rganimda, tuzalib ketadi, deb o'ylagan edim.

paras.en: “Well, I positively haven’t called there ever since the holidays. I’ve kept meaning to go.”
paras.uz: — Men esa bayramlardan beri u yerga umuman bormadim. Doim boraman, deb yurardim.

paras.en: “Had he any property?”
paras.uz: — Uning mol-mulki bormidi?

paras.en: “I think there’s something, very small, of his wife’s. But something quite trifling.”
paras.uz: — Menimcha, xotinining ozgina narsasi bor. Lekin juda arzimas.

paras.en: “Yes, one will have to go and call. They live such a terribly long way off.”
paras.uz: — Ha, borib ko'ngil so'rash kerak bo'ladi. Ular juda uzoqda yashashadi-da.

paras.en: “A long way from you, you mean. Everything’s a long way from your place.”
paras.uz: — Sizdan uzoqda demoqchisiz. Sizning uyingizdan hamma narsa uzoq.

paras.en: “There, he can never forgive me for living the other side of the river,” said Pyotr Ivanovitch, smiling at Shebek. And they began to talk of the great distances between different parts of the town, and went back into the court.
paras.uz: — Mana, daryoning narigi tomonida yashaganim uchun meni sira kechira olmaydi, — dedi Pyotr Ivanovich Shebekka jilmayib. Va ular shaharning turli qismlari orasidagi katta masofalar haqida gaplashib, sud zaliga qaytishdi.

paras.en: Besides the reflections upon the changes and promotions in the service likely to ensue from this death, the very fact of the death of an intimate acquaintance excited in everyone who heard of it, as such a fact always does, a feeling of relief that “it is he that is dead, and not I.”
paras.uz: Bu o'limdan keyin xizmatda bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan o'zgarishlar va lavozim ko'tarilishlari haqidagi mulohazalardan tashqari, yaqin tanishning o'limi haqidagi xabarning o'zi uni eshitgan har kimda, bunday xabar doim uyg'otganidek, «o'lgan u, men emas» degan yengillik hissini uyg'otdi.

paras.en: “Only think! he is dead, but here am I all right,” each one thought or felt. The more intimate acquaintances, the so-called friends of Ivan Ilyitch, could not help thinking too that now they had the exceedingly tiresome social duties to perform of going to the funeral service and paying the widow a visit of condolence.
paras.uz: «Qarang-a! U o'ldi, men esa sog'-salomatman», deb har biri o'yladi yoki his qildi. Ivan Ilichning yaqinroq tanishlari, uning do'stlari deb ataladiganlar, endi ularga dafn marosimiga borish va bevaga hamdardlik bildirish uchun kirish kabi o'ta zerikarli ijtimoiy burchlarni bajarish kerakligini ham beixtiyor o'ylashdi.

paras.en: The most intimately acquainted with their late colleague were Fyodor Vassilievitch and Pyotr Ivanovitch.
paras.uz: Marhum hamkasbni eng yaqindan bilganlar Fyodor Vasilyevich bilan Pyotr Ivanovich edi.

paras.en: Pyotr Ivanovitch had been a comrade of his at the school of jurisprudence, and considered himself under obligations to Ivan Ilyitch.
paras.uz: Pyotr Ivanovich u bilan huquqshunoslik maktabida birga o'qigan va o'zini Ivan Ilichdan qarzdor deb hisoblardi.

paras.en: Telling his wife at dinner of the news of Ivan Ilyitch’s death and his reflections as to the possibility of getting her brother transferred into their circuit, Pyotr Ivanovitch, without lying down for his usual nap, put on his frockcoat and drove to Ivan Ilyitch’s.
paras.uz: Tushlik paytida xotiniga Ivan Ilichning o'limi haqidagi xabarni va uning ukasini o'z okrugiga o'tkazish imkoniyati haqidagi o'ylarini aytib bergach, Pyotr Ivanovich odatdagi tushki uyqusiga yotmasdan, syurtugini kiydi va Ivan Ilichnikiga jo'nadi.

paras.en: At the entrance before Ivan Ilyitch’s flat stood a carriage and two hired flies. Downstairs in the entry near the hatstand there was leaning against the wall a coffin-lid with tassels and braiding freshly rubbed up with pipeclay. Two ladies were taking off their cloaks. One of them he knew, the sister of Ivan Ilyitch; the other was a lady he did not know. Pyotr Ivanovitch’s colleague, Shvarts, was coming down; and from the top stair, seeing who it was coming in, he stopped and winked at him, as though to say: “Ivan Ilyitch has made a mess of it; it’s a very different matter with you and me.”
paras.uz: Ivan Ilichning kvartirasi kiraverishida bitta kareta va ikkita yollangan izvosh turardi. Pastda, dahlizda, kiyim ilgich yonida devorga suyab qo'yilgan, tobut qopqog'i turardi: uning popuklari va jiyaklari bo'r kukuni bilan endigina tozalangan edi. Ikki xonim plashlarini yechayotgan edi. Ulardan birini u tanirdi — Ivan Ilichning singlisi; ikkinchisi u tanimaydigan xonim edi. Pyotr Ivanovichning hamkasbi Shvarts pastga tushib kelayotgan edi; u yuqori zinadan kim kirayotganini ko'rib, to'xtadi va unga ko'z qisib qo'ydi, go'yo: «Ivan Ilich ishni rasvo qilib qo'ydi; siz bilan menda esa ish butunlay boshqacha», demoqchidek.

paras.en: Shvarts’s face, with his English whiskers and all his thin figure in his frockcoat, had, as it always had, an air of elegant solemnity; and this solemnity, always such a contrast to Shvarts’s playful character, had a special piquancy here. So thought Pyotr Ivanovitch.
paras.uz: Shvartsning inglizcha bakenbardli yuzi va syurtukdagi butun ozg'in qomati, doimgidek, nafis tantanavorlik ko'rinishida edi; Shvartsning o'ynoqi tabiatiga doim zid bo'lgan bu tantanavorlik bu yerda alohida bir nash'a kasb etgan edi. Pyotr Ivanovich shunday deb o'yladi.

paras.en: Pyotr Ivanovitch let the ladies pass on in front of him, and walked slowly up the stairs after them. Shvarts had not come down, but was waiting at the top. Pyotr Ivanovitch knew what for; he wanted obviously to settle with him where their game of “screw” was to be that evening. The ladies went up to the widow’s room; while Shvarts, with his lips tightly and gravely shut, and amusement in his eyes, with a twitch of his eyebrows motioned Pyotr Ivanovitch to the right, to the room where the dead man was.
paras.uz: Pyotr Ivanovich xonimlarni oldinga o'tkazib yubordi va ularning ortidan zinadan sekin ko'tarildi. Shvarts pastga tushmagan, yuqorida kutib turardi. Pyotr Ivanovich nima uchun ekanini bilardi: u, aftidan, o'sha kecha «vint» o'yinini qayerda o'ynashlarini kelishib olmoqchi edi. Xonimlar bevaning xonasiga kirib ketishdi; Shvarts esa lablarini qattiq va jiddiy qimtib, ko'zlarida esa kulgi bilan, qoshlarini qimirlatib, Pyotr Ivanovichga o'ng tomonga — marhum yotgan xonaga ishora qildi.

paras.en: Pyotr Ivanovitch went in, as people always do on such occasions, in uncertainty as to what he would have to do there. One thing he felt sure of⁠—that crossing oneself never comes amiss on such occasions. As to whether it was necessary to bow down while doing so, he did not feel quite sure, and so chose a middle course. On entering the room he began crossing himself, and made a slight sort of bow. So far as the movements of his hands and head permitted him, he glanced while doing so about the room. Two young men, one a high school boy, nephews probably, were going out of the room, crossing themselves. An old lady was standing motionless; and a lady, with her eyebrows queerly lifted, was saying something to her in a whisper. A deacon in a frockcoat, resolute and hearty, was reading something aloud with an expression that precluded all possibility of contradiction. A young peasant who used to wait at table, Gerasim, walking with light footsteps in front of Pyotr Ivanovitch, was sprinkling something on the floor. Seeing this, Pyotr Ivanovitch was at once aware of the faint odour of the decomposing corpse. On his last visit to Ivan Ilyitch Pyotr Ivanovitch had seen this peasant in his room; he was performing the duties of a sicknurse, and Ivan Ilyitch liked him particularly. Pyotr Ivanovitch continued crossing himself and bowing in a direction intermediate between the coffin, the deacon, and the holy pictures on the table in the corner. Then when this action of making the sign of the cross with his hand seemed to him to have been unduly prolonged, he stood still and began to scrutinise the dead man.
paras.uz: Pyotr Ivanovich, bunday hollarda odamlar doim qilganidek, u yerda nima qilishi kerakligini aniq bilmagan holda ichkariga kirdi. U bir narsaga amin edi: bunday paytlarda cho'qinish hech qachon ortiqcha bo'lmaydi. Bunda ta'zim qilish ham kerakmi-yo'qmi, bunga uncha amin emas edi, shuning uchun o'rtacha yo'lni tanladi. Xonaga kirib, cho'qina boshladi va biroz ta'zim qilgandek bo'ldi. Qo'li va boshining harakatlari imkon bergancha, u shu asnoda xonaga ko'z yugurtirdi. Ikki yigit — biri gimnazist, ehtimol jiyanlar — cho'qinib xonadan chiqib ketishayotgan edi. Bir kampir qimirlamay turardi; qoshlari g'alati ko'tarilgan bir xonim unga pichirlab nimadir derdi. Syurtukli, qat'iyatli va baquvvat diakon har qanday e'tirozni rad etadigan qiyofa bilan ovoz chiqarib nimadir o'qirdi. Ilgari dasturxon atrofida xizmat qiladigan yosh mujik Gerasim Pyotr Ivanovichning oldidan yengil qadamlar bilan o'tib, polga nimadir separdi. Buni ko'rib, Pyotr Ivanovich darhol chirib borayotgan jasadning xira hidini sezdi. Ivan Ilichning oldiga oxirgi kelganida Pyotr Ivanovich bu mujikni uning xonasida ko'rgan edi; u kasalga qarovchi vazifasini bajarardi va Ivan Ilich uni ayniqsa yaxshi ko'rardi. Pyotr Ivanovich tobut, diakon va burchakdagi stol ustidagi ikonalar o'rtasidagi bir yo'nalishga qarab cho'qinishda va ta'zim qilishda davom etdi. Keyin qo'li bilan cho'qinish harakati unga haddan tashqari cho'zilib ketgandek tuyulgach, to'xtadi va marhumga tikilib qaray boshladi.

paras.en: The dead man lay, as dead men always do lie, in a peculiarly heavy dead way, his stiffened limbs sunk in the cushions of the coffin, and his head bent back forever on the pillow, and thrust up, as dead men always do, his yellow waxen forehead with bald spots on the sunken temples, and his nose that stood out sharply and as it were squeezed on the upper lip. He was much changed, even thinner since Pyotr Ivanovitch had seen him, but his face⁠—as always with the dead⁠—was more handsome, and, above all, more impressive than it had been when he was alive. On the face was an expression of what had to be done having been done, and rightly done. Besides this, there was too in that expression a reproach or a reminder for the living. This reminder seemed to Pyotr Ivanovitch uncalled for, or, at least, to have nothing to do with him. He felt something unpleasant; and so Pyotr Ivanovitch once more crossed himself hurriedly, and, as it struck him, too hurriedly, not quite in accordance with the proprieties, turned and went to the door. Shvarts was waiting for him in the adjoining room, standing with his legs apart and both hands behind his back playing with his top hat. A single glance at the playful, sleek, and elegant figure of Shvarts revived Pyotr Ivanovitch. He felt that he, Shvarts, was above it, and would not give way to depressing impressions. The mere sight of him said plainly: the incident of the service over the body of Ivan Ilyitch cannot possibly constitute a sufficient ground for recognising the business of the session suspended⁠—in other words, in no way can it hinder us from shuffling and cutting a pack of cards this evening, while the footman sets four unsanctified candles on the table for us; in fact, there is no ground for supposing that this incident could prevent us from spending the evening agreeably. He said as much indeed to Pyotr Ivanovitch as he came out, proposing that the party should meet at Fyodor Vassilievitch’s. But apparently it was Pyotr Ivanovitch’s destiny not to play “screw” that evening. Praskovya Fyodorovna, a short, fat woman who, in spite of all efforts in a contrary direction, was steadily broader from her shoulders downwards, all in black, with lace on her head and her eyebrows as queerly arched as the lady standing beside the coffin, came out of her own apartments with some other ladies, and conducting them to the dead man’s room, said: “The service will take place immediately; come in.”
paras.uz: Marhum, marhumlar doim yotganidek, o'ziga xos og'ir, jonsiz tarzda yotardi: qotib qolgan a'zolari tobut yostiqlariga botgan, boshi yostiqqa abadiy egilgan, marhumlarnikidek, botiq chakkalarida taqir dog'lari bor sarg'ish mumdek peshonasi va go'yo ustki labga qisilib, keskin turtib chiqqan burni yuqoriga qaragan edi. Pyotr Ivanovich uni ko'rganidan beri u ancha o'zgargan, yana ham ozib ketgan edi, lekin yuzi — marhumlarda doim bo'lganidek — tirikligidagidan chiroyliroq va, eng muhimi, salobatliroq edi. Yuzida qilinishi kerak bo'lgan ish qilindi va to'g'ri qilindi, degan ifoda bor edi. Bundan tashqari, bu ifodada tiriklarga qaratilgan qandaydir ta'na yoki eslatma ham bor edi. Bu eslatma Pyotr Ivanovichga o'rinsiz yoki, hech bo'lmaganda, unga aloqasi yo'qdek tuyuldi. U qandaydir noxush narsani his qildi; shuning uchun Pyotr Ivanovich yana bir bor shoshib — o'ziga ham juda shoshib, odob qoidalariga uncha mos kelmaydigandek tuyulgan tarzda — cho'qindi-da, burilib eshik tomon yurdi. Shvarts uni qo'shni xonada kutib turardi: oyoqlarini kerib, ikki qo'lini orqasiga qilib, silindr shlyapasini o'ynab turardi. Shvartsning o'ynoqi, ozoda va nafis qomatiga bir qarashning o'zi Pyotr Ivanovichni jonlantirdi. U Shvarts bularning hammasidan yuqorida turishini, tushkun taassurotlarga berilmasligini his qildi. Uning ko'rinishining o'zi ochiq aytib turardi: Ivan Ilichning jasadi ustidagi marosim hodisasi majlis ishini to'xtatilgan deb tan olish uchun yetarli asos bo'la olmaydi — boshqacha aytganda, bu bizga bugun kechqurun, malay stolga to'rtta muqaddaslanmagan sham qo'yib turganida, bir dasta qartani aralashtirib, bo'lishimizga hech qanday xalal bera olmaydi; aslida, bu hodisa bizga kechani yoqimli o'tkazishimizga to'sqinlik qilishi mumkin, deb o'ylashga hech qanday asos yo'q. Haqiqatan ham, u Pyotr Ivanovich chiqqanida unga shunday dedi va o'yinchilar Fyodor Vasilyevichnikida yig'ilishni taklif qildi. Lekin, aftidan, Pyotr Ivanovichning taqdirida o'sha kecha «vint» o'ynash yo'q ekan. Praskovya Fyodorovna — past bo'yli, semiz, qarshi tomonga qilingan barcha urinishlarga qaramay yelkasidan pastga qarab tobora kengayib borayotgan, boshdan-oyoq qora kiygan, boshida to'r, qoshlari tobut yonida turgan xonimnikidek g'alati qayrilgan ayol — boshqa xonimlar bilan o'z xonalaridan chiqib, ularni marhumning xonasiga boshlab borarkan: «Marosim hozir boshlanadi; kiringlar», dedi.

paras.en: Shvarts, making an indefinite bow, stood still, obviously neither accepting nor declining this invitation. Praskovya Fyodorovna, recognising Pyotr Ivanovitch, sighed, went right up to him, took his hand, and said, “I know that you were a true friend of Ivan Ilyitch’s⁠ ⁠…” and looked at him, expecting from him the suitable action in response to these words. Pyotr Ivanovitch knew that, just as before he had to cross himself, now what he had to do was to press her hand, to sigh and to say, “Ah, I was indeed!” And he did so. And as he did so, he felt that the desired result had been attained; that he was touched, and she was touched.
paras.uz: Shvarts noaniq ta'zim qilib, to'xtab qoldi; u bu taklifni na qabul qilgani, na rad etgani aniq edi. Praskovya Fyodorovna Pyotr Ivanovichni tanib, xo'rsindi, uning oldiga yaqin kelib, qo'lini oldi-da: «Bilaman, siz Ivan Ilichning haqiqiy do'sti edingiz…» dedi va bu so'zlarga javoban undan munosib harakatni kutib, unga qaradi. Pyotr Ivanovich biladiki, avval cho'qinishi kerak bo'lganidek, endi uning qo'lini siqishi, xo'rsinishi va «Ha, albatta!» deyishi kerak edi. U shunday qildi ham. Va shunday qilarkan, kutilgan natijaga erishilganini — o'zi ham, u ham ta'sirlanganini his qildi.

paras.en: “Come, since it’s not begun yet, I have something I want to say to you,” said the widow. “Give me your arm.”
paras.uz: — Yuring, hali boshlanmadi, sizga aytmoqchi bo'lgan gapim bor, — dedi beva. — Qo'lingizni bering.

paras.en: Pyotr Ivanovitch gave her his arm, and they moved towards the inner rooms, passing Shvarts, who winked gloomily at Pyotr Ivanovitch.
paras.uz: Pyotr Ivanovich unga qo'lini berdi va ular ichkari xonalar tomon yurishdi; Shvartsning yonidan o'tishganda, u Pyotr Ivanovichga ma'yus ko'z qisib qo'ydi.

paras.en: “So much for our ‘screw’! Don’t complain if we find another partner. You can make a fifth when you do get away,” said his humorous glance.
paras.uz: «Mana sizga «vint»! Boshqa sherik topsak, xafa bo'lmang. Qutulganingizda beshinchi bo'lib qo'shilasiz», derdi uning hazilomuz nigohi.

paras.en: Pyotr Ivanovitch sighed still more deeply and despondently, and Praskovya Fyodorovna pressed his hand gratefully. Going into her drawing-room, that was upholstered with pink cretonne and lighted by a dismal-looking lamp, they sat down at the table, she on a sofa and Pyotr Ivanovitch on a low ottoman with deranged springs which yielded spasmodically under his weight. Praskovya Fyodorovna was about to warn him to sit on another seat, but felt such a recommendation out of keeping with her position, and changed her mind. Sitting down on the ottoman, Pyotr Ivanovitch remembered how Ivan Ilyitch had arranged this drawing-room, and had consulted him about this very pink cretonne with green leaves. Seating herself on the sofa, and pushing by the table (the whole drawing-room was crowded with furniture and things), the widow caught the lace of her black fichu in the carving of the table. Pyotr Ivanovitch got up to disentangle it for her; and the ottoman, freed from his weight, began bobbing up spasmodically under him. The widow began unhooking her lace herself, and Pyotr Ivanovitch again sat down, suppressing the mutinous ottoman springs under him. But the widow could not quite free herself, and Pyotr Ivanovitch rose again, and again the ottoman became mutinous and popped up with a positive snap. When this was all over, she took out a clean cambric handkerchief and began weeping. Ivanovitch had been chilled off by the incident with the lace and the struggle with the ottoman springs, and he sat looking sullen. This awkward position was cut short by the entrance of Sokolov, Ivan Ilyitch’s butler, who came in to announce that the place in the cemetery fixed on by Praskovya Fyodorovna would cost two hundred roubles. She left off weeping, and with the air of a victim glancing at Pyotr Ivanovitch, said in French that it was very terrible for her. Pyotr Ivanovitch made a silent gesture signifying his unhesitating conviction that it must indeed be so.
paras.uz: Pyotr Ivanovich yanada chuqurroq va mungliroq xo'rsindi, Praskovya Fyodorovna esa uning qo'lini minnatdorlik bilan siqdi. Pushti kreton bilan qoplangan va g'amgin chiroq bilan yoritilgan mehmonxonasiga kirib, ular stol yoniga o'tirishdi: u divanga, Pyotr Ivanovich esa prujinalari buzilib, og'irligi ostida titrab-tirishib egiladigan past puf ustiga. Praskovya Fyodorovna uni boshqa joyga o'tirishga ogohlantirmoqchi bo'ldi, lekin bunday maslahat o'z holatiga to'g'ri kelmasligini his qilib, fikridan qaytdi. Puf ustiga o'tirarkan, Pyotr Ivanovich Ivan Ilich bu mehmonxonani qanday jihozlaganini va aynan shu yashil barglar tushirilgan pushti kreton haqida u bilan maslahatlashganini esladi. Divanga o'tirib, stol yonidan o'tayotganda (butun mehmonxona mebel va buyumlarga to'la edi) beva qora ro'molining to'rini stolning o'ymakoriga ilintirib oldi. Pyotr Ivanovich uni bo'shatish uchun o'rnidan turdi; uning og'irligidan qutulgan puf esa ostida silkinib, sakray boshladi. Beva to'rini o'zi bo'shata boshladi, Pyotr Ivanovich esa ostidagi isyonkor prujinalarni bosib, yana o'tirdi. Lekin beva o'zini butunlay bo'shata olmadi, Pyotr Ivanovich yana turdi va puf yana isyon ko'tarib, hatto shiqillab sakrab chiqdi. Bularning hammasi tugagach, u toza batist ro'molcha chiqarib, yig'lay boshladi. To'r voqeasi va prujinalar bilan kurash Pyotr Ivanovichning hissiyotini sovutib qo'ygan edi, u qovog'ini solib o'tirardi. Bu noqulay vaziyatni Ivan Ilichning boshqaruvchisi Sokolov kirib kelib to'xtatdi: u Praskovya Fyodorovna tanlagan qabristondagi joy ikki yuz rubl turishini ma'lum qildi. U yig'lashdan to'xtadi va Pyotr Ivanovichga jabrdiyda qiyofasida qarab, fransuzcha bu uning uchun juda og'irligini aytdi. Pyotr Ivanovich indamay, bu shubhasiz shunday bo'lishi kerakligiga qat'iy ishonchini bildiruvchi ishora qildi.

paras.en: “Please, smoke,” she said in a magnanimous, and at the same time, crushed voice, and she began discussing with Sokolov the question of the price of the site for the grave.
paras.uz: — Iltimos, cheking, — dedi u olijanob va ayni paytda ezilgan ovozda va Sokolov bilan qabr joyining narxi masalasini muhokama qila boshladi.

paras.en: Pyotr Ivanovitch, lighting a cigarette, listened to her very circumstantial inquiries as to the various prices of sites and her decision as to the one to be selected. Having settled on the site for the grave, she made arrangements also about the choristers. Sokolov went away.
paras.uz: Pyotr Ivanovich papiros tutatib, uning turli joylarning narxlari haqidagi juda batafsil so'rovlarini va qaysi birini tanlash haqidagi qarorini tingladi. Qabr joyini hal qilgach, u xonandalar haqida ham buyruq berdi. Sokolov chiqib ketdi.

paras.en: “I see to everything myself,” she said to Pyotr Ivanovitch, moving on one side the albums that lay on the table; and noticing that the table was in danger from the cigarette-ash, she promptly passed an ashtray to Pyotr Ivanovitch, and said: “I consider it affectation to pretend that my grief prevents me from looking after practical matters. On the contrary, if anything could⁠—not console me⁠ ⁠… but distract me, it is seeing after everything for him.” She took out her handkerchief again, as though preparing to weep again; and suddenly, as though struggling with herself, she shook herself, and began speaking calmly: “But I’ve business to talk about with you.”
paras.uz: — Hammasini o'zim qilaman, — dedi u Pyotr Ivanovichga stol ustidagi albomlarni bir chetga surib; stolga papiros kuli tushish xavfini payqab, darhol Pyotr Ivanovichga kuldon uzatdi-da, dedi: — Qayg'um amaliy ishlar bilan shug'ullanishimga xalal beryapti, deb ko'rsatishni sun'iylik deb hisoblayman. Aksincha, agar biror narsa meni — taskin bermasa-da… chalg'ita olsa, bu uning uchun hamma narsani o'zim qilishdir. — U yana ro'molchasini oldi, go'yo yana yig'lashga hozirlanayotgandek; va birdan, o'zi bilan kurashayotgandek, silkinib oldi-da, xotirjam gapira boshladi: — Lekin siz bilan gaplashadigan ishim bor.

paras.en: Pyotr Ivanovitch bowed, carefully keeping in check the springs of the ottoman, which had at once begun quivering under him.
paras.uz: Pyotr Ivanovich ostida darhol titray boshlagan puf prujinalarini ehtiyotkorlik bilan bosib turib, ta'zim qildi.

paras.en: “The last few days his sufferings were awful.”
paras.uz: — Oxirgi kunlari uning azoblari dahshatli edi.

paras.en: “Did he suffer very much?” asked Pyotr Ivanovitch.
paras.uz: — Juda qiynaldimi? — so'radi Pyotr Ivanovich.

paras.en: “Oh, awfully! For the last moments, hours indeed, he never left off screaming. For three days and nights in succession he screamed incessantly. It was insufferable. I can’t understand how I bore it; one could hear it through three closed doors. Ah, what I suffered!”
paras.uz: — Oh, dahshatli! So'nggi daqiqalarda, aniqrog'i soatlarda, u qichqirishdan to'xtamadi. Uch kecha-kunduz uzluksiz qichqirdi. Chidab bo'lmas edi. Qanday chidaganimni tushunmayman; uchta yopiq eshik ortidan eshitilardi. Oh, men nimalarni boshdan kechirdim!

paras.en: “And was he really conscious?” asked Pyotr Ivanovitch.
paras.uz: — U rostdan ham hushida edimi? — so'radi Pyotr Ivanovich.

paras.en: “Yes,” she whispered, “up to the last minute. He said goodbye to us a quarter of an hour before his death, and asked Volodya to be taken away too.”
paras.uz: — Ha, — pichirladi u, — so'nggi daqiqagacha. O'limidan chorak soat oldin biz bilan xayrlashdi va Volodyani ham olib chiqib ketishni so'radi.

paras.en: The thought of the sufferings of a man he had known so intimately, at first as a lighthearted boy, a schoolboy, then grown up as a partner at whist, in spite of the unpleasant consciousness of his own and this woman’s hypocrisy, suddenly horrified Pyotr Ivanovitch. He saw again that forehead, the nose that seemed squeezing the lip, and he felt frightened for himself. “Three days and nights of awful suffering and death. Why, that may at once, any minute, come upon me too,” he thought, and he felt for an instant terrified. But immediately, he could not himself have said how, there came to his support the customary reflection that this had happened to Ivan Ilyitch and not to him, and that to him this must not and could not happen; that in thinking thus he was giving way to depression, which was not the right thing to do, as was evident from Shvarts’s expression of face. And making these reflections, Pyotr Ivanovitch felt reassured, and began with interest inquiring details about Ivan Ilyitch’s end, as though death were a mischance peculiar to Ivan Ilyitch, but not at all incidental to himself.
paras.uz: O'zining va bu ayolning ikkiyuzlamachiligini noxush anglashiga qaramay, avval beg'am bola, maktab o'quvchisi, keyin katta bo'lib vist o'yinidagi sherik sifatida shunchalik yaqindan tanigan odamning azoblari haqidagi o'y Pyotr Ivanovichni birdan dahshatga soldi. U yana o'sha peshonani, go'yo labni qisib turgan burunni ko'rdi va o'zi uchun qo'rqib ketdi. «Uch kecha-kunduz dahshatli azob va o'lim. Axir bu darhol, istalgan daqiqada mening boshimga ham tushishi mumkin», deb o'yladi u va bir lahza vahimaga tushdi. Lekin darhol, o'zi ham qanday qilib ekanini ayta olmasdi, unga odatiy mulohaza yordamga keldi: bu Ivan Ilichning boshiga tushdi, unikiga emas, va uning boshiga bu tushmasligi kerak va tusha olmaydi; bunday o'ylash bilan u tushkunlikka berilyapti, bu esa, Shvartsning yuz ifodasidan ko'rinib turganidek, to'g'ri ish emas. Shunday mulohaza qilib, Pyotr Ivanovich tinchlandi va Ivan Ilichning oxiri haqida tafsilotlarni qiziqish bilan so'ray boshladi, go'yo o'lim faqat Ivan Ilichga xos bo'lgan omadsizlik-u, o'ziga mutlaqo taalluqli emasdek.

paras.en: After various observations about the details of the truly awful physical sufferings endured by Ivan Ilyitch (these details Pyotr Ivanovitch learned only through the effect Ivan Ilyitch’s agonies had had on the nerves of Praskovya Fyodorovna), the widow apparently thought it time to get to business.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich chekkan haqiqatan dahshatli jismoniy azoblarning tafsilotlari haqida turli gaplardan keyin (bu tafsilotlarni Pyotr Ivanovich faqat Ivan Ilichning azoblari Praskovya Fyodorovnaning asablariga qanday ta'sir qilgani orqali bildi), beva, aftidan, ishga o'tish vaqti keldi, deb o'yladi.

paras.en: “Ah, Pyotr Ivanovitch, how hard it is, how awfully, awfully hard!” and she began to cry again.
paras.uz: — Oh, Pyotr Ivanovich, bu qanchalik og'ir, qanchalik dahshatli, dahshatli og'ir! — va u yana yig'lay boshladi.

paras.en: Pyotr Ivanovitch sighed, and waited for her to blow her nose. When she had done so, he said, “Indeed it is,” and again she began to talk, and brought out what was evidently the business she wished to discuss with him; that business consisted in the inquiry as to how on the occasion of her husband’s death she was to obtain a grant from the government. She made a show of asking Pyotr Ivanovitch’s advice about a pension. But he perceived that she knew already to the minutest details, what he did not know himself indeed, everything that could be got out of the government on the ground of this death; but that what she wanted to find out was, whether there were not any means of obtaining a little more? Pyotr Ivanovitch tried to imagine such means; but after pondering a little, and out of politeness abusing the government for its stinginess, he said that he believed that it was impossible to obtain more. Then she sighed and began unmistakably looking about for an excuse for getting rid of her visitor. He perceived this, put out his cigarette, got up, pressed her hand, and went out into the passage.
paras.uz: Pyotr Ivanovich xo'rsindi va uning burnini qoqishini kutdi. U buni qilib bo'lgach: «Haqiqatan ham», dedi va u yana gapira boshladi va, aftidan, u bilan muhokama qilmoqchi bo'lgan ishini o'rtaga tashladi; bu ish erining o'limi munosabati bilan davlatdan qanday qilib pul olish mumkinligini so'rashdan iborat edi. U pensiya haqida Pyotr Ivanovichdan maslahat so'rayotgandek ko'rinish qildi. Lekin u payqadiki, ayol bu o'lim asosida davlatdan olish mumkin bo'lgan hamma narsani — Pyotr Ivanovichning o'zi bilmagan narsalarni ham — eng mayda tafsilotlarigacha allaqachon biladi; u esa yana ozgina ko'proq olishning biror yo'li yo'qmikan, shuni bilmoqchi. Pyotr Ivanovich bunday yo'lni tasavvur qilishga urindi; lekin biroz o'ylab, odob yuzasidan davlatni xasisligi uchun so'kib, ko'proq olish imkonsiz, deb hisoblashini aytdi. Shunda u xo'rsindi va mehmonidan qutulish uchun bahona izlay boshlagani aniq sezildi. U buni payqadi, papirosini o'chirdi, o'rnidan turdi, uning qo'lini siqdi va dahlizga chiqdi.

paras.en: In the dining-room, where was the bric-a-brac clock that Ivan Ilyitch had been so delighted at buying, Pyotr Ivanovitch met the priest and several people he knew who had come to the service for the dead, and saw too Ivan Ilyitch’s daughter, a handsome young lady. She was all in black. Her very slender figure looked even slenderer than usual. She had a gloomy, determined, almost wrathful expression. She bowed to Pyotr Ivanovitch as though he were to blame in some way. Behind the daughter, with the same offended air on his face, stood a rich young man, whom Pyotr Ivanovitch knew too, an examining magistrate, the young lady’s fiancé, as he had heard. He bowed dejectedly to him, and would have gone on into the dead man’s room, when from the staircase there appeared the figure of the son, the high school boy, extraordinarily like Ivan Ilyitch. He was the little Ivan Ilyitch over again as Pyotr Ivanovitch remembered him at school. His eyes were red with crying, and had that look often seen in unclean boys of thirteen or fourteen. The boy, seeing Pyotr Ivanovitch, scowled morosely and bashfully. Pyotr Ivanovitch nodded to him and went into the dead man’s room. The service for the dead began⁠—candles, groans, incense, tears, sobs. Pyotr Ivanovitch stood frowning, staring at his feet in front of him. He did not once glance at the dead man, and right through to the end did not once give way to depressing influences, and was one of the first to walk out. In the hall there was no one. Gerasim, the young peasant, darted out of the dead man’s room, tossed over with his strong hand all the fur cloaks to find Pyotr Ivanovitch’s, and gave it him.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich sotib olganidan juda xursand bo'lgan antiqa soat turgan ovqat xonasida Pyotr Ivanovich ruhoniyni va marosimga kelgan bir necha tanishini uchratdi, shuningdek Ivan Ilichning qizini — chiroyli yosh qizni ko'rdi. U boshdan-oyoq qora kiygan edi. Juda xipcha qomati odatdagidan ham xipcharoq ko'rinardi. Uning yuzida g'amgin, qat'iy, deyarli g'azabnok ifoda bor edi. U Pyotr Ivanovichga go'yo u qandaydir aybdordek ta'zim qildi. Qizning orqasida, yuzida xuddi shunday xafa ifoda bilan, Pyotr Ivanovich taniydigan boy yigit — tergovchi, eshitishicha, qizning kuyovi turardi. U unga ma'yus ta'zim qildi va marhumning xonasiga o'tmoqchi edi, shu payt zinadan Ivan Ilichga g'ayrioddiy o'xshaydigan o'g'li — gimnazist ko'rindi. Bu Pyotr Ivanovich maktabdan eslagan kichkina Ivan Ilichning aynan o'zi edi. Uning ko'zlari yig'idan qizargan va o'n uch-o'n to'rt yoshli nopok o'g'il bolalarda ko'p uchraydigan qarash bor edi. Bola Pyotr Ivanovichni ko'rib, qovog'ini uyib, uyalib qaradi. Pyotr Ivanovich unga bosh irg'adi va marhumning xonasiga kirdi. Janoza marosimi boshlandi — shamlar, ingrashlar, isiriq, ko'z yoshlar, ho'ngrashlar. Pyotr Ivanovich qovog'ini solib, oyog'i ostiga tikilib turdi. U marhumga bir marta ham qaramadi, oxirigacha bir marta ham tushkun ta'sirlarga berilmadi va birinchilardan bo'lib chiqib ketdi. Dahlizda hech kim yo'q edi. Yosh mujik Gerasim marhumning xonasidan otilib chiqdi, Pyotr Ivanovichning po'stinini topish uchun kuchli qo'li bilan barcha po'stinlarni ag'dar-to'ntar qildi va uni unga berdi.

paras.en: “Well, Gerasim, my boy?” said Pyotr Ivanovitch, so as to say something. “A sad business, isn’t it?”
paras.uz: — Xo'sh, Gerasim, birodar? — dedi Pyotr Ivanovich biror narsa deyish uchun. — Achinarli ish, a?

paras.en: “It’s God’s will. We shall come to the same,” said Gerasim, showing his white, even, peasant teeth in a smile, and, like a man in a rush of extra work, he briskly opened the door, called up the coachman, saw Pyotr Ivanovitch into the carriage, and darted back to the steps as though bethinking himself of what he had to do next.
paras.uz: — Xudoning irodasi. Hammamiz o'sha yerga boramiz, — dedi Gerasim oppoq, tekis mujik tishlarini ko'rsatib jilmayarkan va ishi ko'payib ketgan odamdek chaqqonlik bilan eshikni ochdi, aravakashni chaqirdi, Pyotr Ivanovichni aravaga o'tqazdi va go'yo endi nima qilishi kerakligini eslagandek, zinaga qaytib yugurdi.

paras.en: Pyotr Ivanovitch had a special pleasure in the fresh air after the smell of incense, of the corpse, and of carbolic acid.
paras.uz: Isiriq, jasad va karbol kislota hididan keyin toza havo Pyotr Ivanovichga alohida rohat bag'ishladi.

paras.en: “Where to?” asked the coachman.
paras.uz: — Qayerga? — so'radi aravakash.

paras.en: “It’s not too late. I’ll still go round to Fyodor Vassilievitch’s.”
paras.uz: — Hali kech emas. Fyodor Vasilyevichnikiga ham kirib o'taman.

paras.en: And Pyotr Ivanovitch drove there. And he did, in fact, find them just finishing the first rubber, so that he came just at the right time to take a hand.
paras.uz: Va Pyotr Ivanovich o'sha yoqqa jo'nadi. Va haqiqatan ham ularni birinchi robberni endigina tugatayotgan paytda topdi, shuning uchun u o'yinga qo'shilish uchun aynan o'z vaqtida yetib keldi.

chapters.recap_uz: Sudda hamkasblar Ivan Ilichning o'limini eshitib, avvalo o'z lavozimlari haqida o'ylashadi. Faqat mujik Gerasim o'limni oddiy haqiqat deb qabul qiladi. Pyotr Ivanovich kechqurun «vint» o'yiniga ulguradi.

chapters.title: II. The most ordinary life

paras.en: The previous history of Ivan Ilyitch was the simplest, the most ordinary, and the most awful.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilichning o'tmish tarixi eng oddiy, eng odatiy va eng dahshatli edi.

paras.en: Ivan Ilyitch died at the age of forty-five, a member of the Judicial Council. He was the son of an official, whose career in Petersburg through various ministries and departments had been such as leads people into that position in which, though it is distinctly obvious that they are unfit to perform any kind of real duty, they yet cannot, owing to their long past service and their official rank, be dismissed; and they therefore receive a specially created fictitious post, and by no means fictitious thousands⁠—from six to ten⁠—on which they go on living till extreme old age. Such was the privy councillor, the superfluous member of various superfluous institutions, Ilya Efimovitch Golovin.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich qirq besh yoshida, Sud palatasi a'zosi bo'lib vafot etdi. U Peterburgda turli vazirlik va departamentlarda xizmat qilib, odamlarni shunday holatga olib keladigan martaba qilgan amaldorning o'g'li edi: ular hech qanday haqiqiy vazifani bajarishga yaroqsiz ekanlari aniq ko'rinib tursa ham, uzoq yillik xizmatlari va unvonlari tufayli ularni ishdan bo'shatib bo'lmaydi; shuning uchun ular maxsus o'ylab topilgan soxta lavozimni va hech ham soxta bo'lmagan minglarni — oltidan o'n minggacha — oladilar va shu pul bilan juda keksayguncha yashayveradilar. Turli keraksiz muassasalarning keraksiz a'zosi, maxfiy maslahatchi Ilya Yefimovich Golovin ana shunday odam edi.

paras.en: He had three sons. Ivan Ilyitch was the second son. The eldest son’s career was exactly like his father’s, only in a different department, and he was by now close upon that stage in the service in which the same sinecure would be reached. The third son was the unsuccessful one. He had in various positions always made a mess of things, and was now employed in the railway department. And his father and his brothers, and still more their wives, did not merely dislike meeting him, but avoided, except in extreme necessity, recollecting his existence. His sister had married Baron Greff, a Petersburg official of the same stamp as his father-in-law. Ivan Ilyitch was le phénix de la famille, as people said. He was not so frigid and precise as the eldest son, nor so wild as the youngest. He was the happy mean between them⁠—a shrewd, lively, pleasant, and well-bred man. He had been educated with his younger brother at the school of jurisprudence. The younger brother had not finished the school course, but was expelled when in the fifth class. Ivan Ilyitch completed the course successfully. At school he was just the same as he was later on all his life⁠—an intelligent fellow, highly good-humoured and sociable, but strict in doing what he considered to be his duty. His duty he considered whatever was so considered by those persons who were set in authority over him. He was not a toady as a boy, nor later on as a grown-up person; but from his earliest years he was attracted, as a fly to the light, to persons of good standing in the world, assimilated their manners and their views of life, and established friendly relations with them. All the enthusiasms of childhood and youth passed, leaving no great traces in him; he gave way to sensuality and to vanity, and latterly when in the higher classes at school to liberalism, but always keeping within certain limits which were unfailingly marked out for him by his instincts.
paras.uz: Uning uch o'g'li bor edi. Ivan Ilich ikkinchi o'g'il edi. To'ng'ich o'g'ilning martabasi xuddi otasinikiga o'xshardi, faqat boshqa departamentda, va u allaqachon xizmatda o'sha mashaqqatsiz lavozimga yetiladigan bosqichga yaqinlashib qolgan edi. Uchinchi o'g'il omadsiz chiqdi. U turli joylarda doim ishni barbod qilgan va endi temir yo'l idorasida xizmat qilardi. Otasi va akalari, ularning xotinlari esa undan ham ko'proq, u bilan uchrashishni yoqtirmabgina qolmay, juda zarur bo'lmasa, uning mavjudligini eslashdan ham qochishardi. Singlisi otasi bilan bir xil toifadagi peterburglik amaldor baron Greffga turmushga chiqqan edi. Odamlar aytganidek, Ivan Ilich le phénix de la famille — «oilaning faxri» edi. U to'ng'ich o'g'ildek sovuq va rasmiyatchi ham, kenja o'g'ildek telba ham emas edi. U ularning o'rtasidagi baxtli o'rta yo'l edi — ziyrak, jonli, yoqimli va odobli odam. U ukasi bilan birga huquqshunoslik maktabida o'qigan edi. Ukasi maktabni tugatmadi, beshinchi sinfda haydaldi. Ivan Ilich kursni muvaffaqiyatli tugatdi. Maktabda u keyinchalik butun umri davomida qanday bo'lsa, xuddi shunday edi — aqlli, juda xushchaqchaq va kirishimli, lekin o'z burchi deb hisoblagan narsani bajarishda qattiqqo'l. U o'zidan yuqori turgan hokimiyat egalari burch deb hisoblagan narsani burch deb bilardi. U na bolaligida, na keyin katta bo'lganida laganbardor bo'lmadi; lekin eng yosh yillaridan boshlab, chivin yorug'likka intilgandek, dunyoda yuqori mavqega ega odamlarga intilar, ularning odob-axloqi va hayotga qarashlarini o'zlashtirar va ular bilan do'stona munosabat o'rnatardi. Bolalik va yoshlikning barcha havaslari unda katta iz qoldirmay o'tib ketdi; u nafsga va shuhratparastlikka, maktabning yuqori sinflarida esa liberalizmga berildi, lekin doim instinktlari unga aniq belgilab bergan muayyan chegaralar ichida qoldi.

paras.en: At school he had committed actions which had struck him beforehand as great vileness, and gave him a feeling of loathing for himself at the very time he was committing them. But later on, perceiving that such actions were committed also by men of good position, and were not regarded by them as base, he was able, not to regard them as good, but to forget about them completely, and was never mortified by recollections of them.
paras.uz: Maktabda u avvaldan o'ziga katta pastkashlik bo'lib tuyulgan va aynan ularni qilayotgan paytda o'zidan jirkanish hissini uyg'otgan ishlarni qilgan edi. Lekin keyinchalik bunday ishlarni yuqori mavqedagi odamlar ham qilishini va ular buni pastkashlik deb hisoblamasligini ko'rib, u ularni yaxshi deb hisoblamasa-da, butunlay unuta oldi va ularni eslab hech qachon iztirob chekmadi.

paras.en: Leaving the school of jurisprudence in the tenth class, and receiving from his father a sum of money for his outfit, Ivan Ilyitch ordered his clothes at Sharmer’s, hung on his watch-chain a medallion inscribed “respice finem,” said goodbye to the prince who was the principal of his school, had a farewell dinner with his comrades at Donon’s, and with all his new fashionable belongings⁠—travelling trunk, linen, suits of clothes, shaving and toilet appurtenances, and travelling rug, all ordered and purchased at the very best shops⁠—set off to take the post of secretary on special commissions for the governor of a province, a post which had been obtained for him by his father.
paras.uz: Huquqshunoslik maktabini o'ninchi darajali unvon bilan tugatib, otasidan kiyim-kechak uchun pul olgach, Ivan Ilich kiyimlarini Sharmerga buyurtma qildi, soat zanjiriga «respice finem» («oxirini o'yla») deb yozilgan medalyon osdi, maktab rahbari bo'lgan knyaz bilan xayrlashdi, o'rtoqlari bilan Donon restoranida vidolashuv tushligini qildi va barcha yangi, zamonaviy narsalari — eng yaxshi do'konlardan buyurtma qilingan va sotib olingan safar sandig'i, ichki kiyimlari, kostyumlari, soqol olish va yuvinish anjomlari va yo'l pledi bilan — otasi olib bergan lavozimga, gubernator huzuridagi maxsus topshiriqlar bo'yicha kotib lavozimiga jo'nadi.

paras.en: In the province Ivan Ilyitch without loss of time made himself a position as easy and agreeable as his position had been in the school of jurisprudence. He did his work, made his career, and at the same time led a life of well-bred social gaiety. Occasionally he visited various districts on official duty, behaved with dignity both with his superiors and his inferiors; and with exactitude and an incorruptible honesty of which he could not help feeling proud, performed the duties with which he was entrusted, principally having to do with the dissenters. When engaged in official work he was, in spite of his youth and taste for frivolous amusements, exceedingly reserved, official, and even severe. But in social life he was often amusing and witty, and always good-natured, well bred, and bon enfant, as was said of him by his chief and his chief’s wife, with whom he was like one of the family.
paras.uz: Gubernada Ivan Ilich vaqtni boy bermay o'ziga huquqshunoslik maktabidagidek yengil va yoqimli mavqe yaratdi. U ishini qildi, martaba qildi va ayni paytda odobli, shod-xurram ijtimoiy hayot kechirdi. Vaqti-vaqti bilan xizmat yuzasidan turli uyezdlarga borardi, boshliqlari bilan ham, qo'l ostidagilar bilan ham o'zini salobatli tutardi; va o'ziga ishonib topshirilgan, asosan raskolniklar (eski diniy marosim tarafdorlari) bilan bog'liq vazifalarni aniqlik va beg'araz halollik bilan bajarardi va bundan beixtiyor faxrlanardi. Xizmat ishlari bilan band bo'lganida, yoshligi va yengil-yelpi o'yin-kulgiga moyilligiga qaramay, u nihoyatda vazmin, rasmiy va hatto qattiqqo'l edi. Lekin jamiyatda u ko'pincha quvnoq va hazilkash, doim xushfe'l, odobli va bon enfant — «yaxshi bola» edi; boshlig'i va boshlig'ining xotini u haqida shunday deyishardi, u ular bilan oiladan biridek edi.

paras.en: In the province there was, too, a connection with one of the ladies who obtruded their charms on the stylish young lawyer. There was a dressmaker, too, and there were drinking bouts with smart officers visiting the neighbourhood, and visits to a certain outlying street after supper; there was a rather cringing obsequiousness in his behaviour, too, with his chief, and even his chief’s wife. But all this was accompanied with such a tone of the highest breeding, that it could not be called by harsh names; it all came under the rubric of the French saying, Il faut que la jeunesse se passe. Everything was done with clean hands, in clean shirts, with French phrases, and, what was of most importance, in the highest society, and consequently with the approval of people of rank.
paras.uz: Gubernada, shuningdek, zamonaviy yosh huquqshunosga o'z jozibasini taqib olgan xonimlardan biri bilan munosabat ham bo'ldi. Bir tikuvchi qiz ham bor edi, atrofga kelgan olifta ofitserlar bilan ichkilikbozliklar ham, kechki ovqatdan keyin shahar chetidagi bir ko'chaga borishlar ham bo'ldi; boshlig'i va hatto boshlig'ining xotiniga nisbatan muomalasida biroz xushomadgo'ylik ham bor edi. Lekin bularning barchasi shunday yuksak odob ohangi bilan birga kechardiki, ularni qo'pol nomlar bilan atab bo'lmasdi; hammasi fransuzcha «Il faut que la jeunesse se passe» — «Yoshlik o'z yo'lini o'tishi kerak» degan maqol ostiga tushardi. Hammasi toza qo'llar bilan, toza ko'ylaklarda, fransuzcha iboralar bilan va, eng muhimi, eng yuqori doiralarda, demakki, mansabdor odamlarning ma'qullashi bilan qilinardi.

paras.en: Such was Ivan Ilyitch’s career for five years, and then came a change in his official life. New methods of judicial procedure were established; new men were wanted to carry them out. And Ivan Ilyitch became such a new man. Ivan Ilyitch was offered the post of examining magistrate, and he accepted it in spite of the fact that this post was in another province, and he would have to break off all the ties he had formed and form new ones. Ivan Ilyitch’s friends met together to see him off, had their photographs taken in a group, presented him with a silver cigarette-case, and he set off to his new post.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilichning besh yillik martabasi shunday bo'ldi, keyin xizmat hayotida o'zgarish yuz berdi. Sud ishlarini yuritishning yangi tartiblari joriy etildi; ularni amalga oshirish uchun yangi odamlar kerak edi. Va Ivan Ilich ana shunday yangi odamga aylandi. Ivan Ilichga tergovchi lavozimi taklif qilindi va bu lavozim boshqa gubernada bo'lgani va u o'rnatgan barcha aloqalarini uzib, yangilarini o'rnatishi kerak bo'lishiga qaramay, u uni qabul qildi. Ivan Ilichning do'stlari uni kuzatish uchun yig'ilishdi, birgalikda suratga tushishdi, unga kumush portsigar sovg'a qilishdi va u yangi lavozimiga jo'nadi.

paras.en: As an examining magistrate, Ivan Ilyitch was as comme il faut, as well bred, as adroit in keeping official duties apart from private life, and as successful in gaining universal respect, as he had been as secretary of private commissions. The duties of his new office were in themselves of far greater interest and attractiveness for Ivan Ilyitch. In his former post it had been pleasant to pass in his smart uniform from Sharmer’s through the crowd of petitioners and officials waiting timorously and envying him, and to march with his easy swagger straight into the governor’s private room, there to sit down with him to tea and cigarettes. But the persons directly subject to his authority were few. The only such persons were the district police superintendents and the dissenters, when he was serving on special commissions. And he liked treating such persons affably, almost like comrades; liked to make them feel that he, able to annihilate them, was behaving in this simple, friendly way with them. But such people were then few in number. Now as an examining magistrate Ivan Ilyitch felt that everyone⁠—everyone without exception⁠—the most dignified, the most self-satisfied people, all were in his hands, and that he had but to write certain words on a sheet of paper with a printed heading, and this dignified self-satisfied person would be brought before him in the capacity of a defendant or a witness; and if he did not care to make him sit down, he would have to stand up before him and answer his questions. Ivan Ilyitch never abused this authority of his; on the contrary, he tried to soften the expression of it. But the consciousness of this power and the possibility of softening its effect constituted for him the chief interest and attractiveness of his new position. In the work itself, in the preliminary inquiries, that is, Ivan Ilyitch very rapidly acquired the art of setting aside every consideration irrelevant to the official aspect of the case, and of reducing every case, however complex, to that form in which it could in a purely external fashion be put on paper, completely excluding his personal view of the matter, and what was of paramount importance, observing all the necessary formalities. All this work was new. And he was one of the first men who put into practical working the reforms in judicial procedure enacted in 1864.
paras.uz: Tergovchi sifatida Ivan Ilich maxsus topshiriqlar kotibi bo'lganidagidek comme il faut — «qanday bo'lishi kerak bo'lsa, shunday», xuddi shunday odobli, xizmat vazifalarini shaxsiy hayotdan ajrata bilishda xuddi shunday mohir va umumiy hurmatni qozonishda xuddi shunday muvaffaqiyatli edi. Yangi lavozimning vazifalari o'z-o'zidan Ivan Ilich uchun ancha qiziqarli va jozibali edi. Oldingi lavozimida Sharmerdan tikilgan olifta mundirda qo'rqib kutib turgan va unga havas qilayotgan arzchilar va amaldorlar olomoni orasidan o'tib, yengil bir viqor bilan to'g'ri gubernatorning shaxsiy xonasiga kirib, u bilan choy va papiros ustida o'tirish yoqimli edi. Lekin bevosita uning hokimiyatiga bo'ysunadigan odamlar kam edi. Maxsus topshiriqlarda xizmat qilganida bunday odamlar faqat uyezd politsiya boshliqlari va raskolniklar edi. U bunday odamlarga xushmuomala, deyarli o'rtoqlarcha munosabatda bo'lishni yoqtirardi; ularni yanchib tashlay oladigan odam ular bilan shunday oddiy, do'stona muomala qilayotganini his ettirishni yoqtirardi. Lekin bunday odamlar o'shanda kam edi. Endi tergovchi sifatida Ivan Ilich har kim — hech istisnosiz har kim — eng obro'li, eng o'zidan mamnun odamlar ham, hammasi uning qo'lida ekanini his qilardi: u faqat bosma sarlavhali qog'ozga muayyan so'zlarni yozsa bas, bu obro'li, o'zidan mamnun odam uning oldiga ayblanuvchi yoki guvoh sifatida keltiriladi; agar u uni o'tqazishni istamasa, u uning oldida tik turib, savollariga javob berishiga to'g'ri keladi. Ivan Ilich bu hokimiyatini hech qachon suiiste'mol qilmadi; aksincha, uning ko'rinishini yumshatishga harakat qildi. Lekin bu hokimiyatni anglash va uning ta'sirini yumshatish imkoniyati u uchun yangi lavozimining asosiy qiziqishi va jozibasini tashkil etardi. Ishning o'zida, ya'ni dastlabki tergovda Ivan Ilich ishning rasmiy tomoniga aloqasi bo'lmagan har qanday mulohazani chetga surib qo'yish va har qanday, eng murakkab ishni ham faqat tashqi tomondan qog'ozga tushirish mumkin bo'lgan shaklga keltirish san'atini juda tez egalladi, bunda o'zining shaxsiy qarashini butunlay chiqarib tashlar va, eng muhimi, barcha zarur rasmiyatchiliklarga rioya qilardi. Bu ishlarning hammasi yangi edi. Va u 1864-yilda qabul qilingan sud islohotlarini amalda qo'llagan birinchi odamlardan biri edi.

paras.en: On settling in a new town in his position as examining magistrate, Ivan Ilyitch made new acquaintances, formed new ties, took up a new line, and adopted a rather different attitude. He took up an attitude of somewhat dignified aloofness towards the provincial authorities, while he picked out the best circle among the legal gentlemen and wealthy gentry living in the town, and adopted a tone of slight dissatisfaction with the government, moderate liberalism, and lofty civic virtue. With this, while making no change in the elegance of his getup, Ivan Ilyitch in his new office gave up shaving, and left his beard free to grow as it liked. Ivan Ilyitch’s existence in the new town proved to be very agreeable; the society which took the line of opposition to the governor was friendly and good; his income was larger, and he found a source of increased enjoyment in whist, at which he began to play at this time; and having a faculty for playing cards good-humouredly, and being rapid and exact in his calculations, he was as a rule on the winning side.
paras.uz: Tergovchi sifatida yangi shaharga joylashgach, Ivan Ilich yangi tanishlar orttirdi, yangi aloqalar o'rnatdi, yangi yo'l tutdi va biroz boshqacha munosabatni tanladi. U guberna hokimiyatiga nisbatan biroz salobatli uzoqlikni saqladi, shaharda yashovchi sud xodimlari va badavlat dvoryanlar orasidan eng yaxshi doirani tanladi va hukumatdan biroz norozilik, mo'tadil liberalizm va yuksak fuqarolik fazilati ohangini oldi. Shu bilan birga, kiyinishidagi nafislikni o'zgartirmagan holda, Ivan Ilich yangi lavozimida soqol olishni tashladi va soqolini erkin o'stirib qo'ydi. Ivan Ilichning yangi shahardagi hayoti juda yoqimli bo'lib chiqdi; gubernatorga muxolif bo'lgan jamiyat do'stona va yaxshi edi; maoshi kattaroq edi va u shu paytda o'ynay boshlagan vistda qo'shimcha zavq manbaini topdi; qarta o'yinini xushfe'llik bilan o'ynash qobiliyati borligi va hisoblarida tez va aniq bo'lgani uchun u odatda yutardi.

paras.en: After living two years in the new town, Ivan Ilyitch met his future wife. Praskovya Fyodorovna Mihel was the most attractive, clever, and brilliant girl in the set in which Ivan Ilyitch moved. Among other amusements and recreations after his labours as a magistrate, Ivan Ilyitch started a light, playful flirtation with Praskovya Fyodorovna.
paras.uz: Yangi shaharda ikki yil yashagach, Ivan Ilich bo'lajak xotini bilan tanishdi. Praskovya Fyodorovna Mixel Ivan Ilich aylanib yurgan doiradagi eng jozibali, aqlli va porloq qiz edi. Tergovchilik mehnatidan keyingi boshqa ermak va hordiqlar qatorida Ivan Ilich Praskovya Fyodorovna bilan yengil, o'ynoqi noz-karashma boshladi.

paras.en: Ivan Ilyitch when he was an assistant secretary had danced as a rule; as an examining magistrate he danced only as an exception. He danced now as it were under protest, as though to show “that though I am serving on the new reformed legal code, and am of the fifth class in official rank, still if it comes to a question of dancing, in that line too I can do better than others.” In this spirit he danced now and then towards the end of the evening with Praskovya Fyodorovna, and it was principally during these dances that he won the heart of Praskovya Fyodorovna. She fell in love with him. Ivan Ilyitch had no clearly defined intention of marrying; but when the girl fell in love with him, he put the question to himself: “After all, why not get married?” he said to himself.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich yordamchi kotib bo'lganida odatda raqsga tushardi; tergovchi sifatida esa faqat istisno tariqasida raqsga tushardi. Endi u go'yo norozilik bilan raqsga tushardi, go'yo: «Garchi men yangi, isloh qilingan qonunlar asosida xizmat qilsam va beshinchi darajali unvonga ega bo'lsam ham, gap raqsga kelsa, bu sohada ham boshqalardan yaxshiroq qila olaman», demoqchidek. Shu ruhda u kechaning oxirlarida vaqti-vaqti bilan Praskovya Fyodorovna bilan raqsga tushardi va asosan shu raqslar paytida Praskovya Fyodorovnaning qalbini zabt etdi. U uni sevib qoldi. Ivan Ilichda uylanish haqida aniq niyat yo'q edi; lekin qiz uni sevib qolganida, u o'ziga savol berdi: «Aslida, nega uylanmasligim kerak?» dedi u o'ziga.

paras.en: The young lady, Praskovya Fyodorovna, was of good family, nice-looking. There was a little bit of property. Ivan Ilyitch might have reckoned on a more brilliant match, but this was a good match. Ivan Ilyitch had his salary; she, he hoped, would have as much of her own. It was a good family; she was a sweet, pretty, and perfectly comme il faut young woman. To say that Ivan Ilyitch got married because he fell in love with his wife and found in her sympathy with his views of life, would be as untrue as to say that he got married because the people of his world approved of the match. Ivan Ilyitch was influenced by both considerations; he was doing what was agreeable to himself in securing such a wife, and at the same time doing what persons of higher standing looked upon as the correct thing.
paras.uz: Yosh qiz Praskovya Fyodorovna yaxshi oiladan, ko'rinishi yoqimli edi. Ozgina mulki ham bor edi. Ivan Ilich yanada porloqroq juftlikka umid qilishi mumkin edi, lekin bu ham yaxshi juftlik edi. Ivan Ilichning maoshi bor edi; uning ham, u umid qilganidek, o'shancha o'z puli bo'lardi. Oila yaxshi edi; qiz shirin, chiroyli va mutlaqo comme il faut yosh ayol edi. Ivan Ilich xotinini sevib qolgani va unda hayotga qarashlariga hamfikrlik topgani uchun uylandi, deyish, uning doirasidagi odamlar bu juftlikni ma'qullagani uchun uylandi, deyish kabi noto'g'ri bo'lardi. Ivan Ilichga ikkala mulohaza ham ta'sir qildi: bunday xotinga ega bo'lish bilan u o'ziga yoqadigan ishni qilardi va ayni paytda yuqori mavqedagi odamlar to'g'ri deb hisoblagan ishni qilardi.

paras.en: And Ivan Ilyitch got married.
paras.uz: Va Ivan Ilich uylandi.

paras.en: The process itself of getting married and the early period of married life, with the conjugal caresses, the new furniture, the new crockery, the new house linen, all up to the time of his wife’s pregnancy, went off very well; so that Ivan Ilyitch had already begun to think that so far from marriage breaking up that kind of frivolous, agreeable, lighthearted life, always decorous and always approved by society, which he regarded as the normal life, it would even increase its agreeableness. But at that point, in the early months of his wife’s pregnancy, there came in a new element, unexpected, unpleasant, tiresome and unseemly, which could never have been anticipated, and from which there was no escape.
paras.uz: Uylanish jarayonining o'zi va oilaviy hayotning dastlabki davri — er-xotin erkalashlari, yangi mebel, yangi idish-tovoq, yangi choyshablar bilan — xotinining homiladorligigacha juda yaxshi o'tdi; shuning uchun Ivan Ilich allaqachon nikoh o'zi normal hayot deb bilgan, doim odobli va jamiyat doim ma'qullaydigan yengil-yelpi, yoqimli, beg'am hayotni buzish u yoqda tursin, hatto uning yoqimliligini oshiradi, deb o'ylay boshlagan edi. Lekin shu paytda, xotinining homiladorligining dastlabki oylarida, hech qachon oldindan ko'rib bo'lmaydigan va undan qochib qutulib bo'lmaydigan yangi bir narsa — kutilmagan, noxush, zerikarli va nomaqbul narsa paydo bo'ldi.

paras.en: His wife, without any kind of reason, it seemed to Ivan Ilyitch, de gaité de cœur as he expressed it, began to disturb the agreeableness and decorum of their life. She began without any sort of justification to be jealous, exacting in her demands on his attention, squabbled over everything, and treated him to the coarsest and most unpleasant scenes.
paras.uz: Xotini, Ivan Ilichga tuyulishicha, hech qanday sababsiz, o'zi aytganidek, de gaité de cœur — «shunchaki ermak uchun», ularning hayotining yoqimliligi va odobini buza boshladi. U hech qanday asossiz rashk qila boshladi, unga e'tibor berishni talab qildi, har narsa uchun janjal qildi va unga eng qo'pol va eng noxush sahnalarni ko'rsatdi.

paras.en: At first Ivan Ilyitch hoped to escape from the unpleasantness of this position by taking up the same frivolous and well-bred line that had served him well on other occasions of difficulty. He endeavoured to ignore his wife’s ill-humour, went on living lightheartedly and agreeably as before, invited friends to play cards, tried to get away himself to the club or to his friends. But his wife began on one occasion with such energy, abusing him in such coarse language, and so obstinately persisted in her abuse of him every time he failed in carrying out her demands, obviously having made up her mind firmly to persist till he gave way, that is, stayed at home and was as dull as she was, that Ivan Ilyitch took alarm. He perceived that matrimony, at least with his wife, was not invariably conducive to the pleasures and proprieties of life; but, on the contrary, often destructive of them, and that it was therefore essential to erect some barrier to protect himself from these disturbances. And Ivan Ilyitch began to look about for such means of protecting himself. His official duties were the only thing that impressed Praskovya Fyodorovna, and Ivan Ilyitch began to use his official position, and the duties arising from it in his struggle with his wife to fence off his own independent world apart.
paras.uz: Avvaliga Ivan Ilich bu holatning noxushligidan boshqa qiyin paytlarda unga yaxshi xizmat qilgan o'sha yengil-yelpi va odobli yo'lni tutib qutulishga umid qildi. U xotinining kayfiyatsizligiga e'tibor bermaslikka urindi, avvalgidek beg'am va yoqimli yashashda davom etdi, qarta o'ynash uchun do'stlarini taklif qildi, o'zi klubga yoki do'stlarinikiga ketishga harakat qildi. Lekin xotini bir safar shunday g'ayrat bilan boshladi, uni shunday qo'pol so'zlar bilan so'kdi va u har safar uning talablarini bajarmaganida shunday qaysarlik bilan so'kishda davom etdi — u bo'yin egmaguncha, ya'ni uyda qolib, o'zidek zerikmaguncha turib olishga qat'iy qaror qilgani aniq edi — Ivan Ilich xavotirga tushdi. U nikoh, hech bo'lmaganda o'z xotini bilan nikoh, har doim ham hayot lazzatlari va odobiga xizmat qilavermasligini; aksincha, ko'pincha ularni buzishini va shuning uchun bu bezovtaliklardan o'zini himoya qilish uchun qandaydir to'siq qurish zarurligini angladi. Va Ivan Ilich o'zini himoya qilishning shunday vositalarini izlay boshladi. Uning xizmat vazifalari Praskovya Fyodorovnaga ta'sir qiladigan yagona narsa edi va Ivan Ilich xotini bilan kurashda o'zining mustaqil dunyosini to'siq bilan ajratib olish uchun xizmat mavqeidan va undan kelib chiqadigan vazifalardan foydalana boshladi.

paras.en: With the birth of the baby, the attempts at nursing it, and the various unsuccessful experiments with foods, with the illnesses, real and imaginary, of the infant and its mother, in which Ivan Ilyitch was expected to sympathise, though he never had the slightest idea about them, the need for him to fence off a world apart for himself outside his family life became still more imperative. As his wife grew more irritable and exacting, so did Ivan Ilyitch more and more transfer the centre of gravity of his life to his official work. He became fonder and fonder of official life, and more ambitious than he had been.
paras.uz: Bola tug'ilishi, uni emizishga urinishlar, ovqat bilan turli muvaffaqiyatsiz tajribalar, Ivan Ilich hamdardlik bildirishi kutilgan, lekin u haqida zarracha tasavvurga ega bo'lmagan go'dak va onasining haqiqiy va xayoliy kasalliklari bilan unga oilaviy hayotdan tashqarida o'zi uchun alohida dunyoni to'siq bilan ajratib olish zarurati yanada kuchaydi. Xotini qanchalik jahldor va talabchan bo'lib borgan sari, Ivan Ilich ham hayotining og'irlik markazini shunchalik ko'proq xizmat ishiga ko'chirdi. U xizmat hayotini tobora ko'proq yaxshi ko'rib qoldi va avvalgidan shuhratparastroq bo'ldi.

paras.en: Very quickly, not more than a year after his wedding, Ivan Ilyitch had become aware that conjugal life, though providing certain comforts, was in reality a very intricate and difficult business towards which one must, if one is to do one’s duty, that is, lead the decorous life approved by society, work out for oneself a definite line, just as in the government service.
paras.uz: Juda tez, to'yidan bir yil o'tmay, Ivan Ilich oilaviy hayot muayyan qulayliklar bersa-da, aslida juda murakkab va qiyin ish ekanini angladi; agar burchingni bajarmoqchi bo'lsang, ya'ni jamiyat ma'qullaydigan odobli hayot kechirmoqchi bo'lsang, unga nisbatan, xuddi davlat xizmatidagidek, o'zing uchun aniq bir yo'l ishlab chiqishing kerak.

paras.en: And such a line Ivan Ilyitch did work out for himself in his married life. He expected from his home life only those comforts⁠—of dinner at home, of housekeeper and bed which it could give him, and, above all, that perfect propriety in external observances required by public opinion. For the rest, he looked for good-humoured pleasantness, and if he found it he was very thankful. If he met with antagonism and querulousness, he promptly retreated into the separate world he had shut off for himself in his official life, and there he found solace.
paras.uz: Va Ivan Ilich oilaviy hayotida o'zi uchun shunday yo'lni ishlab chiqdi. U uy hayotidan faqat u bera oladigan qulayliklarni — uyda tushlik, uy bekasi va to'shakni va, eng muhimi, jamoatchilik fikri talab qiladigan tashqi odobga to'liq rioya qilinishini kutardi. Qolganida u xushfe'l yoqimlilik izlardi va topsa, juda minnatdor bo'lardi. Agar qarshilik va noliqlarga duch kelsa, darhol xizmat hayotida o'zi uchun ajratib olgan alohida dunyoga chekinardi va u yerda taskin topardi.

paras.en: Ivan Ilyitch was prized as a good official, and three years later he was made assistant public prosecutor. The new duties of this position, their dignity, the possibility of bringing anyone to trial and putting anyone in prison, the publicity of the speeches and the success Ivan Ilyitch had in that part of his work⁠—all this made his official work still more attractive to him.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich yaxshi amaldor sifatida qadrlanardi va uch yildan keyin prokuror yordamchisi etib tayinlandi. Bu lavozimning yangi vazifalari, ularning salobati, istalgan odamni sudga berish va istalgan odamni qamoqqa tashlash imkoniyati, nutqlarining ommaviyligi va Ivan Ilichning ishining bu qismida erishgan muvaffaqiyati — bularning hammasi xizmat ishini unga yanada jozibali qildi.

paras.en: Children were born to him. His wife became steadily more querulous and ill-tempered, but the line Ivan Ilyitch had taken up for himself in home life put him almost out of reach of her grumbling.
paras.uz: Uning bolalari tug'ildi. Xotini tobora noliqchi va jahldor bo'lib bordi, lekin Ivan Ilich uy hayotida o'zi uchun tanlagan yo'l uni uning to'ng'illashlaridan deyarli yetib bo'lmaydigan qilib qo'ydi.

paras.en: After seven years of service in the same town, Ivan Ilyitch was transferred to another province with the post of public prosecutor. They moved, money was short, and his wife did not like the place they had moved to. The salary was indeed a little higher than before, but their expenses were larger. Besides, a couple of children died, and home life consequently became even less agreeable for Ivan Ilyitch.
paras.uz: Bir shaharda yetti yil xizmat qilgach, Ivan Ilich prokuror lavozimi bilan boshqa gubernaga o'tkazildi. Ular ko'chishdi, pul yetishmasdi, xotiniga esa ko'chib kelgan joylari yoqmadi. Maosh avvalgidan biroz yuqoriroq edi, lekin xarajatlari kattaroq edi. Buning ustiga, ikki bola vafot etdi va natijada uy hayoti Ivan Ilich uchun yanada yoqimsiz bo'lib qoldi.

paras.en: For every mischance that occurred in their new place of residence, Praskovya Fyodorovna blamed her husband. The greater number of subjects of conversation between husband and wife, especially the education of the children, led to questions which were associated with previous quarrels, and quarrels were ready to break out at every instant. There remained only those rare periods of being in love which did indeed come upon them, but never lasted long. These were the islands at which they put in for a time, but they soon set off again upon the ocean of concealed hostility, that was made manifest in their aloofness from one another. This aloofness might have distressed Ivan Ilyitch if he had believed that this ought not to be so, but by now he regarded this position as perfectly normal, and it was indeed the goal towards which he worked in his home life. His aim was to make himself more and more free from the unpleasant aspects of domestic life and to render them harmless and decorous. And he attained this aim by spending less and less time with his family; and when he was forced to be at home, he endeavoured to secure his tranquillity by the presence of outsiders. The great thing for Ivan Ilyitch was having his office. In the official world all the interest of life was concentrated for him. And this interest absorbed him. The sense of his own power, the consciousness of being able to ruin anyone he wanted to ruin, even the external dignity of his office, when he made his entry into the court or met subordinate officials, his success in the eyes of his superiors and his subordinates, and, above all, his masterly handling of cases, of which he was conscious⁠—all this delighted him and, together with chat with his colleagues, dining out, and whist, filled his life. So that, on the whole, Ivan Ilyitch’s life still went on in the way he thought it should go⁠—agreeably and decorously.
paras.uz: Yangi yashash joylarida yuz bergan har bir omadsizlik uchun Praskovya Fyodorovna erini aybladi. Er-xotin o'rtasidagi suhbat mavzularining aksariyati, ayniqsa bolalar tarbiyasi, avvalgi janjallar bilan bog'liq masalalarga olib borardi va janjallar har lahzada chiqishga tayyor edi. Faqat ularning boshiga haqiqatan ham kelgan, lekin hech qachon uzoq davom etmagan kamdan-kam oshiqlik davrlari qoldi. Bular ular bir muddat to'xtagan orollar edi, lekin ular tez orada yana bir-biridan uzoqlashishda namoyon bo'lgan yashirin adovat ummoniga suzib ketishardi. Agar Ivan Ilich bunday bo'lmasligi kerak, deb ishonganida, bu uzoqlashish uni qayg'uga solishi mumkin edi, lekin endi u bu holatni mutlaqo normal deb bilardi va aslida uy hayotida aynan shunga intilardi. Uning maqsadi oilaviy hayotning noxush tomonlaridan o'zini tobora ozod qilish va ularni zararsiz va odobli qilish edi. Va u bu maqsadga oilasi bilan tobora kamroq vaqt o'tkazish orqali erishdi; uyda bo'lishga majbur bo'lganida esa, begonalar ishtiroki bilan xotirjamligini ta'minlashga harakat qilardi. Ivan Ilich uchun eng muhim narsa xizmati edi. Hayotning butun qiziqishi u uchun xizmat dunyosida jamlangan edi. Va bu qiziqish uni butunlay o'ziga tortdi. O'z hokimiyatini his qilish, istagan odamini halok qila olishini anglash, hatto sud zaliga kirib kelganida yoki qo'l ostidagi amaldorlarni uchratganida lavozimining tashqi salobati, boshliqlari va qo'l ostidagilar nazarida muvaffaqiyati va, eng muhimi, o'zi anglagan ishlarni mohirona yuritishi — bularning hammasi uni quvontirardi va hamkasblari bilan suhbat, mehmondorchiliklar va vist bilan birga uning hayotini to'ldirardi. Shunday qilib, umuman olganda, Ivan Ilichning hayoti hamon u o'ylaganidek — yoqimli va odobli kechardi.

paras.en: So he lived for another seven years. His eldest daughter was already sixteen, another child had died, and there was left only one other, a boy at the high school, a subject of dissension. Ivan Ilyitch wanted to send him to the school of jurisprudence, while Praskovya Fyodorovna to spite him sent him to the high school. The daughter had been educated at home, and had turned out well; the boy too did fairly well at his lessons.
paras.uz: U yana yetti yil shunday yashadi. To'ng'ich qizi allaqachon o'n olti yoshda edi, yana bir bola vafot etdi va faqat bittasi — kelishmovchilik mavzusi bo'lgan gimnazist o'g'il qoldi. Ivan Ilich uni huquqshunoslik maktabiga yubormoqchi edi, Praskovya Fyodorovna esa uning gapiga qarshi qilib, uni gimnaziyaga yubordi. Qiz uyda ta'lim olgan va yaxshi tarbiyalangan edi; o'g'il ham darslarida ancha yaxshi o'qirdi.
