chapters.title: III. The new apartment and the fall

paras.en: Such was Ivan Ilyitch’s life for seventeen years after his marriage. He had been by now a long while prosecutor, and had refused several appointments offered him, looking out for a more desirable post, when there occurred an unexpected incident which utterly destroyed his peace of mind. Ivan Ilyitch had been expecting to be appointed presiding judge in a university town, but a certain Goppe somehow stole a march on him and secured the appointment. Ivan Ilyitch took offence, began upbraiding him, and quarrelled with him and with his own superiors. A coolness was felt towards him, and on the next appointment that was made he was again passed over.
paras.uz: Uylanganidan keyin o'n yetti yil davomida Ivan Ilichning hayoti shunday kechdi. U allaqachon uzoq vaqtdan beri prokuror edi va kerakliroq lavozimni kutib, unga taklif qilingan bir necha tayinlovni rad etgan edi, shu payt uning xotirjamligini butunlay buzgan kutilmagan voqea yuz berdi. Ivan Ilich universitet shahrida sud raisi etib tayinlanishini kutayotgan edi, lekin qandaydir Goppe qandaydir yo'l bilan undan o'zib ketdi va bu lavozimni egalladi. Ivan Ilich xafa bo'ldi, uni ayblay boshladi va u bilan ham, o'z boshliqlari bilan ham janjallashdi. Unga nisbatan sovuqlik sezildi va keyingi tayinlovda uni yana chetlab o'tishdi.

paras.en: This was in the year 1880. That year was the most painful one in Ivan Ilyitch’s life. During that year it became evident on the one hand that his pay was insufficient for his expenses; on the other hand, that he had been forgotten by everyone, and that what seemed to him the most monstrous, the cruelest injustice, appeared to other people as a quite commonplace fact. Even his father felt no obligation to assist him. He felt that everyone had deserted him, and that everyone regarded his position with an income of three thousand five hundred roubles as a quite normal and even fortunate one. He alone, with a sense of the injustice done him, and the everlasting nagging of his wife and the debts he had begun to accumulate, living beyond his means, knew that his position was far from being normal.
paras.uz: Bu 1880-yilda bo'ldi. O'sha yil Ivan Ilichning hayotidagi eng og'ir yil bo'ldi. O'sha yili bir tomondan maoshi xarajatlariga yetmasligi, ikkinchi tomondan esa hamma uni unutgani va unga eng dahshatli, eng shafqatsiz adolatsizlik bo'lib tuyulgan narsa boshqalarga mutlaqo oddiy fakt bo'lib ko'rinishi ayon bo'ldi. Hatto otasi ham unga yordam berishni o'z burchi deb hisoblamadi. U hamma uni tashlab ketganini va hamma uch ming besh yuz rubl daromadli holatini mutlaqo normal va hatto baxtli deb bilishini his qildi. Faqat uning o'zi — o'ziga qilingan adolatsizlikni his qilib, xotinining abadiy to'ng'illashlari va imkoniyatidan ortiq yashab yig'a boshlagan qarzlari bilan — uning holati normal bo'lishdan juda yiroq ekanini bilardi.

paras.en: The summer of that year, to cut down his expenses, he took a holiday and went with his wife to spend the summer in the country at her brother’s.
paras.uz: O'sha yilning yozida xarajatlarini qisqartirish uchun u ta'til oldi va xotini bilan yozni qishloqda, xotinining akasinikida o'tkazish uchun jo'nadi.

paras.en: In the country, with no official duties to occupy him, Ivan Ilyitch was for the first time a prey not to simple boredom, but to intolerable depression; and he made up his mind that things could not go on like that, and that it was absolutely necessary to take some decisive steps.
paras.uz: Qishloqda, uni band qiladigan xizmat vazifalari bo'lmagani uchun, Ivan Ilich birinchi marta oddiy zerikishga emas, chidab bo'lmas tushkunlikka tushdi; va u ishlar bunday davom eta olmasligiga, qandaydir qat'iy qadamlar qo'yish mutlaqo zarurligiga qaror qildi.

paras.en: After a sleepless night spent by Ivan Ilyitch walking up and down the terrace, he determined to go to Petersburg to take active steps and to get transferred to some other department, so as to revenge himself on them, the people, that is, who had not known how to appreciate him.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich terrasada u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yurib o'tkazgan uyqusiz tundan keyin, Peterburgga borib, faol harakat qilishga va boshqa vazirlikka o'tishga — ularni, ya'ni uni qadrlay bilmagan odamlarni jazolash uchun — qaror qildi.

paras.en: Next day, in spite of all the efforts of his wife and his mother-in-law to dissuade him, he set off to Petersburg.
paras.uz: Ertasi kuni xotini va qaynonasining uni qaytarish uchun qilgan barcha urinishlariga qaramay, u Peterburgga jo'nab ketdi.

paras.en: He went with a single object before him⁠—to obtain a post with an income of five thousand. He was ready now to be satisfied with a post in any department, of any tendency, with any kind of work. He must only have a post⁠—a post with five thousand, in the executive department, the banks, the railways, the Empress Marya’s institutions, even in the customs duties⁠—what was essential was five thousand, and essential it was, too, to get out of the department in which they had failed to appreciate his value.
paras.uz: U yagona maqsad bilan ketdi — besh ming daromadli lavozim olish. U endi har qanday vazirlikdagi, har qanday yo'nalishdagi, har qanday ishli lavozimga rozi edi. Faqat lavozim bo'lsa bas — besh minglik lavozim, ma'muriy idorada, banklarda, temir yo'llarda, Imperatritsa Mariya muassasalarida, hatto bojxonada — eng muhimi besh ming edi, uning qadrini bilmagan vazirlikdan chiqib ketish ham shunchalik muhim edi.

paras.en: And, behold, this quest of Ivan Ilyitch’s was crowned with wonderful, unexpected success. At Kursk there got into the same first-class carriage F. S. Ilyin, an acquaintance, who told him of a telegram just received by the governor of Kursk, announcing a change about to take place in the ministry⁠—Pyotr Ivanovitch was to be superseded by Ivan Semyonovitch.
paras.uz: Va mana, Ivan Ilichning bu izlanishi ajoyib, kutilmagan muvaffaqiyat bilan toj kiydi. Kurskda o'sha birinchi toifa vagoniga tanishi F. S. Ilyin chiqdi va unga Kursk gubernatori endigina olgan telegramma haqida gapirib berdi: vazirlikda o'zgarish bo'lishi kutilayotgan ekan — Pyotr Ivanovichning o'rniga Ivan Semyonovich tayinlanar ekan.

paras.en: The proposed change, apart from its significance for Russia, had special significance for Ivan Ilyitch from the fact that by bringing to the front a new person, Pyotr Petrovitch, and obviously, therefore, his friend Zahar Ivanovitch, it was in the highest degree propitious to Ivan Ilyitch’s own plans. Zahar Ivanovitch was a friend and schoolfellow of Ivan Ilyitch’s.
paras.uz: Taxmin qilinayotgan o'zgarish, Rossiya uchun ahamiyatidan tashqari, Ivan Ilich uchun alohida ahamiyatga ega edi, chunki u oldinga yangi odamni — Pyotr Petrovichni va, aniqki, uning do'sti Zaxar Ivanovichni olib chiqib, Ivan Ilichning o'z rejalari uchun nihoyatda qulay edi. Zaxar Ivanovich Ivan Ilichning do'sti va maktabdoshi edi.

paras.en: At Moscow the news was confirmed. On arriving at Petersburg, Ivan Ilyitch looked up Zahar Ivanovitch, and received a positive promise of an appointment in his former department⁠—that of justice.
paras.uz: Moskvada xabar tasdiqlandi. Peterburgga yetib kelgach, Ivan Ilich Zaxar Ivanovichni topdi va o'zining avvalgi vazirligida — adliya vazirligida — lavozim haqida aniq va'da oldi.

paras.en: A week later he telegraphed to his wife: “Zahar Miller’s place. At first report I receive appointment.”
paras.uz: Bir haftadan keyin u xotiniga telegramma yubordi: «Zaxar Millerning o'rnida. Birinchi ma'ruzadayoq tayinlov olaman.»

paras.en: Thanks to these changes, Ivan Ilyitch unexpectedly obtained, in the same department as before, an appointment which placed him two stages higher than his former colleagues, and gave him an income of five thousand, together with the official allowance of three thousand five hundred for travelling expenses. All his ill-humour with his former enemies and the whole department was forgotten, and Ivan Ilyitch was completely happy.
paras.uz: Bu o'zgarishlar tufayli Ivan Ilich kutilmaganda avvalgi vazirligining o'zida uni sobiq hamkasblaridan ikki pog'ona yuqoriga qo'ygan va safar xarajatlari uchun uch ming besh yuzlik rasmiy pul bilan birga besh ming daromad beradigan lavozimni oldi. Sobiq dushmanlariga va butun vazirlikka bo'lgan barcha jahli unutildi va Ivan Ilich butunlay baxtiyor edi.

paras.en: Ivan Ilyitch went back to the country more lighthearted and good-tempered than he had been for a very long while. Praskovya Fyodorovna was in better spirits, too, and peace was patched up between them. Ivan Ilyitch described what respect everyone had shown him in Petersburg; how all those who had been his enemies had been put to shame, and were cringing now before him; how envious they were of his appointment, and still more of the high favour in which he stood at Petersburg.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich qishloqqa juda uzoq vaqtdan beri bo'lmaganidek beg'am va xushfe'l holda qaytdi. Praskovya Fyodorovnaning ham kayfiyati yaxshilandi va ular o'rtasida yarash tuzildi. Ivan Ilich Peterburgda hamma unga qanday hurmat ko'rsatganini; uning dushmanlari bo'lgan barcha odamlar qanday sharmanda bo'lgani va endi uning oldida laganbardorlik qilayotganini; ular uning tayinlanishiga, undan ham ko'proq Peterburgda unga bo'lgan yuksak iltifotga qanday hasad qilishayotganini gapirib berdi.

paras.en: Praskovya Fyodorovna listened to this, and pretended to believe it, and did not contradict him in anything, but confined herself to making plans, for her new arrangements in the town to which they would be moving. And Ivan Ilyitch saw with delight that these plans were his plans; that they were agreed; and that his life after this disturbing hitch in its progress was about to regain its true, normal character of lighthearted agreeableness and propriety.
paras.uz: Praskovya Fyodorovna buni tingladi, ishongandek ko'rindi va hech narsada unga qarshi chiqmadi, faqat ular ko'chib boradigan shahardagi yangi tartiblari uchun rejalar tuzish bilan cheklandi. Va Ivan Ilich bu rejalar uning rejalari ekanini, ular hamfikr ekanini va uning hayoti bu tashvishli to'xtalishdan keyin o'zining haqiqiy, normal beg'am yoqimlilik va odob xususiyatini qayta tiklash arafasida ekanini quvonch bilan ko'rdi.

paras.en: Ivan Ilyitch had come back to the country for a short stay only. He had to enter upon the duties of his new office on the 10th of September; and besides, he needed some time to settle in a new place, to move all his belongings from the other province, to purchase and order many things in addition; in short, to arrange things as settled in his own mind, and almost exactly as settled in the heart too of Praskovya Fyodorovna.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich qishloqqa faqat qisqa muddatga qaytgan edi. U 10-sentabrda yangi lavozim vazifalariga kirishishi kerak edi; buning ustiga, yangi joyga joylashish, barcha narsalarini boshqa gubernadan ko'chirish, qo'shimcha ko'p narsalarni sotib olish va buyurtma qilish uchun, qisqasi, hamma narsani o'z ko'nglida belgilanganidek va deyarli aynan Praskovya Fyodorovnaning ko'nglida ham belgilanganidek tartibga keltirish uchun unga biroz vaqt kerak edi.

paras.en: And now when everything was so successfully arranged, and when he and his wife were agreed in their aim, and were, besides, so little together, they got on with one another as they had not got on together since the early years of their married life. Ivan Ilyitch had thought of taking his family away with him at once; but his sister and his brother-in-law, who had suddenly become extremely cordial and intimate with him and his family, were so pressing in urging them to stay that he set off alone.
paras.uz: Va endi hamma narsa shunchalik muvaffaqiyatli joyiga tushgan, u va xotini maqsadda hamfikr va buning ustiga birga juda kam bo'lgan bir paytda, ular oilaviy hayotlarining dastlabki yillaridan beri bo'lmaganidek bir-biri bilan yaxshi kelishib ketishdi. Ivan Ilich oilasini darhol o'zi bilan olib ketishni o'ylagan edi; lekin to'satdan u va uning oilasiga nihoyatda samimiy va yaqin bo'lib qolgan singlisi va pochchasi qolishlarini shunchalik qattiq so'rashdiki, u yolg'iz jo'nadi.

paras.en: Ivan Ilyitch started off; and the lighthearted temper produced by his success, and his good understanding with his wife, one thing backing up another, did not desert him all the time. He found a charming set of apartments, the very thing both husband and wife had dreamed of. Spacious, lofty reception-rooms in the old style, a comfortable, dignified-looking study for him, rooms for his wife and daughter, a schoolroom for his son, everything as though planned on purpose for them. Ivan Ilyitch himself looked after the furnishing of them, chose the wallpapers, bought furniture, by preference antique furniture, which had a peculiar comme-il-faut style to his mind, and it all grew up and grew up, and really attained the ideal he had set before himself. When he had half finished arranging the house, his arrangement surpassed his own expectations. He saw the comme-il-faut character, elegant and free from vulgarity, that the whole would have when it was all ready. As he fell asleep he pictured to himself the reception-room as it would be. Looking at the drawing-room, not yet finished, he could see the hearth, the screen, the étagère, and the little chairs dotted here and there, the plates and dishes on the wall, and the bronzes as they would be when they were all put in their places. He was delighted with the thought of how he would impress Praskovya and Lizanka, who had taste too in this line. They would never expect anything like it. He was particularly successful in coming across and buying cheap old pieces of furniture, which gave a peculiarly aristocratic air to the whole. In his letters he purposely disparaged everything so as to surprise them. All this so absorbed him that the duties of his new office, though he was so fond of his official work, interested him less than he had expected. During sittings of the court he had moments of inattention; he pondered the question which sort of cornices to have on the window-blinds, straight or fluted. He was so interested in this business that he often set to work with his own hands, moved a piece of furniture, or hung up curtains himself. One day he went up a ladder to show a workman, who did not understand, how he wanted some hangings draped, made a false step and slipped; but, like a strong and nimble person, he clung on, and only knocked his side against the corner of a frame. The bruised place ached, but it soon passed off. Ivan Ilyitch felt all this time particularly good-humoured and well. He wrote: “I feel fifteen years younger.” He thought his house-furnishing would be finished in September, but it dragged on to the middle of October. But then the effect was charming; not he only said so, but everyone who saw it told him so too.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich jo'nab ketdi; muvaffaqiyati va xotini bilan yaxshi kelishuvi tug'dirgan beg'am kayfiyat, biri ikkinchisini quvvatlab, butun vaqt davomida uni tark etmadi. U er-xotin orzu qilgan aynan o'sha narsa — maftunkor kvartira topdi. Eski uslubdagi keng, baland mehmon xonalari, o'zi uchun qulay va salobatli ko'rinishdagi kabinet, xotini va qizi uchun xonalar, o'g'li uchun dars xonasi — hammasi go'yo ataylab ular uchun rejalashtirilgandek edi. Ivan Ilich ularni jihozlash bilan o'zi shug'ullandi, gulqog'ozlarni tanladi, mebel sotib oldi — afzalroq antiqa mebel, uning fikricha, bunda alohida comme il faut uslub bor edi — va hammasi o'sib-o'sib bordi va haqiqatan ham u o'z oldiga qo'ygan idealga yetdi. Uyni yarmigacha jihozlaganida, uning tartibi o'z kutganidan ham oshib ketdi. U hammasi tayyor bo'lganda butun uy qanday nafis va qo'pollikdan xoli comme il faut ko'rinishga ega bo'lishini ko'rardi. Uxlab qolayotib, mehmonxona qanday bo'lishini ko'z oldiga keltirardi. Hali tugallanmagan mehmonxonaga qarab, u kaminni, to'siqni, etajerkani, u yer-bu yerga qo'yilgan kichkina stullarni, devordagi likopcha va laganlarni, bronza buyumlarni — hammasi o'z joyiga qo'yilganda qanday bo'lishini ko'rardi. Bu sohada didi bor Praskovya va Lizankani qanday hayratga solishini o'ylab quvonardi. Ular hech qachon bunday narsani kutmaydilar. U ayniqsa arzon eski mebellarni topib, sotib olishda muvaffaqiyatli edi, ular butun uyga alohida aristokratik ko'rinish berardi. Maktublarida ularni hayratga solish uchun hamma narsani ataylab kamsitib yozardi. Bularning hammasi uni shunchalik o'ziga tortdiki, xizmat ishini juda yaxshi ko'rsa ham, yangi lavozim vazifalari uni kutganidan kamroq qiziqtirdi. Sud majlislari paytida u parishonxotir bo'lib qolardi: deraza pardalarining karnizlari qanday bo'lishi kerak — to'g'rimi yoki o'ymali — degan savol ustida o'ylardi. U bu ishga shunchalik qiziqib ketdiki, ko'pincha o'z qo'li bilan ishga kirishar, mebelni o'zi surar yoki pardalarni o'zi osardi. Bir kuni u tushunmagan ustaga pardani qanday osishni xohlayotganini ko'rsatish uchun narvonga chiqdi, qadamini noto'g'ri bosib, sirpanib ketdi; lekin kuchli va chaqqon odam sifatida ushlanib qoldi va faqat biqinini rom burchagiga urib oldi. Lat yegan joy og'ridi, lekin tez o'tib ketdi. Ivan Ilich butun shu vaqt davomida o'zini ayniqsa xushchaqchaq va sog'lom his qildi. U yozdi: «O'zimni o'n besh yosh yosharib ketgandek his qilyapman.» U uyni jihozlash sentabrda tugaydi deb o'ylagan edi, lekin u oktabr o'rtalarigacha cho'zildi. Lekin natija maftunkor bo'ldi; buni faqat u emas, uni ko'rgan har kim ham aytdi.

paras.en: In reality, it was all just what is commonly seen in the houses of people who are not exactly wealthy but want to look like wealthy people, and so succeed only in being like one another⁠—hangings, dark wood, flowers, rugs and bronzes, everything dark and highly polished, everything that all people of a certain class have so as to be like all people of a certain class. And in his case it was all so like that it made no impression at all; but it all seemed to him somehow special. When he met his family at the railway station and brought them to his newly furnished rooms, all lighted up in readiness, and a footman in a white tie opened the door into an entry decorated with flowers, and then they walked into the drawing-room and the study, uttering cries of delight, he was very happy, conducted them everywhere, eagerly drinking in their praises, and beaming with satisfaction. The same evening, while they talked about various things at tea, Praskovya Fyodorovna inquired about his fall, and he laughed and showed them how he had gone flying, and how he had frightened the upholsterer.
paras.uz: Aslida bularning hammasi unchalik boy bo'lmagan, lekin boy odamlarga o'xshashni istaydigan va shuning uchun faqat bir-biriga o'xshab qoladigan odamlarning uylarida odatda ko'rinadigan narsalarning aynan o'zi edi — pardalar, qora yog'och, gullar, gilamlar va bronzalar, hammasi qoramtir va yaltiroq, ma'lum tabaqadagi barcha odamlarga o'xshash bo'lish uchun ma'lum tabaqadagi barcha odamlarda bo'ladigan hamma narsa. Uning uyida ham hammasi shunchalik o'xshash ediki, hech qanday taassurot qoldirmasdi; lekin unga hammasi negadir alohida bo'lib tuyulardi. Oilasini temir yo'l vokzalida kutib olib, ularni yangi jihozlangan, kutib olishga tayyorlab yoritilgan xonalarga olib kelganida, oq galstukli malay gullar bilan bezatilgan dahlizga eshikni ochganida, keyin ular hayrat bilan qichqirib, mehmonxona va kabinetga kirganlarida, u juda baxtiyor edi, ularni hamma joyni aylantirib ko'rsatdi, ularning maqtovlarini ishtiyoq bilan tinglab, mamnuniyatdan porlab turdi. O'sha oqshom, choy ustida turli narsalar haqida gaplashishayotganida, Praskovya Fyodorovna uning yiqilishi haqida so'radi, u esa kulib, qanday uchib ketganini va pardachi ustani qanday qo'rqitib yuborganini ko'rsatdi.

paras.en: “It’s as well I’m something of an athlete. Another man might have been killed, and I got nothing worse than a blow here; when it’s touched it hurts, but it’s going off already; nothing but a bruise.”
paras.uz: — Yaxshiyamki, men biroz atletman. Boshqa odam o'lib qolishi mumkin edi, menga esa faqat mana shu yerga zarba tegdi xolos; ushlasang og'riydi, lekin allaqachon o'tib ketyapti; shunchaki lat yegan joy.

paras.en: And they began to live in their new abode, which, as is always the case, when they had got thoroughly settled in they found to be short of just one room, and with their new income, which, as always, was only a little⁠—some five hundred roubles⁠—too little, and everything went very well. Things went particularly well at first, before everything was quite finally arranged, and there was still something to do to the place⁠—something to buy, something to order, something to move, something to make to fit. Though there were indeed several disputes between husband and wife, both were so well satisfied, and there was so much to do, that it all went off without serious quarrels. When there was nothing left to arrange, it became a little dull, and something seemed to be lacking, but by then they were making acquaintances and forming habits, and life was filled up again.
paras.uz: Va ular yangi uylarida yashay boshlashdi; u, doim bo'lganidek, ular butunlay joylashib olgach, faqat bitta xonasi yetishmaydigan bo'lib chiqdi, yangi daromadlari esa, doim bo'lganidek, faqat ozgina — besh yuz rubl chamasi — yetishmasdi, va hammasi juda yaxshi ketdi. Avvaliga, hamma narsa uzil-kesil joyiga tushmagan va uyda hali qilinadigan biror ish bor — nimanidir sotib olish, nimanidir buyurtma qilish, nimanidir surish, nimanidir moslash kerak bo'lgan paytda ishlar ayniqsa yaxshi ketdi. Er-xotin o'rtasida haqiqatan ham bir necha nizolar bo'lgan bo'lsa-da, ikkalasi ham shunchalik mamnun edi va qiladigan ish shunchalik ko'p ediki, hammasi jiddiy janjallarsiz o'tdi. Tartibga keltiradigan narsa qolmaganda, biroz zerikarli bo'lib qoldi va nimadir yetishmayotgandek tuyuldi, lekin o'shanda ular tanishlar orttirib, odatlar shakllantirayotgan edilar va hayot yana to'ldi.

paras.en: Ivan Ilyitch, after spending the morning in the court, returned home to dinner, and at first he was generally in a good humour, although this was apt to be upset a little, and precisely on account of the new abode. Every spot on the tablecloth, on the hangings, the string of a window blind broken, irritated him. He had devoted so much trouble to the arrangement of the rooms that any disturbance of their order distressed him. But, on the whole, the life of Ivan Ilyitch ran its course as, according to his conviction, life ought to do⁠—easily, agreeably, and decorously. He got up at nine, drank his coffee, read the newspaper, then put on his official uniform, and went to the court. There the routine of the daily work was ready mapped out for him, and he stepped into it at once. People with petitions, inquiries in the office, the office itself, the sittings⁠—public and preliminary. In all this the great thing necessary was to exclude everything with the sap of life in it, which always disturbs the regular course of official business, not to admit any sort of relations with people except the official relations; the motive of all intercourse had to be simply the official motive, and the intercourse itself to be only official. A man would come, for instance, anxious for certain information. Ivan Ilyitch, not being the functionary on duty, would have nothing whatever to do with such a man. But if this man’s relation to him as a member of the court is such as can be formulated on official stamped paper⁠—within the limits of such a relation Ivan Ilyitch would do everything, positively everything he could, and in doing so would observe the semblance of human friendly relations, that is, the courtesies of social life. But where the official relation ended, there everything else stopped too. This art of keeping the official aspect of things apart from his real life, Ivan Ilyitch possessed in the highest degree; and through long practice and natural aptitude, he had brought it to such a pitch of perfection that he even permitted himself at times, like a skilled specialist as it were in jest, to let the human and official relations mingle. He allowed himself this liberty just because he felt he had the power at any moment if he wished it to take up the purely official line again and to drop the human relation. This thing was not simply easy, agreeable, and decorous; in Ivan Ilyitch’s hands it attained a positively artistic character. In the intervals of business he smoked, drank tea, chatted a little about politics, a little about public affairs, a little about cards, but most of all about appointments in the service. And tired, but feeling like some artist who has skilfully played his part in the performance, one of the first violins in the orchestra, he returned home. At home his daughter and her mother had been paying calls somewhere, or else someone had been calling on them; the son had been at school, had been preparing his lessons with his teachers, and duly learning correctly what was taught at the high school. Everything was as it should be. After dinner, if there were no visitors, Ivan Ilyitch sometimes read some book of which people were talking, and in the evening sat down to work, that is, read official papers, compared them with the laws, sorted depositions, and put them under the laws. This he found neither tiresome nor entertaining. It was tiresome when he might have been playing “screw”; but if there were no “screw” going on, it was anyway better than sitting alone or with his wife. Ivan Ilyitch’s pleasures were little dinners, to which he invited ladies and gentlemen of good social position, and such methods of passing the time with them as were usual with such persons, so that his drawing-room might be like all other drawing-rooms.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich ertalabni sudda o'tkazib, tushlikka uyga qaytardi va avvaliga odatda kayfiyati yaxshi bo'lardi, garchi bu biroz buzilishga moyil bo'lsa-da, aynan yangi uy tufayli. Dasturxondagi, pardalardagi har bir dog', uzilgan parda ipi uning jahlini chiqarardi. U xonalarni tartibga keltirishga shunchalik ko'p mehnat sarflagan ediki, ularning tartibi har qanday buzilishi uni xafa qilardi. Lekin umuman olganda, Ivan Ilichning hayoti, uning ishonchiga ko'ra, hayot qanday kechishi kerak bo'lsa, shunday — yengil, yoqimli va odobli kechardi. U soat to'qqizda turardi, qahvasini ichardi, gazeta o'qirdi, keyin mundirini kiyib, sudga borardi. U yerda kundalik ishning tartibi uning uchun oldindan belgilangan edi va u darhol unga kirishib ketardi. Arizali odamlar, idorada so'rovlar, idoraning o'zi, majlislar — ochiq va dastlabki. Bularning barchasida eng zarur narsa — xizmat ishlarining muntazam borishini doim buzadigan hayot shirasi bor hamma narsani chiqarib tashlash, odamlar bilan rasmiy munosabatlardan boshqa hech qanday munosabatga yo'l qo'ymaslik edi; har qanday muloqotning sababi faqat rasmiy sabab bo'lishi, muloqotning o'zi esa faqat rasmiy bo'lishi kerak edi. Masalan, muayyan ma'lumot olishni istagan bir odam kelardi. Ivan Ilich navbatchi amaldor bo'lmagani uchun bunday odam bilan hech qanday ishi bo'lmasdi. Lekin agar bu odamning unga sud a'zosi sifatidagi munosabati muhrli rasmiy qog'ozda ifodalanishi mumkin bo'lsa — bunday munosabat chegarasida Ivan Ilich qo'lidan kelgan hamma narsani, mutlaqo hamma narsani qilardi va bunda insoniy do'stona munosabatlar ko'rinishini, ya'ni jamiyatdagi xushmuomalalikni saqlardi. Lekin rasmiy munosabat tugagan joyda, qolgan hamma narsa ham to'xtardi. Narsalarning rasmiy tomonini haqiqiy hayotidan ajratib turish san'atini Ivan Ilich eng yuksak darajada egallagan edi; uzoq mashq va tabiiy qobiliyat tufayli uni shunday mukammallik darajasiga yetkazgan ediki, ba'zan, go'yo hazillashayotgan mohir mutaxassisdek, insoniy va rasmiy munosabatlarni aralashtirishga ham o'ziga ruxsat berardi. U o'ziga bu erkinlikni aynan istalgan paytda, xohlasa, yana sof rasmiy yo'lga qaytish va insoniy munosabatni tashlash qudratiga ega ekanini his qilgani uchun berardi. Bu ish shunchaki yengil, yoqimli va odobli emas edi; Ivan Ilichning qo'lida u hatto badiiy xususiyat kasb etardi. Ishlar oralig'ida u chekardi, choy ichardi, biroz siyosat haqida, biroz jamoat ishlari haqida, biroz qarta haqida, lekin eng ko'p xizmatdagi tayinlovlar haqida gaplashardi. Va charchagan, lekin spektakldagi rolini mohirona ijro etgan san'atkordek, orkestrdagi birinchi skripkachilardan biridek his qilib, uyiga qaytardi. Uyda qizi va onasi qayergadir mehmonga borib kelgan yoki kimdir ularnikiga kelgan bo'lardi; o'g'li gimnaziyada bo'lgan, o'qituvchilari bilan darslarini tayyorlagan va gimnaziyada o'qitiladigan narsalarni tartib bilan to'g'ri o'rgangan bo'lardi. Hammasi qanday bo'lishi kerak bo'lsa, shunday edi. Tushlikdan keyin, mehmonlar bo'lmasa, Ivan Ilich ba'zan odamlar gaplashayotgan biror kitobni o'qirdi, kechqurun esa ishga o'tirardi, ya'ni rasmiy qog'ozlarni o'qirdi, ularni qonunlar bilan solishtirardi, ko'rsatmalarni saralardi va ularni qonunlar ostiga qo'yardi. Bu unga na zerikarli, na qiziqarli tuyulardi. «Vint» o'ynash mumkin bo'lganda zerikarli edi; lekin «vint» bo'lmasa, baribir yolg'iz yoki xotini bilan o'tirishdan yaxshiroq edi. Ivan Ilichning lazzatlari jamiyatda yaxshi mavqega ega xonim va janoblarni taklif qiladigan kichik tushliklar va mehmonxonasi boshqa barcha mehmonxonalarga o'xshashi uchun bunday odamlar bilan odatdagidek vaqt o'tkazish usullari edi.

paras.en: Once they even gave a party⁠—a dance. And Ivan Ilyitch enjoyed it, and everything was very successful, except that it led to a violent quarrel with his wife over the tarts and sweetmeats. Praskovya Fyodorovna had her own plan; while Ivan Ilyitch insisted on getting everything from an expensive pastrycook, and ordered a great many tarts, and the quarrel was because these tarts were left over and the pastrycook’s bill came to forty-five roubles. The quarrel was a violent and unpleasant one, so much so that Praskovya Fyodorovna called him, “Fool, imbecile.” And he clutched at his head, and in his anger made some allusion to a divorce. But the party itself was enjoyable. There were all the best people, and Ivan Ilyitch danced with Princess Trufonov, the sister of the one so well known in connection with the charitable association called, “Bear my Burden.” His official pleasures lay in the gratification of his pride; his social pleasures lay in the gratification of his vanity. But Ivan Ilyitch’s most real pleasure was the pleasure of playing “screw,” the Russian equivalent for “poker.” He admitted to himself that after all, after whatever unpleasant incidents there had been in his life, the pleasure which burned like a candle before all others was sitting with good players, and not noisy partners, at “screw”; and, of course, a four-hand game (playing with five was never a success, though one pretends to like it particularly), and with good cards, to play a shrewd, serious game, then supper and a glass of wine. And after “screw,” especially after winning some small stakes (winning large sums was unpleasant), Ivan Ilyitch went to bed in a particularly happy frame of mind.
paras.uz: Bir safar ular hatto ziyofat — raqs kechasi uyushtirishdi. Ivan Ilichga yoqdi va hamma narsa juda muvaffaqiyatli o'tdi, faqat pirog va shirinliklar tufayli xotini bilan qattiq janjal chiqdi. Praskovya Fyodorovnaning o'z rejasi bor edi; Ivan Ilich esa hamma narsani qimmat qandolatchidan olishni talab qildi va juda ko'p pirog buyurtma qildi, janjal esa bu piroglar ortib qolgani va qandolatchining hisobi qirq besh rublga yetgani uchun chiqdi. Janjal shunchalik qattiq va noxush bo'ldiki, Praskovya Fyodorovna uni «Ahmoq, nodon» deb atadi. U esa boshini changallab, jahl ustida ajrashish haqida nimadir deb shama qildi. Lekin ziyofatning o'zi yoqimli o'tdi. Eng yaxshi odamlarning hammasi bor edi va Ivan Ilich «Yukimni ko'tar» deb ataladigan xayriya jamiyati bilan mashhur bo'lgan knyaginyaning singlisi knyaginya Trufonova bilan raqsga tushdi. Uning xizmat lazzatlari g'ururini qondirishda edi; ijtimoiy lazzatlari shuhratparastligini qondirishda edi. Lekin Ivan Ilichning eng haqiqiy lazzati «vint» o'ynash lazzati edi. U o'ziga tan olardiki, axir, hayotidagi har qanday noxush voqealardan keyin ham, boshqa barcha lazzatlardan oldin sham kabi yonib turgan lazzat — yaxshi o'yinchilar va shovqin qilmaydigan sheriklar bilan «vint» o'ynab o'tirish edi; albatta, to'rt kishilik o'yinda (besh kishi bilan o'ynash hech qachon yaxshi chiqmaydi, garchi bu ayniqsa yoqadigandek ko'rsatilsa ham) va yaxshi qartalar bilan, aqlli, jiddiy o'yin o'ynash, keyin kechki ovqat va bir qadah vino. «Vint»dan keyin, ayniqsa kichik pul yutib olgandan keyin (katta pul yutish noxush edi) Ivan Ilich ayniqsa baxtiyor kayfiyatda uxlashga yotardi.

paras.en: So they lived. They moved in the very best circle, and were visited by people of consequence and young people.
paras.uz: Ular shunday yashashdi. Ular eng yaxshi doirada aylanishardi, ularnikiga obro'li odamlar va yoshlar kelishardi.

paras.en: In their views of their circle of acquaintances, the husband, the wife, and the daughter were in complete accord; and without any expressed agreement on the subject, they all acted alike in dropping and shaking off various friends and relations, shabby persons who swooped down upon them in their drawing-room with Japanese plates on the walls, and pressed their civilities on them. Soon these shabby persons ceased fluttering about them, and none but the very best society was seen at the Golovins. Young men began to pay attention to Lizanka; and Petrishtchev, the son of Dmitry Ivanovitch Petrishtchev, and the sole heir of his fortune, an examining magistrate, began to be so attentive to Lizanka, that Ivan Ilyitch had raised the question with his wife whether it would not be as well to arrange a sledge drive for them, or to get up some theatricals. So they lived. And everything went on in this way without change, and everything was very nice.
paras.uz: O'z tanishlar doirasiga qarashda er, xotin va qiz to'liq hamfikr edilar; va bu haqda hech qanday og'zaki kelishuvsiz, devorlarida yapon likopchalari osilgan mehmonxonalariga yopirilib kelib, ularga xushomad qiladigan turli do'stlar va qarindoshlardan — ko'rimsiz odamlardan — qutulish va ularni o'zlaridan uzoqlashtirishda hammasi bir xil harakat qilishdi. Tez orada bu ko'rimsiz odamlar ularning atrofida pirpirashni to'xtatishdi va Golovinlarnikida faqat eng yaxshi jamiyat ko'rinadigan bo'ldi. Yigitlar Lizankaga e'tibor bera boshlashdi; Dmitriy Ivanovich Petrishchevning o'g'li va boyligining yagona merosxo'ri, tergovchi Petrishchev Lizankaga shunchalik e'tiborli bo'la boshladiki, Ivan Ilich xotini bilan ular uchun chana sayri uyushtirish yoki biror tomosha qo'yish yaxshi bo'lmasmikan, degan masalani ko'tardi. Ular shunday yashashdi. Va hamma narsa o'zgarishsiz shunday davom etdi va hamma narsa juda yaxshi edi.

chapters.recap_uz: 1880-yildagi omadsizlikdan keyin Ivan Ilich Peterburgda yaxshi lavozim oladi. U yangi kvartirani zavq bilan jihozlaydi; parda osayotib narvondan yiqilib, biqinini urib oladi. chapters.title: IV. The doctors

paras.en: All were in good health. One could not use the word ill-health in connection with the symptoms Ivan Ilyitch sometimes complained of, namely, a queer taste in his mouth and a sort of uncomfortable feeling on the left side of the stomach.
paras.uz: Hamma sog'-salomat edi. Ivan Ilich ba'zan shikoyat qiladigan alomatlar — og'zidagi g'alati ta'm va qornining chap tomonidagi qandaydir noqulaylik — haqida kasallik so'zini ishlatib bo'lmasdi.

paras.en: But it came to pass that this uncomfortable feeling kept increasing, and became not exactly a pain, but a continual sense of weight in his side and irritable temper. This irritable temper continually growing and growing, began at last to mar the agreeable easiness and decorum that had reigned in the Golovin household. Quarrels between the husband and wife became more and more frequent, and soon all the easiness and amenity of life had fallen away, and mere propriety was maintained with difficulty. Scenes became again more frequent. Again there were only islands in the sea of contention⁠—and but few of these⁠—at which the husband and wife could meet without an outbreak. And Praskovya Fyodorovna said now, not without grounds, that her husband had a trying temper. With her characteristic exaggeration, she said he had always had this awful temper, and she had needed all her sweetness to put up with it for twenty years. It was true that it was he now who began the quarrels. His gusts of temper always broke out just before dinner, and often just as he was beginning to eat, at the soup. He would notice that some piece of the crockery had been chipped, or that the food was not nice, or that his son put his elbow on the table, or his daughter’s hair was not arranged as he liked it. And whatever it was, he laid the blame of it on Praskovya Fyodorovna. Praskovya Fyodorovna had at first retorted in the same strain, and said all sorts of horrid things to him; but on two occasions, just at the beginning of dinner, he had flown into such a frenzy that she perceived that it was due to physical derangement, and was brought on by taking food, and she controlled herself; she did not reply, but simply made haste to get dinner over. Praskovya Fyodorovna took great credit to herself for this exercise of self-control. Making up her mind that her husband had a fearful temper, and made her life miserable, she began to feel sorry for herself. And the more she felt for herself, the more she hated her husband. She began to wish he were dead; yet could not wish it, because then there would be no income. And this exasperated her against him even more. She considered herself dreadfully unfortunate, precisely because even his death could not save her, and she felt irritated and concealed it, and this hidden irritation on her side increased his irritability.
paras.uz: Lekin shunday bo'ldiki, bu noqulaylik tobora kuchayib bordi va aniq og'riq bo'lmasa ham, biqinida doimiy og'irlik hissi va asabiy fe'lga aylandi. Tobora o'sib borayotgan bu asabiy fe'l oxir-oqibat Golovinlar xonadonida hukm surgan yoqimli yengillik va odobni buza boshladi. Er-xotin o'rtasidagi janjallar tobora tez-tez bo'la boshladi va tez orada hayotning butun yengilligi va yoqimliligi yo'qoldi, faqat odob zo'rg'a saqlanardi. Sahnalar yana tez-tezlashdi. Yana nizolar dengizida faqat orollar — ularning ham ozgina — qoldi, u yerda er-xotin portlashsiz uchrasha olishardi. Va Praskovya Fyodorovna endi asossiz emas, erining fe'li og'ir, derdi. O'ziga xos mubolag'a bilan u, erining fe'li doim shunday dahshatli bo'lgan, unga yigirma yil chidash uchun butun yumshoqligi kerak bo'lgan, derdi. Rost, endi janjallarni u boshlardi. Uning jahl portlashlari doim tushlikdan oldin, ko'pincha esa aynan ovqatlana boshlaganda, sho'rva ustida boshlanardi. U qaysidir idishning lab-chetida darz borligini, yoki ovqat mazasiz ekanini, yoki o'g'li tirsagini stolga qo'yganini, yoki qizining sochi u xohlaganidek turmaganini payqardi. Va nima bo'lmasin, aybni Praskovya Fyodorovnaga qo'yardi. Praskovya Fyodorovna avvaliga xuddi shu ohangda javob qaytarar va unga har xil yomon gaplarni aytardi; lekin ikki marta, aynan tushlik boshlanishida, u shunday g'azabga tushdiki, ayol buning sababi jismoniy buzilish ekanini va bu ovqat yeyish bilan qo'zg'alishini payqadi va o'zini tutdi; u javob bermadi, shunchaki tushlikni tezroq tugatishga shoshildi. Praskovya Fyodorovna o'zini tutgani uchun o'zini juda maqtardi. Eri dahshatli fe'lli va uning hayotini azobga aylantirgan, degan qarorga kelib, u o'ziga achina boshladi. Va o'ziga qanchalik achinsa, erini shunchalik yomon ko'rardi. U erining o'limini tilay boshladi; lekin tilay olmasdi ham, chunki unda daromad bo'lmay qolardi. Bu esa uni eriga qarshi yanada g'azablantirardi. U o'zini dahshatli baxtsiz deb hisoblardi, aynan erining o'limi ham uni qutqara olmasligi uchun; u jahli chiqar va buni yashirardi, uning bu yashirin jahli esa erining asabiyligini oshirardi.

paras.en: After one violent scene, in which Ivan Ilyitch had been particularly unjust, and after which he had said in explanation that he certainly was irritable, but that it was due to illness, she said that if he were ill he ought to take steps, and insisted on his going to see a celebrated doctor.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich ayniqsa adolatsiz bo'lgan bir qattiq sahnadan keyin, u izoh berib, albatta, asabiyman, lekin bu kasallikdan, deganidan so'ng, xotini agar kasal bo'lsa, chora ko'rishi kerakligini aytdi va uning mashhur doktorga borishini talab qildi.

paras.en: He went. Everything was as he had expected; everything was as it always is. The waiting and the assumption of dignity, that professional dignity he knew so well, exactly as he assumed it himself in court, and the sounding and listening and questions that called for answers that were foregone conclusions and obviously superfluous, and the significant air that seemed to insinuate⁠—you only leave it all to us, and we will arrange everything, for us it is certain and incontestable how to arrange everything, everything in one way for every man of every sort. It was all exactly as in his court of justice. Exactly the same air as he put on in dealing with a man brought up for judgment, the doctor put on for him.
paras.uz: U bordi. Hammasi u kutganidek edi; hammasi doim qanday bo'lsa, shunday edi. Kutish va o'zini salobatli tutish — u o'zi sudda xuddi shunday tutadigan, unga juda tanish bo'lgan kasbiy salobat; tukillatib, quloq solib tekshirish; javoblari oldindan ma'lum va aniq ortiqcha bo'lgan savollar; va go'yo: «Hammasini bizga topshiring, biz hammasini hal qilamiz, biz uchun hammasini qanday hal qilish aniq va shubhasiz, har qanday odam uchun hammasi bir xil yo'l bilan», deb shama qilayotgandek ma'noli qiyofa. Hammasi xuddi uning sudidagidek edi. U sudlanuvchi bilan ish ko'rganda qanday qiyofa olsa, doktor ham uning oldida aynan shunday qiyofa oldi.

paras.en: The doctor said: This and that proves that you have such-and-such a thing wrong inside you; but if that is not confirmed by analysis of this and that, then we must assume this and that. If we assume this and that, then⁠—and so on. To Ivan Ilyitch there was only one question of consequence, Was his condition dangerous or not? But the doctor ignored that irrelevant inquiry. From the doctor’s point of view this was a side issue, not the subject under consideration; the only real question was the balance of probabilities between a loose kidney, chronic catarrh, and appendicitis. It was not a question of the life of Ivan Ilyitch, but the question between the loose kidney and the intestinal appendix. And this question, as it seemed to Ivan Ilyitch, the doctor solved in a brilliant manner in favour of the appendix, with the reservation that analysis of the water might give a fresh clue, and that then the aspect of the case would be altered. All this was point for point identical with what Ivan Ilyitch had himself done in brilliant fashion a thousand times over in dealing with some man on his trial. Just as brilliantly the doctor made his summing-up, and triumphantly, gaily even, glanced over his spectacles at the prisoner in the dock. From the doctor’s summing-up Ivan Ilyitch deduced the conclusion⁠—that things looked bad, and that he, the doctor, and most likely everyone else, did not care, but that things looked bad for him. And this conclusion impressed Ivan Ilyitch morbidly, arousing in him a great feeling of pity for himself, of great anger against this doctor who could be unconcerned about a matter of such importance.
paras.uz: Doktor dedi: falon-falon narsa sizning ichingizda falon narsa buzilganini ko'rsatadi; lekin agar bu falon-falon tahlil bilan tasdiqlanmasa, unda falon-falonni taxmin qilishimiz kerak. Agar falon-falonni taxmin qilsak, unda — va hokazo. Ivan Ilich uchun faqat bitta muhim savol bor edi: uning ahvoli xavflimi yoki yo'qmi? Lekin doktor bu o'rinsiz savolga e'tibor bermadi. Doktorning nuqtai nazaridan bu ikkinchi darajali masala edi, ko'rib chiqilayotgan mavzu emas; yagona haqiqiy savol — daydi buyrak, surunkali katar va ko'richak o'rtasidagi ehtimollar muvozanati edi. Gap Ivan Ilichning hayoti haqida emas, daydi buyrak bilan ichak o'simtasi o'rtasidagi masala haqida edi. Va bu masalani, Ivan Ilichga tuyulishicha, doktor porloq tarzda ko'richak foydasiga hal qildi, faqat siydik tahlili yangi dalil berishi va unda ishning ko'rinishi o'zgarishi mumkinligini qayd etib qo'ydi. Bularning hammasi Ivan Ilichning o'zi biror sudlanuvchi bilan ish ko'rganda ming martalab porloq tarzda qilgan narsaning nuqtama-nuqta aynan o'zi edi. Doktor ham xuddi shunday porloq tarzda xulosa chiqardi va g'olibona, hatto quvnoq holda ko'zoynagi ustidan sudlanuvchiga qarab qo'ydi. Doktorning xulosasidan Ivan Ilich shunday natija chiqardi: ishlar yomon, u — doktor, va ehtimol boshqa hamma ham bunga befarq, lekin uning uchun ishlar yomon. Va bu xulosa Ivan Ilichga og'ir ta'sir qildi: unda o'ziga nisbatan katta achinish hissini, shunday muhim masalaga befarq bo'la oladigan bu doktorga qarshi katta g'azabni uyg'otdi.

paras.en: But he said nothing of that. He got up, and, laying the fee on the table, he said, with a sigh, “We sick people probably often ask inconvenient questions. Tell me, is this generally a dangerous illness or not?”
paras.uz: Lekin u bu haqda hech narsa demadi. U o'rnidan turdi va haqni stolga qo'yib, xo'rsinib dedi: — Biz kasallar, ehtimol, tez-tez noqulay savollar beramiz. Ayting-chi, umuman bu xavfli kasallikmi yoki yo'qmi?

paras.en: The doctor glanced severely at him with one eye through his spectacles, as though to say: “Prisoner at the bar, if you will not keep within the limits of the questions allowed you, I shall be compelled to take measures for your removal from the precincts of the court.” “I have told you what I thought necessary and suitable already,” said the doctor; “the analysis will show anything further.” And the doctor bowed him out.
paras.uz: Doktor unga ko'zoynagi orqali bir ko'zi bilan qattiq qaradi, go'yo: «Sudlanuvchi, agar sizga ruxsat etilgan savollar doirasidan chiqmasangiz, sizni sud zalidan chiqarish choralarini ko'rishga majbur bo'laman», demoqchidek. — Men sizga zarur va o'rinli deb bilgan narsani aytdim, — dedi doktor, — qolganini tahlil ko'rsatadi. — Va doktor ta'zim qilib, uni kuzatib qo'ydi.

paras.en: Ivan Ilyitch went out slowly and dejectedly, got into his sledge, and drove home. All the way home he was incessantly going over all the doctor had said, trying to translate all these complicated, obscure, scientific phrases into simple language, and to read in them an answer to the question. It’s bad⁠—is it very bad, or nothing much as yet? And it seemed to him that the upshot of all the doctor had said was that it was very bad. Everything seemed dismal to Ivan Ilyitch in the streets. The sledge-drivers were dismal, the houses were dismal, the people passing, and the shops were dismal. This ache, this dull gnawing ache, that never ceased for a second, seemed, when connected with the doctor’s obscure utterances, to have gained a new, more serious significance. With a new sense of misery Ivan Ilyitch kept watch on it now.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich sekin va ma'yus chiqdi, chanasiga o'tirdi va uyiga jo'nadi. Butun yo'l davomida u doktor aytgan hamma narsani tinimsiz ko'z oldidan o'tkazar, bu murakkab, mavhum, ilmiy iboralarning hammasini oddiy tilga o'girishga va ularda savolga javob o'qishga urinardi: yomon — juda yomonmi yoki hozircha unchalik emasmi? Va unga doktor aytgan barcha gaplarning mag'zi — juda yomon degani bo'lib tuyuldi. Ko'chalarda Ivan Ilichga hamma narsa g'amgin ko'rindi. Izvoshchilar g'amgin edi, uylar g'amgin edi, o'tkinchilar va do'konlar g'amgin edi. Bu og'riq, bir soniya ham to'xtamaydigan bu xira, kemiruvchi og'riq doktorning mavhum gaplari bilan bog'langanda yangi, jiddiyroq ma'no kasb etgandek tuyuldi. Ivan Ilich endi uni yangi bir iztirob hissi bilan kuzatib borardi.

paras.en: He reached home and began to tell his wife about it. His wife listened; but in the middle of his account his daughter came in with her hat on, ready to go out with her mother. Reluctantly she half sat down to listen to these tedious details, but she could not stand it for long, and her mother did not hear his story to the end.
paras.uz: U uyga yetib keldi va xotiniga bu haqda gapira boshladi. Xotini tingladi; lekin uning hikoyasining o'rtasida qizi shlyapasini kiyib, onasi bilan chiqishga tayyor holda kirdi. U istamaygina bu zerikarli tafsilotlarni tinglash uchun yarim o'tirdi, lekin uzoq chiday olmadi, onasi esa uning hikoyasini oxirigacha eshitmadi.

paras.en: “Well, I’m very glad,” said his wife; “now you must be sure and take the medicine regularly. Give me the prescription; I’ll send Gerasim to the chemist’s!” And she went to get ready to go out.
paras.uz: — Xo'sh, juda xursandman, — dedi xotini, — endi dorini muntazam ichishni unutmang. Retseptni bering; Gerasimni dorixonaga yuboraman! — Va u chiqishga tayyorlanish uchun ketdi.

paras.en: He had not taken breath while she was in the room, and he heaved a deep sigh when she was gone.
paras.uz: U xonada bo'lganida Ivan Ilich nafas ham olmagan edi, u chiqib ketgach, chuqur xo'rsindi.

paras.en: “Well,” he said, “maybe it really is nothing as yet.”
paras.uz: — Xo'sh, — dedi u, — balki haqiqatan ham hozircha hech narsa emasdir.

paras.en: He began to take the medicine, to carry out the doctor’s directions, which were changed after the analysis of the water. But it was just at this point that some confusion arose, either in the analysis or in what ought to have followed from it. The doctor himself, of course, could not be blamed for it, but it turned out that things had not gone as the doctor had told him. Either he had forgotten or told a lie, or was hiding something from him.
paras.uz: U dori ichishni, doktorning siydik tahlilidan keyin o'zgartirilgan ko'rsatmalarini bajarishni boshladi. Lekin aynan shu yerda yo tahlilda, yo undan keyin kelib chiqishi kerak bo'lgan narsada qandaydir chalkashlik yuz berdi. Bunga, albatta, doktorning o'zini ayblab bo'lmasdi, lekin ishlar doktor unga aytganidek ketmagani ma'lum bo'ldi. Yo u unutgan, yo yolg'on gapirgan, yo undan nimanidir yashirayotgan edi.

paras.en: But Ivan Ilyitch still went on just as exactly carrying out the doctor’s direction, and in doing so he found comfort at first.
paras.uz: Lekin Ivan Ilich doktorning ko'rsatmasini baribir xuddi aniq bajarishda davom etdi va bunda avvaliga taskin topdi.

paras.en: From the time of his visit to the doctor Ivan Ilyitch’s principal occupation became the exact observance of the doctor’s prescriptions as regards hygiene and medicine and the careful observation of his ailment in all the functions of his organism. Ivan Ilyitch’s principal interest came to be people’s ailments and people’s health. When anything was said in his presence about sick people, about deaths and recoveries, especially in the case of an illness resembling his own, he listened, trying to conceal his excitement, asked questions, and applied what he heard to his own trouble.
paras.uz: Doktorga borgan paytidan boshlab Ivan Ilichning asosiy mashg'uloti gigiyena va dori bo'yicha doktor ko'rsatmalariga aniq rioya qilish va organizmining barcha faoliyatlarida kasalligini diqqat bilan kuzatish bo'lib qoldi. Ivan Ilichning asosiy qiziqishi odamlarning kasalliklari va odamlarning sog'lig'i bo'lib qoldi. Uning huzurida kasallar haqida, o'limlar va tuzalishlar haqida, ayniqsa o'zinikiga o'xshash kasallik haqida gap ketsa, u hayajonini yashirishga urinib tinglar, savollar berar va eshitganlarini o'z dardiga tatbiq qilardi.

paras.en: The ache did not grow less; but Ivan Ilyitch made great efforts to force himself to believe that he was better. And he succeeded in deceiving himself so long as nothing happened to disturb him. But as soon as he had a mischance, some unpleasant words with his wife, a failure in his official work, an unlucky hand at “screw,” he was at once acutely sensible of his illness. In former days he had borne with such mishaps, hoping soon to retrieve the mistake, to make a struggle, to reach success later, to have a lucky hand. But now he was cast down by every mischance and reduced to despair. He would say to himself: “Here I’m only just beginning to get better, and the medicine has begun to take effect, and now this mischance or disappointment.” And he was furious against the mischance or the people who were causing him the disappointment and killing him, and he felt that this fury was killing him, but could not check it. One would have thought that it should have been clear to him that this exasperation against circumstances and people was aggravating his disease, and that therefore he ought not to pay attention to the unpleasant incidents. But his reasoning took quite the opposite direction. He said that he needed peace, and was on the watch for everything that disturbed his peace, and at the slightest disturbance of it he flew into a rage. What made his position worse was that he read medical books and consulted doctors. He got worse so gradually that he might have deceived himself, comparing one day with another, the difference was so slight. But when he consulted the doctors, then it seemed to him that he was getting worse, and very rapidly so indeed. And in spite of this, he was continually consulting the doctors.
paras.uz: Og'riq kamaymadi; lekin Ivan Ilich o'zini yaxshilanayotganiga ishontirish uchun katta kuch sarfladi. Va uni bezovta qiladigan hech narsa yuz bermaguncha o'zini aldashga muvaffaq bo'ldi. Lekin biror omadsizlik — xotini bilan biror noxush gap, xizmat ishida muvaffaqiyatsizlik, «vint»da omadsiz qarta — yuz berishi bilanoq, u darhol kasalligini o'tkir his qilardi. Ilgari u bunday omadsizliklarga chidardi, tez orada xatoni tuzatishga, kurashishga, keyinroq muvaffaqiyatga erishishga, omadli qarta tushishiga umid qilardi. Lekin endi har bir omadsizlik uni yiqitar va umidsizlikka solardi. U o'ziga derdi: «Mana, endigina tuzala boshlagan edim, dori ham ta'sir qila boshlagan edi, endi mana bu omadsizlik yoki ko'ngil qolishi.» Va u omadsizlikka yoki unga ko'ngil qolishini keltirib, uni o'ldirayotgan odamlarga qarshi g'azablanardi va bu g'azab uni o'ldirayotganini his qilardi, lekin uni to'xtata olmasdi. Vaziyat va odamlarga qarshi bu g'azab kasalligini og'irlashtirayotgani va shuning uchun noxush voqealarga e'tibor bermasligi kerakligi unga ravshan bo'lishi kerak edi, deb o'ylash mumkin edi. Lekin uning mulohazasi butunlay teskari yo'nalishni oldi. U o'ziga tinchlik kerakligini aytardi va tinchligini buzadigan hamma narsani poylardi, uning eng kichik buzilishida ham g'azabga tushardi. Uning ahvolini yanada og'irlashtirgan narsa — tibbiy kitoblar o'qishi va doktorlar bilan maslahatlashishi edi. U shunchalik asta-sekin yomonlashdiki, bir kunni ikkinchisi bilan solishtirib, o'zini aldashi mumkin edi — farq shunchalik kichik edi. Lekin doktorlar bilan maslahatlashganida, unga yomonlashayotgandek, haqiqatan ham juda tez yomonlashayotgandek tuyulardi. Shunga qaramay, u doktorlar bilan tinimsiz maslahatlashardi.

paras.en: That month he called on another celebrated doctor. The second celebrity said almost the same as the first, but put his questions differently; and the interview with this celebrity only redoubled the doubts and terrors of Ivan Ilyitch. A friend of a friend of his, a very good doctor, diagnosed the disease quite differently; and in spite of the fact that he guaranteed recovery, by his questions and his suppositions he confused Ivan Ilyitch even more and strengthened his suspicions. A homoeopath gave yet another diagnosis of the complaint, and prescribed medicine, which Ivan Ilyitch took secretly for a week; but after a week of the homoeopathic medicine he felt no relief, and losing faith both in the other doctor’s treatment and in this, he fell into even deeper depression. One day a lady of his acquaintance talked to him of the healing wrought by the holy pictures. Ivan Ilyitch caught himself listening attentively and believing in the reality of the facts alleged. This incident alarmed him. “Can I have degenerated to such a point of intellectual feebleness?” he said to himself. “Nonsense! it’s all rubbish. I must not give way to nervous fears, but fixing on one doctor, adhere strictly to his treatment. That’s what I will do. Now it’s settled. I won’t think about it, but till next summer I will stick to the treatment, and then I shall see. Now I’ll put a stop to this wavering!” It was easy to say this, but impossible to carry it out. The pain in his side was always dragging at him, seeming to grow more acute and ever more incessant; it seemed to him that the taste in his mouth was queerer, and there was a loathsome smell even from his breath, and his appetite and strength kept dwindling. There was no deceiving himself; something terrible, new, and so important that nothing more important had ever been in Ivan Ilyitch’s life, was taking place in him, and he alone knew of it. All about him did not or would not understand, and believed that everything in the world was going on as before. This was what tortured Ivan Ilyitch more than anything. Those of his own household, most of all his wife and daughter, who were absorbed in a perfect whirl of visits, did not, he saw, comprehend it at all, and were annoyed that he was so depressed and exacting, as though he were to blame for it. Though they tried indeed to disguise it, he saw he was a nuisance to them; but that his wife had taken up a definite line of her own in regard to his illness, and stuck to it regardless of what he might say and do. This line was expressed thus: “You know,” she would say to acquaintances, “Ivan Ilyitch cannot, like all other simple-hearted folks, keep to the treatment prescribed him. One day he’ll take his drops and eat what he’s ordered, and go to bed in good time; the next day, if I don’t see to it, he’ll suddenly forget to take his medicine, eat sturgeon (which is forbidden by the doctors), yes, and sit up at ‘screw’ till past midnight.”
paras.uz: O'sha oyda u boshqa bir mashhur doktorga bordi. Ikkinchi mashhur doktor ham deyarli birinchisi aytgan narsani aytdi, lekin savollarini boshqacha qo'ydi; bu mashhur doktor bilan suhbat esa Ivan Ilichning shubha va qo'rquvlarini faqat ikki baravar oshirdi. Do'stining do'sti, juda yaxshi doktor, kasallikni butunlay boshqacha aniqladi; va tuzalishga kafolat berganiga qaramay, savollari va taxminlari bilan Ivan Ilichni yanada chalkashtirdi va shubhalarini kuchaytirdi. Gomeopat kasallikka yana boshqa tashxis qo'ydi va dori yozib berdi, Ivan Ilich uni bir hafta yashirincha ichdi; lekin gomeopatik dorining bir haftasidan keyin hech qanday yengillik sezmadi va ham boshqa doktorning davosiga, ham bunisiga ishonchini yo'qotib, yanada chuqurroq tushkunlikka tushdi. Bir kuni tanish bir xonim unga ikonalar orqali bo'lgan shifolar haqida gapirib berdi. Ivan Ilich o'zini diqqat bilan tinglayotganini va aytilgan faktlarning haqiqatligiga ishonayotganini sezib qoldi. Bu voqea uni xavotirga soldi. «Nahotki men aqlan shunchalik zaiflashib qolgan bo'lsam? — dedi u o'ziga. — Bema'nilik! Hammasi safsata. Asabiy qo'rquvlarga berilmasligim kerak, bitta doktorni tanlab, uning davosiga qat'iy amal qilishim kerak. Shunday qilaman. Endi hal bo'ldi. Bu haqda o'ylamayman, lekin kelasi yozgacha davoga amal qilaman, keyin ko'ramiz. Endi bu ikkilanishlarga chek qo'yaman!» Buni aytish oson edi, lekin bajarish imkonsiz edi. Biqinidagi og'riq uni doim tortib turardi, tobora o'tkirlashib, tobora uzluksiz bo'lib borayotgandek tuyulardi; og'zidagi ta'm g'alatiroq bo'lgandek, hatto nafasidan ham jirkanch hid kelayotgandek tuyulardi, ishtahasi va kuchi esa kamayib borardi. O'zini aldab bo'lmasdi: uning ichida dahshatli, yangi va shunchalik muhim narsa sodir bo'layotgan ediki, Ivan Ilichning hayotida bundan muhimroq narsa hech qachon bo'lmagan edi, va bu haqda faqat uning o'zi bilardi. Atrofidagilarning hammasi tushunmas yoki tushunishni istamas va dunyoda hamma narsa avvalgidek davom etyapti, deb ishonardi. Ivan Ilichni hammasidan ko'proq aynan shu qiynardi. O'z uyidagilar, ayniqsa mehmondorchiliklarning to'liq girdobiga sho'ng'ib ketgan xotini va qizi buni umuman tushunmasligini va u shunchalik tushkun va talabchan bo'lgani uchun, go'yo bunga u aybdordek, achchiqlanishlarini ko'rardi. Garchi ular buni yashirishga urinishsa ham, u ularga xalaqit berayotganini ko'rardi; xotini esa uning kasalligiga nisbatan o'zining aniq yo'lini tanlab olgan va u nima demasin, nima qilmasin, shu yo'lda turib olgan edi. Bu yo'l shunday ifodalanardi: — Bilasizmi, — derdi u tanishlariga, — Ivan Ilich boshqa barcha soddadil odamlar kabi unga yozilgan davoga amal qila olmaydi. Bir kuni tomchilarini ichadi, buyurilgan narsani yeydi va o'z vaqtida yotadi; ertasi kuni, agar men qarab turmasam, birdan dori ichishni unutadi, osyotr baliq yeydi (doktorlar buni taqiqlagan), ha, yana yarim tundan keyingacha «vint» o'ynab o'tiradi.

paras.en: “Why, when did I do that?” Ivan Ilyitch asked in vexation one day at Pyotr Ivanovitch’s.
paras.uz: — Qachon shunday qildim? — so'radi Ivan Ilich bir kuni Pyotr Ivanovichnikida achchiqlanib.

paras.en: “Why, yesterday, with Shebek.”
paras.uz: — Kecha-ku, Shebek bilan.

paras.en: “It makes no difference. I couldn’t sleep for pain.”
paras.uz: — Farqi yo'q. Og'riqdan uxlay olmadim.

paras.en: “Well, it doesn’t matter what you do it for, only you’ll never get well like that, and you make us wretched.”
paras.uz: — Xo'sh, nima uchun qilishingizning ahamiyati yo'q, faqat bunday qilsangiz hech qachon tuzalmaysiz, bizni ham baxtsiz qilasiz.

paras.en: Praskovya Fyodorovna’s external attitude to her husband’s illness, openly expressed to others and to himself, was that Ivan Ilyitch was to blame in the matter of his illness, and that the whole illness was another injury he was doing to his wife. Ivan Ilyitch felt that the expression of this dropped from her unconsciously, but that made it no easier for him.
paras.uz: Praskovya Fyodorovnaning erining kasalligiga tashqi munosabati, boshqalarga ham, unga ham ochiq bildirilgani — kasalligi masalasida Ivan Ilich aybdor va butun kasallik u xotiniga qilayotgan navbatdagi ozor, degan munosabat edi. Ivan Ilich buning ifodasi xotinidan beixtiyor chiqayotganini his qilardi, lekin bu unga yengillik bermasdi.

paras.en: In his official life, too, Ivan Ilyitch noticed, or fancied he noticed, a strange attitude to him. At one time it seemed to him that people were looking inquisitively at him, as a man who would shortly have to vacate his position; at another time his friends would suddenly begin chaffing him in a friendly way over his nervous fears, as though that awful and horrible, unheard-of thing that was going on within him, incessantly gnawing at him, and irresistibly dragging him away somewhere, were the most agreeable subject for joking. Shvarts especially, with his jocoseness, his liveliness, and his comme-il-faut tone, exasperated Ivan Ilyitch by reminding him of himself ten years ago.
paras.uz: Xizmat hayotida ham Ivan Ilich o'ziga nisbatan g'alati munosabatni payqardi yoki payqagandek bo'lardi. Goh unga odamlar unga tez orada lavozimini bo'shatishi kerak bo'lgan odamga qaragandek qiziqish bilan qarayotgandek tuyulardi; goh do'stlari birdan uning asabiy qo'rquvlari ustidan do'stona hazil qila boshlashardi, go'yo uning ichida sodir bo'layotgan, tinimsiz uni kemirayotgan va uni chidab bo'lmas tarzda qayergadir sudrayotgan o'sha dahshatli va qo'rqinchli, misli ko'rilmagan narsa hazil uchun eng yoqimli mavzudek. Ayniqsa Shvarts o'zining hazilkashligi, jonliligi va comme il faut ohangi bilan Ivan Ilichga o'n yil oldingi o'zini eslatib, uning jahlini chiqarardi.

paras.en: Friends came sometimes to play cards. They sat down to the card-table; they shuffled and dealt the new cards. Diamonds were led and followed by diamonds, the seven. His partner said, “Can’t trump,” and played the two of diamonds. What then? Why, delightful, capital, it should have been⁠—he had a trump hand. And suddenly Ivan Ilyitch feels that gnawing ache, that taste in his mouth, and it strikes him as something grotesque that with that he could be glad of a trump hand.
paras.uz: Do'stlar ba'zan qarta o'ynash uchun kelishardi. Ular qarta stoliga o'tirishdi; yangi qartalarni aralashtirib, tarqatishdi. G'isht yurildi, g'isht bilan, yettilik bilan javob berildi. Sherigi: «Kozirim yo'q», dedi va g'ishtning ikkiligini tashladi. Xo'sh, keyin-chi? Axir bu ajoyib, zo'r bo'lishi kerak edi — uning qo'lida kozirlar to'la edi. Va birdan Ivan Ilich o'sha kemiruvchi og'riqni, og'zidagi o'sha ta'mni his qiladi va shu holatda kozirli qartaga xursand bo'la olishi unga qandaydir bema'ni narsa bo'lib tuyuladi.

paras.en: He looks at Mihail Mihailovitch, his partner, how he taps on the table with his red hand, and affably and indulgently abstains from snatching up the trick, and pushes the cards towards Ivan Ilyitch so as to give him the pleasure of taking them up, without any trouble, without even stretching out his hand. “What, does he suppose that I’m so weak that I can’t stretch out my hand?” thinks Ivan Ilyitch, and he forgets the trumps, and trumps his partner’s cards, and plays his trump hand without making three tricks; and what’s the most awful thing of all is that he sees how upset Mihail Mihailovitch is about it, while he doesn’t care a bit, and it’s awful for him to think why he doesn’t care.
paras.uz: U sherigi Mixail Mixaylovichga qaraydi: u qizil qo'li bilan stolni qanday chertayotganini, xushmuomalalik va iltifot bilan qo'lni olishdan o'zini tiyib, qartalarni Ivan Ilichga qarab surayotganini — unga hech qanday qiyinchiliksiz, hatto qo'lini cho'zmasdan ularni olish zavqini berish uchun. «Nima, u meni qo'limni cho'za olmaydigan darajada zaif deb o'ylaydimi?» deb o'ylaydi Ivan Ilich va kozirlarni unutib, sherigining qartasini kozir bilan uradi va qo'lidagi kozirlar bilan uchta qo'l ham ololmay o'ynaydi; eng dahshatlisi esa — u Mixail Mixaylovich bundan qanchalik xafa bo'lganini ko'radi, o'zi esa zarracha parvo qilmaydi va nega parvo qilmasligini o'ylash unga dahshatli.

paras.en: They all see that he’s in pain, and say to him, “We can stop if you’re tired. You go and lie down.” Lie down? No, he’s not in the least tired; they will play the rubber. All are gloomy and silent. Ivan Ilyitch feels that it is he who has brought this gloom upon them, and he cannot disperse it. They have supper, and the party breaks up, and Ivan Ilyitch is left alone with the consciousness that his life is poisoned for him and poisons the life of others, and that this poison is not losing its force, but is continually penetrating more and more deeply into his whole existence.
paras.uz: Hammasi uning og'riq chekayotganini ko'radi va unga: «Charchagan bo'lsangiz, to'xtatishimiz mumkin. Borib yoting», deyishadi. Yotish? Yo'q, u zarracha charchagan emas; ular robberni tugatishadi. Hammasi ma'yus va jim. Ivan Ilich bu ma'yuslikni ularga o'zi olib kelganini his qiladi va uni tarqata olmaydi. Ular kechki ovqatni yeyishadi, mehmonlar tarqaladi va Ivan Ilich hayoti o'zi uchun zaharlanganini va boshqalarning hayotini zaharlayotganini, bu zahar kuchini yo'qotmayotganini, balki uning butun borlig'iga tobora chuqurroq singib borayotganini anglash bilan yolg'iz qoladi.

paras.en: And with the consciousness of this, and with the physical pain in addition, and the terror in addition to that, he must lie in his bed, often not able to sleep for pain the greater part of the night; and in the morning he must get up again, dress, go to the law-court, speak, write, or, if he does not go out, stay at home for all the four-and-twenty hours of the day and night, of which each one is a torture. And he had to live thus on the edge of the precipice alone, without one man who would understand and feel for him.
paras.uz: Va buni anglash bilan, ustiga jismoniy og'riq bilan, uning ustiga dahshat bilan u to'shagida yotishi, ko'pincha tunning katta qismida og'riqdan uxlay olmasligi kerak; ertalab esa yana turishi, kiyinishi, sudga borishi, gapirishi, yozishi yoki, chiqmasa, sutkaning har biri azob bo'lgan yigirma to'rt soatining barchasida uyda qolishi kerak. Va u jarlik yoqasida shunday yolg'iz, uni tushunadigan va unga achinadigan birorta ham odamsiz yashashi kerak edi.

quiz.q: Why does the visit to the doctor remind Ivan Ilyitch of his own court?
o: The doctor was a former judge
The doctor treats him exactly as he treated defendants
quiz.why_uz: Doktor unga sudlanuvchiga qaragandek qaraydi.

quiz.q: What is the only question that matters to Ivan Ilyitch?
quiz.why_uz: Uning uchun yagona savol — ahvoli xavflimi.
