chapters.recap_uz: Og'zidagi g'alati ta'm va biqinidagi og'irlik kuchayadi, fe'li buziladi. Mashhur doktor uni xuddi Ivan Ilich sudda sudlanuvchini ko'rganidek ko'radi: savol «buyrakmi yoki ko'richakmi», hayot haqida emas. Doktorlar almashadi, umid va qo'rquv almashadi. Oilasi uni aybdor deb biladi; «vint» o'yinida ham og'riq uni yolg'iz qoldiradi.

chapters.title: V. Life and death

paras.en: In this way one month, then a second, passed by. Just before the New Year his brother-in-law arrived in the town on a visit to them. Ivan Ilyitch was at the court when he arrived. Praskovya Fyodorovna had gone out shopping. Coming home and going into his study, he found there his brother-in-law, a healthy, florid man, engaged in unpacking his trunk. He raised his head, hearing Ivan Ilyitch’s step, and for a second stared at him without a word. That stare told Ivan Ilyitch everything. His brother-in-law opened his mouth to utter an “Oh!” of surprise, but checked himself. That confirmed it all.
paras.uz: Shu tarzda bir oy, keyin ikkinchisi o'tdi. Yangi yil arafasida qaynog'asi ularnikiga mehmonga shaharga keldi. U kelganida Ivan Ilich sudda edi. Praskovya Fyodorovna xarid qilish uchun chiqib ketgan edi. Uyga kelib, kabinetiga kirgach, u yerda qaynog'asini — sog'lom, qizil yuzli odamni sandig'ini ochayotgan holda topdi. U Ivan Ilichning qadam tovushini eshitib, boshini ko'tardi va bir soniya indamay unga tikilib qoldi. Bu tikilish Ivan Ilichga hamma narsani aytdi. Qaynog'asi hayrat bilan «Oh!» deyish uchun og'zini ochdi, lekin o'zini tutdi. Bu hammasini tasdiqladi.

paras.en: “What! have I changed?”
paras.uz: — Nima, men o'zgarib qoldimmi?

paras.en: “Yes, there is a change.”
paras.uz: — Ha, o'zgarish bor.

paras.en: And all Ivan Ilyitch’s efforts to draw him into talking of his appearance his brother-in-law met with obstinate silence. Praskovya Fyodorovna came in; the brother-in-law went to see her. Ivan Ilyitch locked his door, and began gazing at himself in the looking-glass, first full face, then in profile. He took up his photograph, taken with his wife, and compared the portrait with what he saw in the looking-glass. The change was immense. Then he bared his arm to the elbow, looked at it, pulled the sleeve down again, sat down on an ottoman, and felt blacker than night.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich uni tashqi ko'rinishi haqida gapirishga tortish uchun qilgan barcha urinishlariga qaynog'asi qaysar sukut bilan javob berdi. Praskovya Fyodorovna kirdi; qaynog'asi uning oldiga ketdi. Ivan Ilich eshigini qulfladi va ko'zguga qaray boshladi — avval to'g'ridan, keyin yondan. U xotini bilan tushgan suratini olib, suratni ko'zguda ko'rayotgan narsa bilan solishtirdi. O'zgarish juda katta edi. Keyin qo'lini tirsagigacha yalang'ochladi, unga qaradi, yengini yana tushirdi, pufga o'tirdi va o'zini tundan ham qoraroq his qildi.

paras.en: “I mustn’t, I mustn’t,” he said to himself, jumped up, went to the table, opened some official paper, tried to read it, but could not. He opened the door, went into the drawing-room. The door into the drawing-room was closed. He went up to it on tiptoe and listened.
paras.uz: «Kerak emas, kerak emas», dedi u o'ziga, sakrab turdi, stol oldiga bordi, qandaydir rasmiy qog'ozni ochdi, o'qishga urindi, lekin o'qiy olmadi. U eshikni ochib, zalga chiqdi. Mehmonxona eshigi yopiq edi. U oyoq uchida unga yaqinlashib, quloq soldi.

paras.en: “No, you’re exaggerating,” Praskovya Fyodorovna was saying.
paras.uz: — Yo'q, sen mubolag'a qilyapsan, — derdi Praskovya Fyodorovna.

paras.en: “Exaggerating? You can’t see it. Why, he’s a dead man. Look at his eyes⁠—there’s no light in them. But what’s wrong with him?”
paras.uz: — Mubolag'a? Sen ko'rmaysan. Axir u o'lik odam. Ko'zlariga qara — ularda nur yo'q. Lekin unga nima bo'lgan o'zi?

paras.en: “No one can tell. Nikolaev” (that was another doctor) “said something, but I don’t know. Leshtchetitsky” (this was the celebrated doctor) “said the opposite.”
paras.uz: — Hech kim aniq ayta olmaydi. Nikolayev (bu boshqa doktor edi) nimadir dedi, lekin bilmayman. Leshchetitskiy (bu mashhur doktor edi) buning aksini aytdi.

paras.en: Ivan Ilyitch walked away, went to his own room, lay down, and fell to musing. “A kidney⁠—a loose kidney.” He remembered all the doctors had told him, how it had been detached, and how it was loose; and by an effort of imagination he tried to catch that kidney and to stop it, to strengthen it. So little was needed, he fancied. “No, I’ll go again to Pyotr Ivanovitch” (this was the friend who had a friend a doctor). He rang, ordered the horse to be put in, and got ready to go out.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich u yerdan uzoqlashdi, o'z xonasiga borib yotdi va o'yga cho'mdi. «Buyrak — daydi buyrak.» U doktorlar aytganlarining hammasini — buyrak qanday ajralib qolgani va qanday sayr qilib yurganini esladi; va xayol kuchi bilan o'sha buyrakni ushlab, to'xtatishga, mustahkamlashga urindi. Buning uchun juda oz narsa kerakdek tuyuldi unga. «Yo'q, yana Pyotr Ivanovichnikiga boraman» (bu doktor do'sti bor do'st edi). U qo'ng'iroq chalib, otni qo'shishni buyurdi va chiqishga tayyorlandi.

paras.en: “Where are you off to, Jean?” asked his wife with a peculiarly melancholy and exceptionally kind expression.
paras.uz: — Qayoqqa, Jean? — so'radi xotini alohida g'amgin va g'ayrioddiy mehribon ifoda bilan.

paras.en: This exceptionally kind expression exasperated him. He looked darkly at her.
paras.uz: Bu g'ayrioddiy mehribon ifoda uning jahlini chiqardi. U unga qovog'ini solib qaradi.

paras.en: “I want to see Pyotr Ivanovitch.”
paras.uz: — Pyotr Ivanovichni ko'rmoqchiman.

paras.en: He went to the friend who had a friend a doctor. And with him to the doctor’s. He found him in, and had a long conversation with him.
paras.uz: U doktor do'sti bor do'stnikiga bordi. Va u bilan birga doktornikiga. Uni uyda topdi va u bilan uzoq suhbatlashdi.

paras.en: Reviewing the anatomical and physiological details of what, according to the doctor’s view, was taking place within him, he understood it all. It was just one thing⁠—a little thing wrong with the intestinal appendix. It might all come right. Only strengthen one sluggish organ, and decrease the undue activity of another, and absorption would take place, and all would be set right. He was a little late for dinner. He ate his dinner, talked cheerfully, but it was a long while before he could go to his own room to work. At last he went to his study, and at once sat down to work. He read his legal documents and did his work, but the consciousness never left him of having a matter of importance very near to his heart which he had put off, but would look into later. When he had finished his work, he remembered that the matter near his heart was thinking about the intestinal appendix. But he did not give himself up to it; he went into the drawing-room to tea. There were visitors; and there was talking, playing on the piano, and singing; there was the young examining magistrate, the desirable match for the daughter. Ivan Ilyitch spent the evening, as Praskovya Fyodorovna observed, in better spirits than any of them; but he never forgot for an instant that he had the important matter of the intestinal appendix put off for consideration later. At eleven o’clock he said good night and went to his own room. He had slept alone since his illness in a little room adjoining his study. He went in, undressed, and took up a novel of Zola, but did not read it; he fell to thinking. And in his imagination the desired recovery of the intestinal appendix had taken place. There had been absorption, rejection, reestablishment of the regular action.
paras.uz: Doktorning fikricha, uning ichida sodir bo'layotgan narsaning anatomik va fiziologik tafsilotlarini ko'rib chiqib, u hammasini tushundi. Bu faqat bitta narsa edi — ko'richakdagi kichik bir nosozlik. Hammasi joyiga tushishi mumkin edi. Faqat bitta sust a'zoni kuchaytirish va boshqasining ortiqcha faolligini kamaytirish kerak, shunda so'rilish sodir bo'ladi va hammasi tuzaladi. U tushlikka biroz kechikdi. Tushlikni yedi, quvnoq gaplashdi, lekin ishlash uchun o'z xonasiga uzoq vaqt bora olmadi. Nihoyat kabinetiga borib, darhol ishga o'tirdi. Hujjatlarini o'qidi va ishini qildi, lekin yuragiga juda yaqin, keyinga qoldirgan, keyinroq ko'rib chiqadigan muhim ishi borligini anglash uni bir lahza ham tark etmadi. Ishini tugatgach, yuragiga yaqin ish — ko'richak haqida o'ylash ekanini esladi. Lekin unga berilmadi; choy ichish uchun mehmonxonaga chiqdi. Mehmonlar bor edi; gaplashishar, pianino chalishar va qo'shiq aytishardi; qiz uchun maqbul kuyov — yosh tergovchi ham bor edi. Praskovya Fyodorovna payqaganidek, Ivan Ilich oqshomni hammasidan ko'ra yaxshiroq kayfiyatda o'tkazdi; lekin ko'richak haqidagi muhim ishni keyinroq ko'rib chiqish uchun qoldirganini bir lahza ham unutmadi. Soat o'n birda u xayrli tun tilab, o'z xonasiga ketdi. Kasal bo'lganidan beri u kabinetiga tutash kichkina xonada yolg'iz uxlardi. U kirdi, yechindi va Zolaning romanini oldi, lekin o'qimadi; o'yga botdi. Va xayolida ko'richakning orzu qilingan tuzalishi sodir bo'ldi. So'rilish, chiqarilish, muntazam faoliyatning tiklanishi sodir bo'ldi.

paras.en: “Why, it’s all simply that,” he said to himself. “One only wants to assist nature.” He remembered the medicine, got up, took it, lay down on his back, watching for the medicine to act beneficially and overcome the pain. “It’s only to take it regularly and avoid injurious influences; why, already I feel rather better, much better.” He began to feel his side; it was not painful to the touch. “Yes, I don’t feel it⁠—really, much better already.” He put out the candle and lay on his side. “The appendix is getting better, absorption.” Suddenly he felt the familiar, old, dull, gnawing ache, persistent, quiet, in earnest. In his mouth the same familiar loathsome taste. His heart sank, his brain felt dim, misty. “My God, my God!” he said, “again, again, and it will never cease.” And suddenly the whole thing rose before him in quite a different aspect. “Intestinal appendix! kidney!” he said to himself. “It’s not a question of the appendix, not a question of the kidney, but of life and⁠ ⁠… death. Yes, life has been and now it’s going, going away, and I cannot stop it. Yes. Why deceive myself? Isn’t it obvious to everyone, except me, that I’m dying, and it’s only a question of weeks, of days⁠—at once perhaps. There was light, and now there is darkness. I was here, and now I am going! Where?” A cold chill ran over him, his breath stopped. He heard nothing but the throbbing of his heart.
paras.uz: «Axir, hammasi shunchaki shu, — dedi u o'ziga. — Faqat tabiatga yordam berish kerak.» U dorini esladi, turib uni ichdi, chalqancha yotib, dori foydali ta'sir qilib, og'riqni yengishini kuta boshladi. «Faqat muntazam ichish va zararli ta'sirlardan saqlanish kerak; mana, allaqachon biroz yaxshiroq, ancha yaxshiroq his qilyapman.» U biqinini paypaslay boshladi; ushlaganda og'rimasdi. «Ha, sezmayapman — haqiqatan ham allaqachon ancha yaxshi.» U shamni o'chirib, yonboshlab yotdi. «Ko'richak tuzalyapti, so'rilyapti.» Birdan u tanish, eski, xira, kemiruvchi og'riqni his qildi — tinimsiz, sokin, jiddiy. Og'zida o'sha tanish jirkanch ta'm. Yuragi siqildi, miyasi xiralashib, tumanlandi. «Xudoyim, Xudoyim! — dedi u. — Yana, yana, va bu hech qachon to'xtamaydi.» Va birdan butun narsa uning ko'z oldida butunlay boshqa tusda namoyon bo'ldi. «Ko'richak! Buyrak! — dedi u o'ziga. — Gap ko'richakda ham, buyrakda ham emas, balki hayot va… o'limda. Ha, hayot bor edi, endi u ketyapti, ketyapti, men esa uni to'xtata olmayman. Ha. Nega o'zimni aldayman? Mendan boshqa hammaga o'layotganim va gap faqat haftalar, kunlar — balki darhol — haqida ekani ayon emasmi? Nur bor edi, endi esa zulmat. Men shu yerda edim, endi ketyapman! Qayerga?» Uning badanidan sovuq titroq o'tdi, nafasi to'xtadi. U yuragining urishidan boshqa hech narsani eshitmasdi.

paras.en: “I shall be no more, then what will there be? There’ll be nothing. Where then shall I be when I’m no more? Can this be dying? No; I don’t want to!” He jumped up, tried to light the candle; and fumbling with trembling hands, he dropped the candle and the candlestick on the floor and fell back again on the pillow. “Why trouble? it doesn’t matter,” he said to himself, staring with open eyes into the darkness. “Death. Yes, death. And they⁠—all of them⁠—don’t understand, and don’t want to understand, and feel no pity. They are playing.” (He caught through the closed doors the faraway cadence of a voice and the accompaniment.) “They don’t care, but they will die too. Fools! Me sooner and them later; but it will be the same for them. And they are merry. The beasts!” Anger stifled him. And he was agonisingly, insufferably miserable. “It cannot be that all men always have been doomed to this awful horror! He raised himself.
paras.uz: «Men bo'lmayman, unda nima bo'ladi? Hech narsa bo'lmaydi. Men bo'lmaganimda qayerda bo'laman? Nahotki bu o'lim bo'lsa? Yo'q; men istamayman!» U sakrab turdi, shamni yoqmoqchi bo'ldi; titroq qo'llari bilan paypaslab, shamni va shamdonni polga tushirib yubordi va yana yostiqqa yiqildi. «Nima keragi bor? Baribir», dedi u o'ziga, ko'zlarini katta ochib zulmatga tikilarkan. «O'lim. Ha, o'lim. Ular esa — hammasi — tushunishmaydi, tushunishni ham istashmaydi va achinishmaydi. Ular chalishyapti.» (U yopiq eshiklar orqali uzoqdan kelayotgan ovoz va kuyni eshitdi.) «Ularga baribir, lekin ular ham o'lishadi. Ahmoqlar! Men oldinroq, ular keyinroq; lekin ular uchun ham xuddi shunday bo'ladi. Ular esa xursand. Hayvonlar!» G'azab uni bo'g'di. Va u azobli, chidab bo'lmas darajada baxtsiz edi. «Bo'lishi mumkin emas, barcha odamlar doim shu dahshatli qo'rquvga mahkum bo'lgan bo'lsa!» U o'rnidan ko'tarildi.

paras.en: “There is something wrong in it; I must be calm, I must think it all over from the beginning.” And then he began to consider. “Yes, the beginning of my illness. I knocked my side, and I was just the same, that day and the days after; it ached a little, then more, then doctors, then depression, misery, and again doctors; and I’ve gone on getting closer and closer to the abyss. Strength growing less. Nearer and nearer. And here I am, wasting away, no light in my eyes. I think of how to cure the appendix, but this is death. Can it be death?” Again a horror came over him; gasping for breath, he bent over, began feeling for the matches, and knocked his elbow against the bedside table. It was in his way and hurt him; he felt furious with it, in his anger knocked against it more violently, and upset it. And in despair, breathless, he fell back on his spine waiting for death to come that instant.
paras.uz: «Bunda nimadir noto'g'ri; tinchlanishim kerak, hammasini boshidan o'ylab chiqishim kerak.» Va u mulohaza qila boshladi. «Ha, kasalligimning boshlanishi. Biqinimni urib oldim, o'sha kuni ham, keyingi kunlarda ham xuddi avvalgidek edim; biroz og'ridi, keyin ko'proq, keyin doktorlar, keyin tushkunlik, g'am, yana doktorlar; va men jarlikka tobora yaqinlashib bordim. Kuchim kamaymoqda. Tobora yaqinroq. Mana, endi ozib-to'zib ketyapman, ko'zlarimda nur yo'q. Men ko'richakni qanday davolash haqida o'ylayman, bu esa o'lim. Nahotki bu o'lim bo'lsa?» Uni yana dahshat qamrab oldi; nafasi qaytib, u egildi, gugurtni paypaslay boshladi va tirsagini karavot yonidagi tumbochkaga urib oldi. U yo'lini to'sib, uni og'ritdi; u unga g'azablandi, jahl ustida unga yanada qattiqroq urildi va uni ag'darib yubordi. Va umidsizlikda, nafasi tiqilib, chalqancha yiqildi va o'limning shu lahzada kelishini kutdi.

paras.en: The visitors were leaving at that time. Praskovya Fyodorovna was seeing them out. She heard something fall, and came in.
paras.uz: Mehmonlar shu paytda ketishayotgan edi. Praskovya Fyodorovna ularni kuzatayotgan edi. U nimadir tushganini eshitib, kirdi.

paras.en: “What is it?”
paras.uz: — Nima bo'ldi?

paras.en: “Nothing, I dropped something by accident.”
paras.uz: — Hech narsa, tasodifan nimanidir tushirib yubordim.

paras.en: She went out, brought a candle. He was lying, breathing hard and fast, like a man who has run a mile, and staring with fixed eyes at her.
paras.uz: U chiqib, sham olib keldi. U bir verst yugurgan odamdek og'ir va tez nafas olib, unga qotib qolgan ko'zlar bilan tikilib yotardi.

paras.en: “What is it, Jean?”
paras.uz: — Nima bo'ldi, Jean?

paras.en: “No⁠—othing, I say. I dropped something.”⁠—“Why speak? She won’t understand,” he thought.
paras.uz: — Hech na-arsa, deyapman-ku. Nimanidir tushirib yubordim. — «Nega gapiraman? U tushunmaydi», deb o'yladi u.

paras.en: She certainly did not understand. She picked up the candle, lighted it for him, and went out hastily. She had to say goodbye to a departing guest. When she came back, he was lying in the same position on his back, looking upwards.
paras.uz: U haqiqatan ham tushunmadi. U shamni olib, unga yoqib berdi va shoshib chiqib ketdi. Ketayotgan mehmon bilan xayrlashishi kerak edi. U qaytib kelganida, u o'sha holatda chalqancha yotib, tepaga qarab turardi.

paras.en: “How are you⁠—worse?”
paras.uz: — Qalaysiz — yomonroqmi?

paras.en: “Yes.”
paras.uz: — Ha.

paras.en: She shook her head, sat down.
paras.uz: U boshini chayqab, o'tirdi.

paras.en: “Do you know what, Jean? I wonder if we hadn’t better send for Leshtchetitsky to see you here?”
paras.uz: — Bilasizmi, Jean? Leshchetitskiyni sizni shu yerda ko'rishga chaqirsak yaxshi bo'lmasmikan?

paras.en: This meant calling in the celebrated doctor, regardless of expense. He smiled malignantly, and said no. She sat a moment longer, went up to him, and kissed him on the forehead.
paras.uz: Bu mashhur doktorni xarajatga qaramay chaqirish degani edi. U zaharxanda jilmayib, yo'q, dedi. U yana bir lahza o'tirdi, uning oldiga borib, peshonasidan o'pdi.

paras.en: He hated her with all the force of his soul when she was kissing him, and had to make an effort not to push her away.
paras.uz: U o'payotganida, u uni butun qalbi bilan yomon ko'rdi va uni itarib yubormaslik uchun o'zini zo'rg'a tutdi.

paras.en: “Good night. Please God, you’ll sleep.”
paras.uz: — Xayrli tun. Xudo xohlasa, uxlaysiz.

paras.en: “Yes.”
paras.uz: — Ha.

quiz.why_uz: Qaynog'asining tikilishi hammasini aytdi.

chapters.recap_uz: Qaynog'asi uni ko'rib, «o'lik odam» deydi. Ivan Ilich hali ham buyrak va ko'richak haqida o'ylashga urinadi, lekin tunda birdan tushunadi: gap a'zolarda emas, hayot va o'limda. «Nur bor edi, endi zulmat.» U yolg'iz qo'rquvda yotadi, mehmonxonadan musiqa eshitiladi.

chapters.title: VI. Caius is mortal

paras.en: Ivan Ilyitch saw that he was dying, and was in continual despair.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich o'layotganini ko'rardi va doimiy umidsizlikda edi.

paras.en: At the bottom of his heart Ivan Ilyitch knew that he was dying; but so far from growing used to this idea, he simply did not grasp it⁠—he was utterly unable to grasp it.
paras.uz: Yuragining tubida Ivan Ilich o'layotganini bilardi; lekin bu fikrga ko'nikish u yoqda tursin, uni shunchaki anglamasdi — uni anglashga mutlaqo qodir emas edi.

paras.en: The example of the syllogism that he had learned in Kiseveter’s logic⁠—Caius is a man, men are mortal, therefore Caius is mortal⁠—had seemed to him all his life correct only as regards Caius, but not at all as regards himself. In that case it was a question of Caius, a man, an abstract man, and it was perfectly true, but he was not Caius, and was not an abstract man; he had always been a creature quite, quite different from all others; he had been little Vanya with a mamma and papa, and Mitya and Volodya, with playthings and a coachman and a nurse; afterwards with Katenka, with all the joys and griefs and ecstasies of childhood, boyhood, and youth. What did Caius know of the smell of the leathern ball Vanya had been so fond of? Had Caius kissed his mother’s hand like that? Caius had not heard the silk rustle of his mother’s skirts. He had not made a riot at school over the pudding. Had Caius been in love like that? Could Caius preside over the sittings of the court?
paras.uz: Kizeveterning mantiq kitobidan o'rgangan sillogizm misoli — Kay inson, insonlar o'lar, demak Kay o'lar — butun umri davomida unga faqat Kayga nisbatan to'g'ri, o'ziga nisbatan esa umuman to'g'ri emasdek tuyulgan edi. U yerda gap Kay haqida, inson haqida, mavhum inson haqida edi va bu mutlaqo to'g'ri edi, lekin u Kay emas edi, mavhum inson ham emas edi; u doim boshqa hammadan butunlay, butunlay farq qiladigan mavjudot bo'lgan; u onasi va dadasi, Mitya va Volodya bo'lgan, o'yinchoqlari, aravakashi va enagasi bo'lgan kichkina Vanya edi; keyin Katenka bilan, bolalik, o'smirlik va yoshlikning barcha quvonch, qayg'u va zavqlari bilan. Vanya juda yaxshi ko'rgan charm to'pning hidini Kay qayerdan bilsin? Kay onasining qo'lini shunday o'pganmidi? Kay onasining ko'ylagi ipagining shitirlashini eshitmagan. U maktabda pirog uchun to'polon ko'tarmagan. Kay shunday sevganmidi? Kay sud majlislariga raislik qila olarmidi?

paras.en: And Caius certainly was mortal, and it was right for him to die; but for me, little Vanya, Ivan Ilyitch, with all my feelings and ideas⁠—for me it’s a different matter. And it cannot be that I ought to die. That would be too awful.
paras.uz: Kay, albatta, o'ladigan edi va uning o'lishi to'g'ri edi; lekin men uchun, kichkina Vanya, Ivan Ilich uchun, barcha his-tuyg'ularim va fikrlarim bilan — men uchun bu boshqa masala. Va men o'lishim kerak, degani bo'lishi mumkin emas. Bu juda dahshatli bo'lardi.

paras.en: That was his feeling.
paras.uz: Uning his qilgani shu edi.

paras.en: “If I had to die like Caius, I should have known it was so, some inner voice would have told me so. But there was nothing of the sort in me. And I and all my friends, we felt that it was not at all the same as with Caius. And now here it is!” he said to himself. “It can’t be! It can’t be, but it is! How is it? How’s one to understand it?” And he could not conceive it, and tried to drive away this idea as false, incorrect, and morbid, and to supplant it by other, correct, healthy ideas. But this idea, not as an idea merely, but as it were an actual fact, came back again and stood confronting him.
paras.uz: «Agar men Kay kabi o'lishim kerak bo'lganida, buni bilgan bo'lardim, qandaydir ichki ovoz menga buni aytgan bo'lardi. Lekin menda bunday hech narsa yo'q edi. Men ham, do'stlarimning hammasi ham, bu Kaydagidek umuman emasligini his qilardik. Endi esa mana!» dedi u o'ziga. «Bo'lishi mumkin emas! Bo'lishi mumkin emas, lekin bor! Bu qanday? Buni qanday tushunish kerak?» Va u buni tasavvur qila olmasdi va bu fikrni yolg'on, noto'g'ri va kasalvand deb haydashga, uning o'rniga boshqa, to'g'ri, sog'lom fikrlarni qo'yishga urinardi. Lekin bu fikr shunchaki fikr sifatida emas, go'yo haqiqiy fakt sifatida yana qaytib kelar va uning ro'parasida turib olardi.

paras.en: And to replace this thought he called up other thoughts, one after another, in the hope of finding support in them. He tried to get back into former trains of thought, which in old days had screened off the thought of death. But, strange to say, all that had in old days covered up, obliterated the sense of death, could not now produce the same effect. Latterly, Ivan Ilyitch spent the greater part of his time in these efforts to restore his old trains of thought which had shut off death. At one time he would say to himself, “I’ll put myself into my official work; why, I used to live in it.” And he would go to the law-courts, banishing every doubt. He would enter into conversation with his colleagues, and would sit carelessly, as his old habit was, scanning the crowd below dreamily, and with both his wasted hands he would lean on the arms of the oak armchair just as he always did; and bending over to a colleague, pass the papers to him and whisper to him, then suddenly dropping his eyes and sitting up straight, he would pronounce the familiar words that opened the proceedings. But suddenly in the middle, the pain in his side, utterly regardless of the stage he had reached in his conduct of the case, began its work. It riveted Ivan Ilyitch’s attention. He drove away the thought of it, but it still did its work, and then It came and stood confronting him and looked at him, and he felt turned to stone, and the light died away in his eyes, and he began to ask himself again, “Can it be that It is the only truth?” And his colleagues and his subordinates saw with surprise and distress that he, the brilliant, subtle judge, was losing the thread of his speech, was making blunders. He shook himself, tried to regain his self-control, and got somehow to the end of the sitting, and went home with the painful sense that his judicial labours could not as of old hide from him what he wanted to hide; that he could not by means of his official work escape from It. And the worst of it was that It drew him to itself not for him to do anything in particular, but simply for him to look at It straight in the face, to look at It and, doing nothing, suffer unspeakably.
paras.uz: Va bu fikrning o'rniga u ulardan tayanch topish umidida boshqa fikrlarni birin-ketin chaqirardi. U ilgari o'lim haqidagi fikrni to'sib turgan avvalgi fikr yo'nalishlariga qaytishga urinardi. Lekin, g'alati, ilgari o'lim hissini yopib qo'ygan, o'chirib tashlagan hamma narsa endi xuddi shunday ta'sir qila olmasdi. So'nggi paytlarda Ivan Ilich vaqtining katta qismini o'limni to'sib turgan eski fikr yo'nalishlarini tiklashga qaratilgan shu urinishlarga sarflardi. Goh u o'ziga derdi: «Xizmat ishiga sho'ng'iyman; axir men unda yashardim-ku.» Va u har qanday shubhani haydab, sudga borardi. Hamkasblari bilan suhbatga kirishar, eski odatiga ko'ra beparvo o'tirib, pastdagi olomonga xayolchan ko'z yugurtirar va ozib ketgan ikki qo'li bilan, doim qilganidek, eman kreslosining suyanchiqlariga suyanardi; va hamkasbi tomon egilib, qog'ozlarni unga uzatib, unga pichirlar, keyin birdan ko'zlarini tushirib, qaddini rostlab, ish yuritishni ochadigan tanish so'zlarni aytardi. Lekin birdan o'rtada biqinidagi og'riq, ishni yuritishda qaysi bosqichga yetganiga mutlaqo parvo qilmay, o'z ishini boshlardi. U Ivan Ilichning diqqatini o'ziga mixlab qo'yardi. U bu haqdagi fikrni haydardi, lekin og'riq baribir o'z ishini qilardi, keyin U kelib, uning ro'parasida turib, unga qarardi; u esa toshga aylangandek bo'lar, ko'zlaridagi nur so'nar va yana o'zidan so'ray boshlardi: «Nahotki faqat U yagona haqiqat bo'lsa?» Hamkasblari va qo'l ostidagilar esa uning — porloq, nozik fikrli sudyaning nutqi ipini yo'qotayotganini, xatolar qilayotganini hayrat va iztirob bilan ko'rishardi. U silkinib, o'zini qo'lga olishga urinar, majlisni qandaydir oxiriga yetkazar va sudlik mehnati endi avvalgidek u yashirmoqchi bo'lgan narsani undan yashira olmasligini, xizmat ishi orqali Undan qochib qutula olmasligini og'riqli anglagan holda uyga qaytardi. Eng yomoni esa — U uni o'ziga biror alohida ish qilishi uchun emas, balki shunchaki Unga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri yuziga qarashi, Unga qarab, hech narsa qilmasdan, ta'riflab bo'lmas azob chekishi uchun tortardi.

paras.en: And to save himself from this, Ivan Ilyitch sought amusements, other screens, and these screens he found, and for a little while they did seem to save him; but soon again they were not so much broken down as let the light through, as though It pierced through everything, and there was nothing that could shut It off.
paras.uz: Va bundan qutulish uchun Ivan Ilich ermaklar, boshqa to'siqlar izlardi va bu to'siqlarni topardi, ular bir oz vaqt uni qutqarayotgandek ham tuyulardi; lekin tez orada ular buzilmasa-da, yorug'likni o'tkaza boshlardi, go'yo U hamma narsani teshib o'tadigandek va Uni to'sib qo'yadigan hech narsa yo'qdek.

paras.en: Sometimes during those days he would go into the drawing-room he had furnished, that drawing-room where he had fallen, for which⁠—how bitterly ludicrous it was for him to think of it!⁠—for the decoration of which he had sacrificed his life, for he knew that it was that bruise that had started his illness. He went in and saw that the polished table had been scratched by something. He looked for the cause, and found it in the bronze clasps of the album, which had been twisted on one side. He took up the album, a costly one, which he had himself arranged with loving care, and was vexed at the carelessness of his daughter and her friends. Here a page was torn, here the photographs had been shifted out of their places. He carefully put it to rights again and bent the clasp back.
paras.uz: Ba'zan o'sha kunlarda u o'zi jihozlagan mehmonxonaga kirardi — o'zi yiqilgan, — o'ylash unga naqadar achchiq kulgili edi! — bezagi uchun hayotini qurbon qilgan o'sha mehmonxonaga, chunki u kasalligi aynan o'sha lat yeyishdan boshlanganini bilardi. U kirib, sayqallangan stolni nimadir tirnab qo'yganini ko'rdi. Sababini izladi va uni bir tomonga qayrilib qolgan albomning bronza qisqichlarida topdi. U o'zi mehr bilan tartibga solgan qimmatbaho albomni oldi va qizi va uning dugonalarining beparvoligidan achchiqlandi. Bu yerda bir sahifa yirtilgan, bu yerda suratlar joyidan surilgan edi. U uni ehtiyotkorlik bilan yana tartibga keltirdi va qisqichni orqaga egdi.

paras.en: Then the idea occurred to him to move all this établissement of the albums to another corner where the flowers stood. He called the footman; or his daughter or his wife came to help him. They did not agree with him, contradicted him; he argued, got angry. But all that was very well, since he did not think of It; It was not in sight.
paras.uz: Keyin unga albomlarning bu butun établissement'ini — «tartibini» gullar turgan boshqa burchakka ko'chirish fikri keldi. U malayni chaqirdi; yoki unga yordam berish uchun qizi yoki xotini keldi. Ular u bilan rozi bo'lishmadi, unga qarshi chiqishdi; u bahslashdi, jahli chiqdi. Lekin bularning hammasi yaxshi edi, chunki u U haqida o'ylamasdi; U ko'rinmasdi.

paras.en: But then his wife would say, as he moved something himself, “Do let the servants do it, you’ll hurt yourself again,” and all at once It peeped through the screen; he caught a glimpse of It. He caught a glimpse of It, but still he hoped It would hide itself. Involuntarily though, he kept watch on his side; there it is just the same still, aching still, and now he cannot forget it, and It is staring openly at him from behind the flowers. What’s the use of it all?
paras.uz: Lekin keyin xotini, u biror narsani o'zi surayotganida: «Xizmatkorlar qilsin, yana o'zingizni lat yegizasiz», derdi va birdan U to'siq orqali mo'ralardi; u Uni ko'rib qolardi. U Uni ko'rib qolardi, lekin baribir U yashirinadi, deb umid qilardi. Biroq beixtiyor biqinini kuzatardi: u yerda hammasi xuddi o'sha, hamon og'riyapti, endi u buni unuta olmaydi va U gullar orqasidan unga ochiq tikilib turibdi. Bularning hammasidan nima foyda?

paras.en: “And it’s the fact that here, at that curtain, as if it had been storming a fort, I lost my life. Is it possible? How awful and how silly! It cannot be! It cannot be, and it is.”
paras.uz: «Va haqiqatan ham, mana shu yerda, mana shu parda oldida, go'yo qal'ani zabt etayotgandek, hayotimni yo'qotdim. Bo'lishi mumkinmi? Naqadar dahshatli va naqadar ahmoqona! Bo'lishi mumkin emas! Bo'lishi mumkin emas, lekin bor.»

paras.en: He went into his own room, lay down, and was again alone with It. Face to face with it, and nothing to be done with It. Nothing but to look at It and shiver.
paras.uz: U o'z xonasiga borib yotdi va yana U bilan yolg'iz qoldi. U bilan yuzma-yuz, va U bilan hech narsa qilib bo'lmaydi. Faqat Unga qarash va titrash.

quiz.q: What is the syllogism about Caius?
o: Caius is a man, men are mortal, therefore Caius is mortal
quiz.why_uz: Kizeveterning mantiq kitobidagi misol.

quiz.q: Why did the syllogism never seem to apply to Ivan Ilyitch?
o: He felt he was a unique person, little Vanya, not an abstract man
quiz.why_uz: U o'zini mavhum inson emas, betakror mavjudot deb his qilgan.

chapters.recap_uz: Mantiq kitobidagi sillogizm — «Kay inson, insonlar o'lar, demak Kay o'lar» — unga faqat Kayga tegishlidek tuyulgan: u esa kichkina Vanya edi. U o'lim fikrini to'sib turgan eski «to'siqlar»ga — sudga, mehmonxonaga — qaytishga urinadi, lekin «U» hamma narsani teshib o'tadi.

chapters.title: VII. Gerasim

paras.en: How it came to pass during the third month of Ivan Ilyitch’s illness, it would be impossible to say, for it happened little by little, imperceptibly, but it had come to pass that his wife and his daughter and his son and their servants and their acquaintances, and the doctors, and, most of all, he himself⁠—all were aware that all interest in him for other people consisted now in the question how soon he would leave his place empty, free the living from the constraint of his presence, and be set free himself from his sufferings.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich kasalligining uchinchi oyida bu qanday sodir bo'lganini aytib bo'lmasdi, chunki u asta-sekin, sezdirmasdan sodir bo'ldi, lekin shunday bo'ldiki, xotini ham, qizi ham, o'g'li ham, xizmatkorlari ham, tanishlari ham, doktorlar ham va, eng muhimi, uning o'zi ham — hammasi boshqalarning unga bo'lgan butun qiziqishi endi faqat bitta savoldan iborat ekanini bilishardi: u qachon o'rnini bo'shatadi, tiriklarni o'z borligining siqiqligidan ozod qiladi va o'zi ham azoblaridan qutuladi.

paras.en: He slept less and less; they gave him opium, and began to inject morphine. But this did not relieve him. The dull pain he experienced in the half-asleep condition at first only relieved him as a change, but then it became as bad, or even more agonising, than the open pain. He had special things to eat prepared for him according to the doctors’ prescriptions; but these dishes became more and more distasteful, more and more revolting to him.
paras.uz: U tobora kamroq uxlardi; unga afyun berishdi va morfiy ukoli qila boshlashdi. Lekin bu unga yengillik bermadi. Yarim uyqu holatida his qilgan xira og'riq avvaliga faqat o'zgarish sifatida yengillik berdi, keyin esa ochiq og'riq kabi yomon yoki undan ham azobliroq bo'lib qoldi. Doktorlarning ko'rsatmasiga ko'ra unga maxsus ovqatlar tayyorlanardi; lekin bu taomlar unga tobora bemazaroq, tobora jirkanchroq bo'lib bordi.

paras.en: Special arrangements, too, had to be made for his other physical needs, and this was a continual misery to him. Misery from the uncleanliness, the unseemliness, and the stench, from the feeling of another person having to assist in it.
paras.uz: Uning boshqa jismoniy ehtiyojlari uchun ham maxsus tadbirlar ko'rish kerak bo'ldi va bu unga doimiy azob edi. Nopoklikdan, nomaqbullikdan va sassiq hiddan, bunda boshqa odam yordam berishi kerakligi hissidan azob.

paras.en: But just from this most unpleasant side of his illness there came comfort to Ivan Ilyitch. There always came into his room on these occasions to clear up for him the peasant who waited at table, Gerasim.
paras.uz: Lekin aynan kasalligining shu eng noxush tomonidan Ivan Ilichga taskin keldi. Bunday paytlarda uning xonasiga tozalash uchun doim dasturxon atrofida xizmat qiladigan mujik Gerasim kirardi.

paras.en: Gerasim was a clean, fresh, young peasant, who had grown stout and hearty on the good fare in town. Always cheerful and bright. At first the sight of this lad, always cleanly dressed in the Russian style, engaged in this revolting task, embarrassed Ivan Ilyitch.
paras.uz: Gerasim shahardagi yaxshi ovqatdan to'lishib, baquvvat bo'lib ketgan ozoda, tetik yosh mujik edi. Doim quvnoq va ochiq yuzli. Avvaliga doim ruscha ozoda kiyingan bu yigitning bu jirkanch ish bilan band bo'lganini ko'rish Ivan Ilichni xijolat qilardi.

paras.en: One day, getting up from the night-stool, too weak to replace his clothes, he dropped on to a soft low chair and looked with horror at his bare, powerless thighs, with the muscles so sharply standing out on them.
paras.uz: Bir kuni tungi tuvakdan turib, kiyimini kiyishga holi yo'q, u yumshoq past kresloga cho'kdi va mushaklari keskin bo'rtib chiqqan yalang'och, kuchsiz sonlariga dahshat bilan qaradi.

paras.en: Then there came in with light, strong steps Gerasim, in his thick boots, diffusing a pleasant smell of tar from his boots, and bringing in the freshness of the winter air. Wearing a clean hempen apron, and a clean cotton shirt, with his sleeves tucked up on his strong, bare young arms, without looking at Ivan Ilyitch, obviously trying to check the radiant happiness in his face so as not to hurt the sick man, he went up to the night-stool.
paras.uz: Shunda qalin etiklarida, etiklaridan yoqimli qatron hidi taratib, qishki havo tozaligini olib, yengil, mustahkam qadamlar bilan Gerasim kirdi. Toza kanop fartuk va toza chit ko'ylak kiygan, yenglari kuchli, yalang'och yosh qo'llarida shimarilgan, Ivan Ilichga qaramay, kasalni ranjitmaslik uchun yuzidagi porloq baxtni bosishga urinayotgani aniq, u tungi tuvak oldiga bordi.

paras.en: “Gerasim,” said Ivan Ilyitch faintly.
paras.uz: — Gerasim, — dedi Ivan Ilich zaif ovozda.

paras.en: Gerasim started, clearly afraid that he had done something amiss, and with a rapid movement turned towards the sick man his fresh, good-natured, simple young face, just beginning to be downy with the first growth of beard.
paras.uz: Gerasim cho'chib tushdi, aftidan, nimadir noto'g'ri qildimmi, deb qo'rqib, tez harakat bilan kasalga endigina birinchi soqol tuklari chiqa boshlagan tetik, xushfe'l, sodda yosh yuzini burdi.

paras.en: “Yes, your honour.”
paras.uz: — Labbay, taqsir.

paras.en: “I’m afraid this is very disagreeable for you. You must excuse me. I can’t help it.”
paras.uz: — Bu sen uchun juda noxush, deb qo'rqaman. Meni kechir. Ilojim yo'q.

paras.en: “Why, upon my word, sir!” And Gerasim’s eyes beamed, and he showed his white young teeth in a smile. “What’s a little trouble? It’s a case of illness with you, sir.”
paras.uz: — Qo'ying-e, taqsir! — Gerasimning ko'zlari porladi va u jilmayib oppoq yosh tishlarini ko'rsatdi. — Ozgina mehnat nima bo'libdi? Axir sizda kasallik-ku, taqsir.

paras.en: And with his deft, strong arms he performed his habitual task, and went out, stepping lightly. And five minutes later, treading just as lightly, he came back.
paras.uz: Va u chaqqon, kuchli qo'llari bilan odatiy ishini bajardi va yengil qadam tashlab chiqib ketdi. Besh daqiqadan keyin xuddi shunday yengil qadam bosib qaytib keldi.

paras.en: Ivan Ilyitch was still sitting in the same way in the armchair.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich hamon kresloda xuddi o'sha holatda o'tirardi.

paras.en: “Gerasim,” he said, when the latter had replaced the night-stool all sweet and clean, “please help me; come here.” Gerasim went up to him. “Lift me up. It’s difficult for me alone, and I’ve sent Dmitry away.”
paras.uz: — Gerasim, — dedi u, Gerasim tungi tuvakni toza va pokiza holda joyiga qo'ygach, — iltimos, yordam ber; bu yoqqa kel. — Gerasim uning oldiga bordi. — Meni ko'tar. Yolg'iz o'zimga qiyin, Dmitriyni esa jo'natib yubordim.

paras.en: Gerasim went up to him; as lightly as he stepped he put his strong arms round him, deftly and gently lifted and supported him, with the other hand pulled up his trousers, and would have set him down again. But Ivan Ilyitch asked him to carry him to the sofa. Gerasim, without effort, carefully not squeezing him, led him, almost carrying him, to the sofa, and settled him there.
paras.uz: Gerasim uning oldiga bordi; qadam tashlaganidek yengil, kuchli qo'llari bilan uni quchoqladi, chaqqonlik va muloyimlik bilan ko'tarib, suyab turdi, boshqa qo'li bilan shimini tortib qo'ydi va uni yana o'tqazmoqchi bo'ldi. Lekin Ivan Ilich uni divanga olib borishini so'radi. Gerasim zo'riqmay, uni siqmaslikka ehtiyot bo'lib, deyarli ko'tarib, divanga olib bordi va o'sha yerga joylashtirdi.

paras.en: “Thank you; how neatly and well⁠ ⁠… you do everything.”
paras.uz: — Rahmat; hamma narsani qanchalik chaqqon va yaxshi… qilasan.

paras.en: Gerasim smiled again, and would have gone away. But Ivan Ilyitch felt his presence such a comfort that he was reluctant to let him go.
paras.uz: Gerasim yana jilmaydi va chiqib ketmoqchi bo'ldi. Lekin Ivan Ilich uning borligini shunchalik taskin deb his qildiki, uni qo'yib yuborgisi kelmadi.

paras.en: “Oh, move that chair near me, please. No, that one, under my legs. I feel easier when my legs are higher.”
paras.uz: — Oh, iltimos, mana bu stulni yonimga sur. Yo'q, anavisini, oyoqlarim ostiga. Oyoqlarim balandroq bo'lsa, o'zimni yengilroq his qilaman.

paras.en: Gerasim picked up the chair, and without letting it knock, set it gently down on the ground just at the right place, and lifted Ivan Ilyitch’s legs on to it. It seemed to Ivan Ilyitch that he was easier just at the moment when Gerasim lifted his legs higher.
paras.uz: Gerasim stulni oldi va uni taqillatmasdan, aynan kerakli joyga polga ohista qo'ydi va Ivan Ilichning oyoqlarini uning ustiga ko'tardi. Ivan Ilichga Gerasim oyoqlarini yuqoriroq ko'targan aynan o'sha lahzada yengil bo'lgandek tuyuldi.

paras.en: “I’m better when my legs are higher,” said Ivan Ilyitch. “Put that cushion under me.”
paras.uz: — Oyoqlarim balandroq bo'lsa, yaxshiroq, — dedi Ivan Ilich. — Anavi yostiqni tagimga qo'y.

paras.en: Gerasim did so. Again he lifted his legs to put the cushion under them. Again it seemed to Ivan Ilyitch that he was easier at that moment when Gerasim held his legs raised. When he laid them down again, he felt worse.
paras.uz: Gerasim shunday qildi. U yostiqni qo'yish uchun yana oyoqlarini ko'tardi. Yana Ivan Ilichga Gerasim oyoqlarini ko'tarib turgan o'sha lahzada yengil bo'lgandek tuyuldi. U ularni yana qo'yganida, ahvoli yomonlashdi.

paras.en: “Gerasim,” he said to him, “are you busy just now?”
paras.uz: — Gerasim, — dedi u unga, — hozir bandmisan?

paras.en: “Not at all, sir,” said Gerasim, who had learned among the town-bred servants how to speak to gentlefolks.
paras.uz: — Aslo, taqsir, — dedi janoblar bilan qanday gaplashishni shaharlik xizmatkorlar orasida o'rganib olgan Gerasim.

paras.en: “What have you left to do?”
paras.uz: — Yana nima ishing qoldi?

paras.en: “Why, what have I to do? I’ve done everything, there’s only the wood to chop for tomorrow.”
paras.uz: — Nima ishim bo'lardi? Hammasini qildim, faqat ertaga uchun o'tin yorish qoldi.

paras.en: “Then hold my legs up like that⁠—can you?”
paras.uz: — Unda oyoqlarimni mana shunday ko'tarib tur — qo'lingdan keladimi?

paras.en: “To be sure, I can.” Gerasim lifted the legs up. And it seemed to Ivan Ilyitch that in that position he did not feel the pain at all.
paras.uz: — Bo'lmasa-chi, keladi. — Gerasim oyoqlarni ko'tardi. Va Ivan Ilichga bu holatda og'riqni umuman sezmayotgandek tuyuldi.

paras.en: “But how about the wood?”
paras.uz: — O'tin-chi?

paras.en: “Don’t you trouble about that, sir. We shall have time enough.”
paras.uz: — Uni o'ylamang, taqsir. Vaqtimiz yetarli.

paras.en: Ivan Ilyitch made Gerasim sit and hold his legs, and began to talk to him. And, strange to say, he fancied he felt better while Gerasim had hold of his legs.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich Gerasimni o'tqazib, oyoqlarini ushlatib qo'ydi va u bilan gaplasha boshladi. Va, g'alati, Gerasim oyoqlarini ushlab turganida o'zini yaxshiroq his qilayotgandek bo'ldi.

paras.en: From that time forward Ivan Ilyitch would sometimes call Gerasim, and get him to hold his legs on his shoulders, and he liked talking with him. Gerasim did this easily, readily, simply, and with a good-nature that touched Ivan Ilyitch. Health, strength, and heartiness in all other people were offensive to Ivan Ilyitch; but the strength and heartiness of Gerasim did not mortify him, but soothed him.
paras.uz: O'shandan beri Ivan Ilich ba'zan Gerasimni chaqirib, oyoqlarini uning yelkalarida ushlatib turardi va u bilan gaplashishni yoqtirardi. Gerasim buni yengil, tayyorlik bilan, sodda va Ivan Ilichni ta'sirlantiradigan xushfe'llik bilan qilardi. Boshqa barcha odamlardagi sog'lik, kuch va tetiklik Ivan Ilichni haqoratlardi; lekin Gerasimning kuchi va tetikligi uni ranjitmas, balki tinchlantirardi.

paras.en: Ivan Ilyitch’s great misery was due to the deception that for some reason or other everyone kept up with him⁠—that he was simply ill, and not dying, and that he need only keep quiet and follow the doctor’s orders, and then some great change for the better would be the result. He knew that whatever they might do, there would be no result except more agonising sufferings and death. And he was made miserable by this lie, made miserable at their refusing to acknowledge what they all knew and he knew, by their persisting in lying over him about his awful position, and in forcing him too to take part in this lie. Lying, lying, this lying carried on over him on the eve of his death, and destined to bring that terrible, solemn act of his death down to the level of all their visits, curtains, sturgeons for dinner⁠ ⁠… was a horrible agony for Ivan Ilyitch. And, strange to say, many times when they had been going through the regular performance over him, he had been within a hair’s-breadth of screaming at them: “Cease your lying! You know, and I know, that I’m dying; so do, at least, give over lying!” But he had never had the spirit to do this. The terrible, awful act of his dying was, he saw, by all those about him, brought down to the level of a casual, unpleasant, and to some extent indecorous, incident (somewhat as they would behave with a person who should enter a drawing-room smelling unpleasant). It was brought down to this level by that very decorum to which he had been enslaved all his life. He saw that no one felt for him, because no one would even grasp his position. Gerasim was the only person who recognised the position, and felt sorry for him. And that was why Ivan Ilyitch was only at ease with Gerasim. He felt comforted when Gerasim sometimes supported his legs for whole nights at a stretch, and would not go away to bed, saying, “Don’t you worry yourself, Ivan Ilyitch, I’ll get sleep enough yet,” or when suddenly dropping into the familiar peasant forms of speech, he added: “If thou weren’t sick, but as ’tis, ’twould be strange if I didn’t wait on thee.” Gerasim alone did not lie; everything showed clearly that he alone understood what it meant, and saw no necessity to disguise it, and simply felt sorry for his sick, wasting master. He even said this once straight out, when Ivan Ilyitch was sending him away.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilichning katta azobi negadir hamma u bilan davom ettirayotgan yolg'on tufayli edi — u shunchaki kasal, o'layotgani yo'q, faqat tinch yotib, doktorning buyruqlarini bajarsa bas, shunda yaxshi tomonga qandaydir katta o'zgarish bo'ladi, degan yolg'on. U ular nima qilmasin, yanada azobliroq qiynoqlar va o'limdan boshqa hech qanday natija bo'lmasligini bilardi. Va uni bu yolg'on, ular hammasi bilgan va u ham bilgan narsani tan olishdan bosh tortishlari, uning dahshatli ahvoli ustida yolg'on gapirishda davom etishlari va uni ham bu yolg'onda ishtirok etishga majbur qilishlari azoblardi. Yolg'on, yolg'on, uning o'limi arafasida ustida qilinayotgan va uning o'limining o'sha dahshatli, tantanali harakatini ularning barcha mehmondorchiliklari, pardalari, tushlikdagi osyotr baliqlari darajasiga tushirishga mo'ljallangan bu yolg'on… Ivan Ilich uchun dahshatli azob edi. Va, g'alati, ko'p marta, ular uning ustida odatiy tomoshani o'tkazayotganlarida, u ularga qichqirib yuborishiga bir qil qolgan edi: «Yolg'on gapirishni bas qilinglar! Siz ham bilasiz, men ham bilaman, men o'layapman; hech bo'lmasa yolg'on gapirishni to'xtatinglar!» Lekin buni qilishga hech qachon jur'ati yetmadi. Uning o'limining dahshatli, qo'rqinchli harakati, u ko'rib turganidek, atrofidagi barcha odamlar tomonidan tasodifiy, noxush va qaysidir ma'noda odobsiz voqea darajasiga tushirilgan edi (xuddi mehmonxonaga yoqimsiz hid taratib kirgan odamga qanday munosabatda bo'lishsa, shunga o'xshash). U aynan butun umri davomida qul bo'lgan o'sha odob tomonidan shu darajaga tushirilgan edi. U hech kim unga achinmasligini ko'rardi, chunki hech kim uning ahvolini anglashni ham istamasdi. Faqat Gerasim uning ahvolini tan olardi va unga achinardi. Va shuning uchun Ivan Ilich faqat Gerasim bilan o'zini erkin his qilardi. Gerasim ba'zan butun tunlar davomida uning oyoqlarini ushlab turganida va uxlashga ketmay: «Siz xavotir olmang, Ivan Ilich, men hali uxlab olaman», deganida yoki birdan tanish mujikcha gapga o'tib: «Kasal bo'lmaganingda boshqa gap edi, lekin shunday ekan, senga qaramasam g'alati bo'lardi», deb qo'shganida u taskin topardi. Faqat Gerasim yolg'on gapirmasdi; hamma narsa faqat u buning ma'nosini tushunishini, uni yashirishga hojat ko'rmasligini va shunchaki kasal, ozib borayotgan xo'jayiniga achinishini aniq ko'rsatib turardi. Bir safar, Ivan Ilich uni jo'natayotganida, u buni hatto to'g'ridan-to'g'ri aytdi.

paras.en: “We shall all die. So what’s a little trouble?” he said, meaning by this to express that he did not complain of the trouble just because he was taking this trouble for a dying man, and he hoped that for him too someone would be willing to take the same trouble when his time came.
paras.uz: — Hammamiz o'lamiz. Ozgina mehnat nima bo'libdi? — dedi u, bu bilan mehnatdan nolimasligini aynan o'layotgan odam uchun bu mehnatni qilayotgani uchun ekanini va uning ham vaqti kelganda kimdir u uchun xuddi shunday mehnat qilishga tayyor bo'lishiga umid qilishini bildirmoqchi bo'lib.

paras.en: Apart from this deception, or in consequence of it, what made the greatest misery for Ivan Ilyitch was that no one felt for him as he would have liked them to feel for him. At certain moments, after prolonged suffering, Ivan Ilyitch, ashamed as he would have been to own it, longed more than anything for someone to feel sorry for him, as for a sick child. He longed to be petted, kissed, and wept over, as children are petted and comforted. He knew that he was an important member of the law-courts, that he had a beard turning grey, and that therefore it was impossible. But still he longed for it. And in his relations with Gerasim there was something approaching to that. And that was why being with Gerasim was a comfort to him. Ivan Ilyitch longs to weep, longs to be petted and wept over, and then there comes in a colleague, Shebek; and instead of weeping and being petted, Ivan Ilyitch puts on his serious, severe, earnest face, and from mere inertia gives his views on the effect of the last decision in the Court of Appeal, and obstinately insists upon them. This falsity around him and within him did more than anything to poison Ivan Ilyitch’s last days.
paras.uz: Bu yolg'ondan tashqari yoki uning natijasida Ivan Ilichning eng katta azobi hech kim unga u istaganidek achinmasligi edi. Ba'zi lahzalarda, uzoq azoblardan keyin, Ivan Ilich buni tan olishdan qanchalik uyalsa ham, hammasidan ko'ra kimdir unga kasal boladek achinishini istardi. U bolalarni erkalab, ovutganlaridek, uni erkalashlarini, o'pishlarini va uning ustida yig'lashlarini istardi. U sudning muhim a'zosi ekanini, soqoli oqarib borayotganini va shuning uchun bu imkonsizligini bilardi. Lekin baribir buni istardi. Gerasim bilan munosabatlarida esa shunga yaqin nimadir bor edi. Va shuning uchun Gerasim bilan bo'lish unga taskin edi. Ivan Ilich yig'lashni, erkalanishni va ustida yig'lashlarini istaydi, keyin hamkasbi Shebek kirib keladi; va yig'lash va erkalanish o'rniga Ivan Ilich jiddiy, qattiq, salobatli yuz ifodasini oladi va shunchaki inersiya bilan Kassatsiya sudining so'nggi qarori ta'siri haqida o'z fikrini aytadi va unda qaysarlik bilan turib oladi. Uning atrofidagi va ichidagi bu soxtalik Ivan Ilichning so'nggi kunlarini hammasidan ko'ra ko'proq zaharladi.

quiz.why_uz: Gerasim xo'rlovchi ishni ham xushfe'llik bilan qiladi.
