chapters.recap_uz: Uchinchi oyda hamma — oila, doktorlar va uning o'zi — u qachon o'rnini bo'shatishini kutadi. Eng xo'rlovchi ishda yosh mujik Gerasim unga yordam beradi: oyoqlarini yelkasida ushlab turadi. Hamma yolg'on gapiradi — «shunchaki kasalsan» deydi; faqat Gerasim yolg'on gapirmaydi va unga achinadi. Ivan Ilich boladek erkalanishni istaydi.

chapters.title: VIII. A day of falsity

paras.en: It was morning. All that made it morning for Ivan Ilyitch was that Gerasim had gone away, and Pyotr the footman had come in; he had put out the candles, opened one of the curtains, and begun surreptitiously setting the room to rights. Whether it were morning or evening, Friday or Sunday, it all made no difference; it was always just the same thing. Gnawing, agonising pain never ceasing for an instant; the hopeless sense of life always ebbing away, but still not yet gone; always swooping down on him that fearful, hated death, which was the only reality, and always the same falsity. What were days, or weeks, or hours of the day to him?
paras.uz: Tong edi. Ivan Ilich uchun tongni tong qilgan narsa faqat Gerasimning ketgani va malay Pyotrning kirgani edi; u shamlarni o'chirgan, pardalardan birini ochgan va yashirincha xonani yig'ishtira boshlagan edi. Ertalabmi yoki kechqurunmi, jumami yoki yakshanbami — hammasining farqi yo'q edi; hammasi doim bir xil edi. Bir lahza ham to'xtamaydigan kemiruvchi, azobli og'riq; doim so'nib borayotgan, lekin hali ketib ulgurmagan hayotning umidsiz hissi; doim unga yopirilib kelayotgan o'sha qo'rqinchli, nafratli o'lim — yagona haqiqat — va doim o'sha soxtalik. Kunlar, haftalar yoki kunning soatlari unga nima edi?

paras.en: “Will you have tea, sir?”
paras.uz: — Choy ichasizmi, taqsir?

paras.en: “He wants things done in their regular order. In the morning the family should have tea,” he thought, and only said⁠—
paras.uz: «U ishlar odatdagi tartibda bo'lishini istaydi. Ertalab oila choy ichishi kerak», deb o'yladi u va faqat dedi:

paras.en: “No.”
paras.uz: — Yo'q.

paras.en: “Would you care to move on to the sofa?”
paras.uz: — Divanga o'tishni istaysizmi?

paras.en: “He wants to make the room tidy, and I’m in his way. I’m uncleanness, disorder,” he thought, and only said⁠—
paras.uz: «U xonani tartibga keltirmoqchi, men esa unga xalaqit beryapman. Men — nopoklik, tartibsizlik», deb o'yladi u va faqat dedi:

paras.en: “No, leave me alone.”
paras.uz: — Yo'q, meni tinch qo'y.

paras.en: The servant still moved busily about his work. Ivan Ilyitch stretched out his hand. Pyotr went up to offer his services.
paras.uz: Xizmatkor hamon o'z ishi bilan shoshib yurardi. Ivan Ilich qo'lini cho'zdi. Pyotr xizmat taklif qilish uchun yaqin keldi.

paras.en: “What can I get you?”
paras.uz: — Nima beray?

paras.en: “My watch.”
paras.uz: — Soatimni.

paras.en: Pyotr got out the watch, which lay just under his hand, and gave it him.
paras.uz: Pyotr shundoqqina qo'li ostida yotgan soatni olib, unga berdi.

paras.en: “Half-past eight. Are they up?”
paras.uz: — Sakkiz yarim. Ular turishdimi?

paras.en: “Not yet, sir. Vladimir Ivanovitch” (that was his son) “has gone to the high school, and Praskovya Fyodorovna gave orders that she was to be waked if you asked for her. Shall I send word?”
paras.uz: — Hali yo'q, taqsir. Vladimir Ivanovich (bu uning o'g'li edi) gimnaziyaga ketdi, Praskovya Fyodorovna esa agar siz so'rasangiz, uni uyg'otishni buyurdi. Xabar beraymi?

paras.en: “No, no need. Should I try some tea?” he thought.
paras.uz: — Yo'q, kerak emas. — «Choy ichib ko'rsammikan?» deb o'yladi u.

paras.en: “Yes, tea⁠ ⁠… bring it.”
paras.uz: — Ha, choy… olib kel.

paras.en: Pyotr was on his way out. Ivan Ilyitch felt frightened of being left alone. “How keep him? Oh, the medicine. Pyotr, give me my medicine. Oh well, maybe, medicine may still be some good.” He took the spoon, drank it. “No, it does no good. It’s all rubbish, deception,” he decided, as soon as he tasted the familiar, mawkish, hopeless taste. “No, I can’t believe it now. But the pain, why this pain; if it would only cease for a minute.” And he groaned. Pyotr turned round. “No, go on. Bring the tea.”
paras.uz: Pyotr chiqib ketayotgan edi. Ivan Ilich yolg'iz qolishdan qo'rqib ketdi. «Uni qanday ushlab qolsam? Ha, dori. Pyotr, dorimni ber. Nima ham derdim, balki dori hali foyda berar.» U qoshiqni olib, ichdi. «Yo'q, foydasi yo'q. Hammasi safsata, aldov», deb qaror qildi u o'sha tanish, chuchmal, umidsiz ta'mni sezishi bilanoq. «Yo'q, endi ishona olmayman. Lekin og'riq, nega bu og'riq; qaniydi bir daqiqaga bo'lsa ham to'xtasa.» Va u ingradi. Pyotr o'girildi. «Yo'q, bor. Choyni olib kel.»

paras.en: Pyotr went away. Ivan Ilyitch, left alone, moaned, not so much from the pain, awful as it was, as from misery. Always the same thing again and again, all these endless days and nights. If it would only be quicker. Quicker to what? Death, darkness. No, no. Anything better than death!
paras.uz: Pyotr chiqib ketdi. Yolg'iz qolgan Ivan Ilich og'riqdan, u qanchalik dahshatli bo'lmasin, emas, ko'proq g'amdan ingradi. Doim bir xil narsa, qayta-qayta, bu cheksiz kunlar va tunlar davomida. Qaniydi tezroq bo'lsa. Nimaga tezroq? O'limga, zulmatga. Yo'q, yo'q. O'limdan boshqa har qanday narsa yaxshiroq!

paras.en: When Pyotr came in with the tea on a tray, Ivan Ilyitch stared for some time absentmindedly at him, not grasping who he was and what he wanted. Pyotr was disconcerted by this stare. And when he showed he was disconcerted, Ivan Ilyitch came to himself.
paras.uz: Pyotr patnisda choy olib kirganida, Ivan Ilich uning kimligini va nima istayotganini tushunmay, unga bir muddat parishon tikilib qoldi. Pyotr bu nigohdan xijolat bo'ldi. U xijolat bo'lganini ko'rsatganida, Ivan Ilich o'ziga keldi.

paras.en: “Oh yes,” he said, “tea, good, set it down. Only help me to wash and put on a clean shirt.”
paras.uz: — Ha, — dedi u, — choy, yaxshi, qo'y. Faqat yuvinishimga va toza ko'ylak kiyishimga yordam ber.

paras.en: And Ivan Ilyitch began his washing. He washed his hands slowly, and then his face, cleaned his teeth, combed his hair, and looked in the looking-glass. He felt frightened at what he saw, especially at the way his hair clung limply to his pale forehead. When his shirt was being changed, he knew he would be still more terrified if he glanced at his body, and he avoided looking at himself. But at last it was all over. He put on his dressing-gown, covered himself with a rug, and sat in the armchair to drink his tea. For one moment he felt refreshed; but as soon as he began to drink the tea, again there was the same taste, the same pain. He forced himself to finish it, and lay down, stretching out his legs. He lay down and dismissed Pyotr.
paras.uz: Va Ivan Ilich yuvina boshladi. U sekin qo'llarini, keyin yuzini yuvdi, tishlarini tozaladi, sochini taradi va ko'zguga qaradi. Ko'rgan narsasidan, ayniqsa sochlarining oqargan peshonasiga shalvirab yopishib turganidan qo'rqib ketdi. Ko'ylagi almashtirilayotganda, agar tanasiga qarasa, yanada ko'proq dahshatga tushishini bilardi va o'ziga qarashdan qochdi. Lekin nihoyat hammasi tugadi. U xalatini kiydi, pled bilan o'randi va choy ichish uchun kresloga o'tirdi. Bir lahza o'zini tetik his qildi; lekin choy icha boshlashi bilanoq yana o'sha ta'm, o'sha og'riq. U o'zini zo'rlab choyni tugatdi va oyoqlarini cho'zib yotdi. Yotdi va Pyotrni jo'natib yubordi.

paras.en: Always the same. A gleam of hope flashes for a moment, then again the sea of despair roars about him again, and always pain, always pain, always heartache, and always the same thing. Alone it is awfully dreary; he longs to call someone, but he knows beforehand that with others present it will be worse. “Morphine again⁠—only to forget again. I’ll tell him, the doctor, that he must think of something else. It can’t go on; it can’t go on like this.”
paras.uz: Doim bir xil. Bir lahzaga umid uchqunlari chaqnaydi, keyin yana uning atrofida umidsizlik dengizi guvillaydi, va doim og'riq, doim og'riq, doim yurak siqilishi va doim bir xil narsa. Yolg'iz dahshatli zerikarli; u kimnidir chaqirishni istaydi, lekin boshqalar bo'lsa, yomonroq bo'lishini oldindan biladi. «Yana morfiy — faqat yana unutish uchun. Unga, doktorga, boshqa narsa o'ylab topishi kerakligini aytaman. Bunday davom eta olmaydi; bunday davom eta olmaydi.»

paras.en: One hour, two hours pass like this. Then there is a ring at the front door. The doctor, perhaps. Yes, it is the doctor, fresh, hearty, fat, and cheerful, wearing that expression that seems to say, “You there are in a panic about something, but we’ll soon set things right for you.” The doctor is aware that this expression is hardly fitting here, but he has put it on once and for all, and can’t take it off, like a man who has put on a frockcoat to pay a round of calls.
paras.uz: Bir soat, ikki soat shunday o'tadi. Keyin old eshikda qo'ng'iroq chalinadi. Doktor, ehtimol. Ha, bu doktor — tetik, baquvvat, semiz va quvnoq, go'yo: «Siz u yerda nimadandir vahimaga tushgansiz, lekin biz tez orada hammasini to'g'rilab qo'yamiz», deyotgandek ifoda bilan. Doktor bu ifoda bu yerda unchalik o'rinli emasligini biladi, lekin uni bir marta va butunlay kiyib olgan va uni yecha olmaydi — xuddi mehmondorchilikka aylanib chiqish uchun syurtuk kiyib olgan odamdek.

paras.en: In a hearty, reassuring manner the doctor rubs his hands.
paras.uz: Baquvvat, ishontiruvchi tarzda doktor qo'llarini ishqalaydi.

paras.en: “I’m cold. It’s a sharp frost. Just let me warm myself,” he says with an expression, as though it’s only a matter of waiting a little till he’s warm, and as soon as he’s warm he’ll set everything to rights.
paras.uz: — Sovqotdim. Qattiq ayoz. Bir isinib olay, — deydi u go'yo gap faqat isinguncha biroz kutishda-yu, isinishi bilanoq hammasini to'g'rilab qo'yadigandek ifoda bilan.

paras.en: “Well, now, how are you?”
paras.uz: — Xo'sh, endi, qalaysiz?

paras.en: Ivan Ilyitch feels that the doctor would like to say, “How’s the little trouble?” but that he feels that he can’t talk like that, and says, “How did you pass the night?”
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich doktor «Kasalchamiz qalay?» demoqchi ekanini, lekin bunday gapirib bo'lmasligini his qilib, «Tunni qanday o'tkazdingiz?» deyotganini sezadi.

paras.en: Ivan Ilyitch looks at the doctor with an expression that asks⁠—
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich doktorga go'yo shunday so'rayotgan ifoda bilan qaraydi:

paras.en: “Is it possible you’re never ashamed of lying?”
paras.uz: «Nahotki yolg'on gapirishdan hech qachon uyalmasangiz?»

paras.en: But the doctor does not care to understand this look.
paras.uz: Lekin doktor bu nigohni tushunishni istamaydi.

paras.en: And Ivan Ilyitch says⁠—
paras.uz: Va Ivan Ilich deydi:

paras.en: “It’s always just as awful. The pain never leaves me, never ceases. If only there were something!”
paras.uz: — Doim xuddi shunday dahshatli. Og'riq meni hech qachon tark etmaydi, hech qachon to'xtamaydi. Qaniydi biror narsa bo'lsa!

paras.en: “Ah, you’re all like that, all sick people say that. Come, now I do believe I’m thawed; even Praskovya Fyodorovna, who’s so particular, could find no fault with my temperature. Well, now I can say good morning.” And the doctor shakes hands.
paras.uz: — Eh, hammangiz shundaysiz, hamma kasallar shunday deydi. Qani, endi isindim shekilli; hatto shunchalik talabchan Praskovya Fyodorovna ham haroratimdan kamchilik topa olmaydi. Xo'sh, endi xayrli tong deyishim mumkin. — Va doktor qo'l beradi.

paras.en: And dropping his former levity, the doctor, with a serious face, proceeds to examine the patient, feeling his pulse, to take his temperature, and then the tappings and soundings begin.
paras.uz: Va avvalgi yengiltabiatligini tashlab, doktor jiddiy yuz bilan kasalni tekshirishga kirishadi: tomirini ushlab ko'radi, haroratini o'lchaydi, keyin tukillatish va quloq solishlar boshlanadi.

paras.en: Ivan Ilyitch knows positively and indubitably that it’s all nonsense and empty deception; but when the doctor, kneeling down, stretches over him, putting his ear first higher, then lower, and goes through various gymnastic evolutions over him with a serious face, Ivan Ilyitch is affected by this, as he used sometimes to be affected by the speeches of the lawyers in court, though he was perfectly well aware that they were telling lies all the while and why they were telling lies.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich bularning hammasi bema'nilik va quruq aldov ekanini aniq va shubhasiz biladi; lekin doktor tiz cho'kib, uning ustiga egilib, qulog'ini goh yuqoriroq, goh pastroq qo'yib, jiddiy yuz bilan uning ustida turli gimnastik harakatlarni bajarganda, Ivan Ilichga bu ta'sir qiladi — xuddi ilgari sudda advokatlarning nutqlari, ular butun vaqt davomida yolg'on gapirayotganini va nega yolg'on gapirayotganini juda yaxshi bilsa ham, unga ba'zan ta'sir qilganidek.

paras.en: The doctor, kneeling on the sofa, was still sounding him, when there was the rustle of Praskovya Fyodorovna’s silk dress in the doorway, and she was heard scolding Pyotr for not having let her know that the doctor had come.
paras.uz: Doktor divanda tiz cho'kib, hamon uni tekshirayotgan edi, shu payt eshik oldida Praskovya Fyodorovnaning ipak ko'ylagi shitirladi va uning doktor kelganini o'ziga xabar qilmagani uchun Pyotrni koyiyotgani eshitildi.

paras.en: She comes in, kisses her husband, and at once begins to explain that she has been up a long while, and that it was only through a misunderstanding that she was not there when the doctor came.
paras.uz: U kiradi, erini o'padi va darhol u allaqachon ancha oldin turganini, doktor kelganida bu yerda bo'lmagani faqat anglashilmovchilik tufayli ekanini tushuntira boshlaydi.

paras.en: Ivan Ilyitch looks at her, scans her all over, and sets down against her her whiteness and plumpness, and the cleanness of her hands and neck, and the glossiness of her hair, and the gleam full of life in her eyes. With all the force of his soul he hates her. And when she touches him it makes him suffer from the thrill of hatred he feels for her.
paras.uz: Ivan Ilich unga qaraydi, uni boshdan-oyoq ko'zdan kechiradi va uning oqligini, to'laligini, qo'llari va bo'ynining tozaligini, sochlarining yaltirashini va ko'zlaridagi hayotga to'la chaqnashni uning ziyoniga yozib qo'yadi. U uni butun qalbi bilan yomon ko'radi. Va u unga tegsa, unga bo'lgan nafrat titrog'idan azob chekadi.

paras.en: Her attitude to him and his illness is still the same. Just as the doctor had taken up a certain line with the patient which he was not now able to drop, so she too had taken up a line with him⁠—that he was not doing something he ought to do, and was himself to blame, and she was lovingly reproaching him for his neglect, and she could not now get out of this attitude.
paras.uz: Uning unga va kasalligiga munosabati hamon o'sha-o'sha. Doktor kasalga nisbatan endi tashlay olmaydigan muayyan yo'lni tutganidek, u ham unga nisbatan bir yo'lni tutgan edi — u qilishi kerak bo'lgan nimanidir qilmayapti va o'zi aybdor, u esa uni beparvoligi uchun mehr bilan koyiyapti; va u endi bu munosabatdan chiqa olmasdi.

paras.en: “Why, you know, he won’t listen to me; he doesn’t take his medicine at the right times. And what’s worse still, he insists on lying in a position that surely must be bad for him⁠—with his legs in the air.”
paras.uz: — Axir, bilasizmi, u meni tinglamaydi; dorisini o'z vaqtida ichmaydi. Eng yomoni esa — u o'ziga albatta zararli bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan holatda — oyoqlarini havoga ko'tarib yotishda turib oladi.

paras.en: She described how he made Gerasim hold his legs up.
paras.uz: U Gerasimga oyoqlarini qanday ko'tartirib turishini tasvirlab berdi.

paras.en: The doctor smiled with kindly condescension that said, “Oh well, it can’t be helped, these sick people do take up such foolish fancies; but we must forgive them.”
paras.uz: Doktor mehribon kamsitish bilan jilmaydi, bu jilmayish: «Nima ham qilardik, bu kasallar shunday ahmoqona injiqliklarga beriladi; lekin ularni kechirishimiz kerak», derdi.

paras.en: When the examination was over, the doctor looked at his watch, and then Praskovya Fyodorovna informed Ivan Ilyitch that it must of course be as he liked, but she had sent today for a celebrated doctor, and that he would examine him, and have a consultation with Mihail Danilovitch (that was the name of their regular doctor).
paras.uz: Tekshiruv tugagach, doktor soatiga qaradi, keyin Praskovya Fyodorovna Ivan Ilichga, albatta, u qanday xohlasa, shunday bo'ladi, lekin u bugun mashhur doktorni chaqirtirgani, u uni tekshirib, Mixail Danilovich (ularning doimiy doktorining ismi shunday edi) bilan konsilium o'tkazishini ma'lum qildi.

paras.en: “Don’t oppose it now, please. This I’m doing entirely for my own sake,” she said ironically, meaning it to be understood that she was doing it all for his sake, and was only saying this to give him no right to refuse her request. He lay silent, knitting his brows. He felt that he was hemmed in by such a tangle of falsity that it was hard to disentangle anything from it.
paras.uz: — Iltimos, endi qarshilik qilmang. Buni butunlay o'zim uchun qilyapman, — dedi u kinoya bilan, bu bilan hammasini uning uchun qilayotganini va buni faqat unga iltimosini rad etishga haq bermaslik uchun aytayotganini tushuntirmoqchi bo'lib. U qovog'ini solib, indamay yotdi. U shunday soxtalik chigalligi bilan o'ralganini his qildiki, undan biror narsani ajratib olish qiyin edi.

paras.en: Everything she did for him was entirely for her own sake, and she told him she was doing for her own sake what she actually was doing for her own sake as something so incredible that he would take it as meaning the opposite.
paras.uz: U uning uchun qilgan hamma narsasi butunlay o'zi uchun edi va u unga aslida o'zi uchun qilayotgan narsani o'zi uchun qilyapman, deb shunday aql bovar qilmaydigan narsa sifatida aytardiki, u buni teskari ma'noda tushunishi kerak edi.

paras.en: At half-past eleven the celebrated doctor came. Again came the sounding, and then grave conversation in his presence and in the other room about the kidney and the appendix, and questions and answers, with such an air of significance, that again, instead of the real question of life and death, which was now the only one that confronted him, the question that came uppermost was of the kidney and the appendix, which were doing something not as they ought to do, and were for that reason being attacked by Mihail Danilovitch and the celebrated doctor, and forced to mend their ways.
paras.uz: Soat o'n bir yarimda mashhur doktor keldi. Yana quloq solib tekshirish, keyin uning huzurida va boshqa xonada buyrak va ko'richak haqida jiddiy suhbat, shunday ma'noli qiyofali savol-javoblar bo'ldiki, yana endi uning oldida turgan yagona savol — hayot va o'lim haqidagi haqiqiy savol o'rniga buyrak va ko'richak haqidagi savol birinchi o'ringa chiqdi: ular qanday bo'lishi kerak bo'lsa, shunday ish qilmayapti va shuning uchun Mixail Danilovich va mashhur doktor ularga hujum qilib, ularni yo'lga solishga majburlayapti.

paras.en: The celebrated doctor took leave of him with a serious, but not a hopeless face. And to the timid question that Ivan Ilyitch addressed to him while he lifted his eyes, shining with terror and hope, up towards him, Was there a chance of recovery? he answered that he could not answer for it, but that there was a chance. The look of hope with which Ivan Ilyitch watched the doctor out was so piteous that, seeing it, Praskovya Fyodorovna positively burst into tears, as she went out of the door to hand the celebrated doctor his fee in the next room.
paras.uz: Mashhur doktor u bilan jiddiy, lekin umidsiz bo'lmagan yuz bilan xayrlashdi. Ivan Ilich dahshat va umid bilan porlab turgan ko'zlarini unga ko'tarib bergan tortinchoq savolga — tuzalish imkoni bormi? — u kafolat bera olmasligini, lekin imkon borligini aytib javob berdi. Ivan Ilich doktorni kuzatib qo'ygan umid nigohi shunchalik ayanchli ediki, buni ko'rib, Praskovya Fyodorovna qo'shni xonada mashhur doktorga haqini berish uchun eshikdan chiqarkan, hatto yig'lab yubordi.

paras.en: The gleam of hope kindled by the doctor’s assurance did not last long. Again the same room, the same pictures, the curtains, the wallpaper, the medicine-bottles, and ever the same, his aching suffering body. And Ivan Ilyitch began to moan; they gave him injections, and he sank into oblivion. When he waked up it was getting dark; they brought him his dinner. He forced himself to eat some broth; and again everything the same, and again the coming night.
paras.uz: Doktorning ishontirishi yoqqan umid uchquni uzoq davom etmadi. Yana o'sha xona, o'sha rasmlar, pardalar, gulqog'ozlar, dori shishalari va doim o'sha-o'sha, og'riyotgan, azob chekayotgan tanasi. Va Ivan Ilich ingray boshladi; unga ukol qilishdi va u hushsizlikka cho'mdi. Uyg'onganida qorong'i tushayotgan edi; unga tushlik olib kelishdi. U o'zini majburlab biroz sho'rva ichdi; va yana hammasi o'sha-o'sha, yana kelayotgan tun.

paras.en: After dinner at seven o’clock, Praskovya Fyodorovna came into his room, dressed as though to go to a soirée with her full bosom laced in tight, and traces of powder on her face. She had in the morning mentioned to him that they were going to the theatre. Sarah Bernhardt was visiting the town, and they had a box, which he had insisted on their taking. By now he had forgotten about it, and her smart attire was an offence to him. But he concealed this feeling when he recollected that he had himself insisted on their taking a box and going, because it was an aesthetic pleasure, beneficial and instructive for the children.
paras.uz: Soat yettidagi tushlikdan keyin Praskovya Fyodorovna uning xonasiga go'yo kechaga borayotgandek kiyinib, to'la ko'kragini qattiq siqib bog'lagan, yuzida upa izlari bilan kirdi. U ertalab unga teatrga borishlarini aytgan edi. Shaharga Sara Bernar gastrol bilan kelgan edi va ularning lojasi bor edi, uni olishlarini u o'zi talab qilgan edi. Hozir u bu haqda unutib qo'ygan edi va uning olifta kiyimi uni haqoratladi. Lekin lojani olib, borishlarini o'zi talab qilganini — chunki bu bolalar uchun foydali va ibratli estetik zavq ekanini — eslagach, bu hissini yashirdi.

paras.en: Praskovya Fyodorovna came in satisfied with herself, but yet with something of a guilty air. She sat down, asked how he was, as he saw, simply for the sake of asking, and not for the sake of learning anything, knowing indeed that there was nothing to learn, and began telling him how absolutely necessary it was; how she would not have gone for anything, but the box had been taken, and Ellen, their daughter, and Petrishtchev (the examining lawyer, the daughter’s suitor) were going, and that it was out of the question to let them go alone. But that she would have liked much better to stay with him. If only he would be sure to follow the doctor’s prescription while she was away.
paras.uz: Praskovya Fyodorovna o'zidan mamnun, lekin baribir qandaydir aybdor qiyofada kirdi. U o'tirdi, uning ahvolini so'radi — u ko'rib turganidek, biror narsani bilish uchun emas, shunchaki so'rash uchun, aslida biladigan hech narsa yo'qligini bilgan holda — va bu qanchalik zarur ekanini; u hech narsa uchun bormasligini, lekin loja olingani va qizlari Elen bilan Petrishchev (tergovchi, qizning kuyovi) borishayotgani va ularni yolg'iz qo'yib yuborib bo'lmasligini gapira boshladi. Lekin u bilan qolishni ancha afzal ko'rgan bo'lardi. Faqat u yo'qligida doktorning ko'rsatmasiga albatta amal qilsa bas.

paras.en: “Oh, and Fyodor Dmitryevitch” (the suitor) “would like to come in. May he? And Liza?”
paras.uz: — Ha, Fyodor Dmitriyevich (kuyov) kirmoqchi. Mumkinmi? Liza ham?

paras.en: “Yes, let them come in.”
paras.uz: — Ha, kirishsin.

paras.en: The daughter came in, in full dress, her fresh young body bare, while his body made him suffer so. But she made a show of it; she was strong, healthy, obviously in love, and impatient of the illness, suffering, and death that hindered her happiness.
paras.uz: Qizi ochiq yelkali bazm libosida, yosh tetik tanasi yalang'och holda kirdi, uning tanasi esa unga shunchalik azob berayotgan edi. Lekin u buni namoyish qilardi; u kuchli, sog'lom, aniq oshiq edi va baxtiga xalaqit berayotgan kasallik, azob va o'limga toqatsiz edi.

paras.en: Fyodor Dmitryevitch came in too in evening dress, his hair curled à la Capoul with his long sinewy neck tightly fenced round by a white collar, with his vast expanse of white chest and strong thighs displayed in narrow black trousers, with one white glove in his hand and a crush opera hat.
paras.uz: Fyodor Dmitriyevich ham frakda, sochlari à la Capoul jingalak qilingan, uzun tomirli bo'yni oq yoqa bilan mahkam o'ralgan, oq ko'kragining keng kengligi va kuchli sonlari tor qora shim ichida ko'rinib turgan, qo'lida bitta oq qo'lqop va yig'ma shlyapa bilan kirdi.

paras.en: Behind him crept in unnoticed the little high school boy in his new uniform, poor fellow, in gloves, and with that awful blue ring under his eyes that Ivan Ilyitch knew the meaning of.
paras.uz: Uning orqasidan yangi mundirdagi, qo'lqopli, ko'zlari ostida Ivan Ilich ma'nosini biladigan o'sha dahshatli ko'k doira bo'lgan kichkina gimnazist, bechora, sezdirmay sudralib kirdi.

paras.en: He always felt sorry for his son. And pitiable indeed was his scared face of sympathetic suffering. Except Gerasim, Ivan Ilyitch fancied that Volodya was the only one that understood and was sorry.
paras.uz: U doim o'g'liga achinardi. Uning hamdardlik azobiga to'la qo'rqib ketgan yuzi haqiqatan ham ayanchli edi. Ivan Ilichga Gerasimdan tashqari faqat Volodya tushunadi va achinadi, deb tuyulardi.

paras.en: They all sat down; again they asked how he was. A silence followed. Liza asked her mother about the opera-glass. An altercation ensued between the mother and daughter as to who had taken it, and where it had been put. It turned into an unpleasant squabble.
paras.uz: Hammasi o'tirishdi; yana uning ahvolini so'rashdi. Sukut cho'kdi. Liza onasidan durbin haqida so'radi. Ona va qiz o'rtasida uni kim olgani va qayerga qo'yilgani haqida bahs boshlandi. Bu noxush janjalga aylandi.

paras.en: Fyodor Dmitryevitch asked Ivan Ilyitch whether he had seen Sarah Bernhardt? Ivan Ilyitch could not at first catch the question that was asked him, but then he said, “No, have you seen her before?”
paras.uz: Fyodor Dmitriyevich Ivan Ilichdan Sara Bernarni ko'rganmi, deb so'radi. Ivan Ilich avvaliga unga berilgan savolni ilg'ay olmadi, keyin dedi: — Yo'q, siz uni avval ko'rganmisiz?

paras.en: “Yes, in Adrienne Lecouvreur.”
paras.uz: — Ha, «Adrienna Lekuvrer»da.

paras.en: Praskovya Fyodorovna observed that she was particularly good in that part. The daughter made some reply. A conversation sprang up about the art and naturalness of her acting, that conversation that is continually repeated and always the same.
paras.uz: Praskovya Fyodorovna u bu rolda ayniqsa yaxshi ekanini aytdi. Qizi nimadir deb javob berdi. Uning o'yinidagi san'at va tabiiylik haqida tinimsiz takrorlanadigan va doim bir xil bo'lgan o'sha suhbat boshlandi.

paras.en: In the middle of the conversation Fyodor Dmitryevitch glanced at Ivan Ilyitch and relapsed into silence. The others looked at him and became mute too. Ivan Ilyitch was staring with glittering eyes straight before him, obviously furious with them. This had to be set right, but it could not anyhow be set right. This silence had somehow to be broken. No one would venture on breaking it, and all began to feel alarmed that the decorous deception was somehow breaking down, and the facts would be exposed to all. Liza was the first to pluck up courage. She broke the silence. She tried to cover up what they were all feeling, but inadvertently she gave it utterance.
paras.uz: Suhbat o'rtasida Fyodor Dmitriyevich Ivan Ilichga qaradi va jim bo'lib qoldi. Boshqalar ham unga qarab, jim bo'lishdi. Ivan Ilich chaqnab turgan ko'zlari bilan to'g'ri oldiga tikilib turardi va ulardan g'azablangani aniq edi. Buni tuzatish kerak edi, lekin uni hech qanday tuzatib bo'lmasdi. Bu sukutni qandaydir buzish kerak edi. Hech kim uni buzishga jur'at etmasdi va hammasi odobli aldov qandaydir buzilayotganidan va faktlar hammaga ochilib qolishidan xavotirga tusha boshlashdi. Birinchi bo'lib Liza jur'at qildi. U sukutni buzdi. U hammasi his qilayotgan narsani yashirishga urindi, lekin beixtiyor uni ifodalab qo'ydi.

paras.en: “If we are going, though, it’s time to start,” she said, glancing at her watch, a gift from her father; and with a scarcely perceptible meaning smile to the young man, referring to something only known to themselves, she got up with a rustle of her skirts.
paras.uz: — Agar boradigan bo'lsak, yo'lga chiqish vaqti bo'ldi, — dedi u otasining sovg'asi bo'lgan soatiga qarab; va yigitga faqat ularning o'zlariga ma'lum bo'lgan bir narsaga ishora qilib, zo'rg'a seziladigan ma'noli jilmayib qo'yib, etaklarini shitirlatib o'rnidan turdi.

paras.en: They all got up, said goodbye, and went away. When they were gone, Ivan Ilyitch fancied he was easier; there was no falsity⁠—that had gone away with them, but the pain remained. That continual pain, that continual terror, made nothing harder, nothing easier. It was always worse.
paras.uz: Hammasi turishdi, xayrlashishdi va chiqib ketishdi. Ular ketgach, Ivan Ilichga yengilroq bo'lgandek tuyuldi; soxtalik yo'q edi — u ular bilan ketdi, lekin og'riq qoldi. O'sha doimiy og'riq, o'sha doimiy dahshat hech narsani qiyinroq ham, yengilroq ham qilmasdi. Doim yomonroq edi.

paras.en: Again came minute after minute, hour after hour, still the same and still no end, and ever more terrible the inevitable end.
paras.uz: Yana daqiqa ketidan daqiqa, soat ketidan soat keldi, hamon o'sha-o'sha va hamon oxiri yo'q, muqarrar oxir esa tobora dahshatliroq.

chapters.title: IX. The voice of the soul

paras.en: Late at night his wife came back. She came in on tiptoe, but he heard her, opened his eyes, and made haste to close them again. She wanted to send away Gerasim and sit up with him herself instead. He opened his eyes and said, “No, go away.”
paras.uz: Kechasi kech xotini qaytib keldi. U oyoq uchida kirdi, lekin u eshitdi, ko'zlarini ochdi va ularni yana yumishga shoshildi. Xotini Gerasimni jo'natib, uning o'rniga o'zi u bilan tun bo'yi o'tirmoqchi edi. U ko'zlarini ochib: «Yo'q, ket», dedi.

paras.en: “Are you in great pain?”
paras.uz: — Og'riq qattiqmi?

paras.en: “Always the same.”
paras.uz: — Doim o'sha-o'sha.

paras.en: “Take some opium.”
paras.uz: — Afyun iching.

paras.en: He agreed, and drank it. She went away.
paras.uz: U rozi bo'ldi va ichdi. Xotini chiqib ketdi.

paras.en: Till three o’clock he slept a miserable sleep. It seemed to him that he and his pain were being thrust somewhere into a narrow, deep, black sack, and they kept pushing him further and further in, and still could not thrust him to the bottom. And this operation was awful to him, and was accompanied with agony. And he was afraid, and yet wanted to fall into it, and struggled and yet tried to get into it. And all of a sudden he slipped and fell and woke up. Gerasim, still the same, is sitting at the foot of the bed half-dozing peacefully, patient. And he is lying with his wasted legs clad in stockings, raised on Gerasim’s shoulders, the same candle burning in the alcove, and the same interminable pain.
paras.uz: Soat uchgacha u azobli uyqu bilan uxladi. Unga o'zini va og'rig'ini qayergadir tor, chuqur, qora qopga tiqishayotgandek, uni tobora ichkariroq itarishayotgandek, lekin baribir tubigacha tiqa olmayotgandek tuyuldi. Va bu jarayon unga dahshatli edi va azob bilan birga kechardi. U qo'rqardi, lekin ayni paytda unga tushib ketishni istardi, kurashardi-yu, unga kirishga urinardi. Va birdan u sirpanib yiqildi va uyg'onib ketdi. Gerasim hamon o'sha-o'sha, karavotning oyoq tomonida tinch, sabr bilan mudrab o'tiribdi. U esa paypoq kiygan ozg'in oyoqlarini Gerasimning yelkalariga ko'tarib yotibdi, xonaning chuqurligida o'sha sham yonib turibdi va o'sha tugamas og'riq.

paras.en: “Go away, Gerasim,” he whispered.
paras.uz: — Ket, Gerasim, — pichirladi u.

paras.en: “It’s all right, sir. I’ll stay a bit longer.”
paras.uz: — Hechqisi yo'q, taqsir. Yana biroz o'tiraman.

paras.en: “No, go away.”
paras.uz: — Yo'q, ket.

paras.en: He took his legs down, lay sideways on his arm, and he felt very sorry for himself. He only waited till Gerasim had gone away into the next room; he could restrain himself no longer, and cried like a child. He cried at his own helplessness, at his awful loneliness, at the cruelty of people, at the cruelty of God, at the absence of God.
paras.uz: U oyoqlarini tushirdi, qo'liga yonboshlab yotdi va o'ziga juda achinib ketdi. U faqat Gerasim qo'shni xonaga chiqib ketishini kutdi; endi o'zini tuta olmadi va boladek yig'ladi. U o'zining ojizligiga, dahshatli yolg'izligiga, odamlarning shafqatsizligiga, Xudoning shafqatsizligiga, Xudoning yo'qligiga yig'ladi.

paras.en: “Why hast Thou done all this? What brought me to this? Why, why torture me so horribly?”
paras.uz: «Nega Sen bularning hammasini qilding? Meni bu holga nima olib keldi? Nega, nega meni shunchalik dahshatli qiynaysan?»

paras.en: He did not expect an answer, and wept indeed that there was and could be no answer. The pain grew more acute again, but he did not stir, did not call.
paras.uz: U javob kutmadi va haqiqatan ham javob yo'qligi va bo'lishi mumkin emasligi uchun yig'ladi. Og'riq yana kuchaydi, lekin u qimirlamadi, chaqirmadi.

paras.en: He said to himself, “Come, more then; come, strike me! But what for? What have I done to Thee? what for?”
paras.uz: U o'ziga dedi: «Qani, yana; qani, ur meni! Lekin nima uchun? Men Senga nima qildim? Nima uchun?»

paras.en: Then he was still, ceased weeping, held his breath, and was all attention; he listened, as it were, not to a voice uttering sounds, but to the voice of his soul, to the current of thoughts that rose up within him.
paras.uz: Keyin u tinchidi, yig'idan to'xtadi, nafasini ichiga yutdi va butunlay diqqatga aylandi; u go'yo tovush chiqarayotgan ovozni emas, qalbining ovozini, ichida ko'tarilayotgan fikrlar oqimini tinglardi.

paras.en: “What is it you want?” was the first clear idea able to be put into words that he grasped.
paras.uz: «Senga nima kerak?» — bu u ilg'agan, so'z bilan ifodalash mumkin bo'lgan birinchi aniq fikr edi.

paras.en: “What? Not to suffer, to live,” he answered.
paras.uz: «Nima? Azob chekmaslik, yashash», deb javob berdi u.

paras.en: And again he was utterly plunged into attention so intense that even the pain did not distract him.
paras.uz: Va yana u shunchalik kuchli diqqatga butunlay sho'ng'idiki, hatto og'riq ham uni chalg'itmadi.

paras.en: “To live? Live how?” the voice of his soul was asking.
paras.uz: «Yashashmi? Qanday yashash?» — so'rardi qalbining ovozi.

paras.en: “Why, live as I used to live before⁠—happily and pleasantly.”
paras.uz: «Axir, ilgari qanday yashagan bo'lsam, shunday — baxtli va yoqimli.»

paras.en: “As you used to live before⁠—happily and pleasantly?” queried the voice. And he began going over in his imagination the best moments of his pleasant life. But, strange to say, all these best moments of his pleasant life seemed now not at all what they had seemed then. All⁠—except the first memories of childhood⁠—there, in his childhood there had been something really pleasant in which one could have lived if it had come back. But the creature who had this pleasant experience was no more; it was like a memory of someone else.
paras.uz: «Ilgari qanday yashagan bo'lsang, shundaymi — baxtli va yoqimli?» — so'radi ovoz. Va u xayolida yoqimli hayotining eng yaxshi lahzalarini ko'zdan kechira boshladi. Lekin, g'alati, yoqimli hayotining bu eng yaxshi lahzalarining hammasi endi o'shanda tuyulganidek umuman emas edi. Hammasi — bolalikning ilk xotiralaridan tashqari — o'sha yerda, bolaligida haqiqatan ham yoqimli nimadir bor edi, agar u qaytib kelsa, u bilan yashash mumkin bo'lardi. Lekin bu yoqimli tajribani boshdan kechirgan mavjudot endi yo'q edi; bu boshqa birovning xotirasiga o'xshardi.

paras.en: As soon as he reached the beginning of what had resulted in him as he was now, Ivan Ilyitch, all that had seemed joys to him then now melted away before his eyes and were transformed into something trivial, and often disgusting.
paras.uz: Hozirgi u — Ivan Ilichni hosil qilgan narsaning boshlanishiga yetishi bilanoq, o'shanda unga quvonch bo'lib tuyulgan hamma narsa endi ko'z oldida erib ketar va arzimas, ko'pincha jirkanch narsaga aylanardi.

paras.en: And the further he went from childhood, the nearer to the actual present, the more worthless and uncertain were the joys. It began with life at the school of jurisprudence. Then there had still been something genuinely good; then there had been gaiety; then there had been friendship; then there had been hopes. But in the higher classes these good moments were already becoming rarer. Later on, during the first period of his official life, at the governor’s, good moments appeared; but it was all mixed, and less and less of it was good. And further on even less was good, and the further he went the less good there was.
paras.uz: Va bolalikdan qanchalik uzoqlashsa, haqiqiy hozirgi kunga qanchalik yaqinlashsa, quvonchlar shunchalik qadrsiz va noaniq edi. Bu huquqshunoslik maktabidagi hayotdan boshlandi. O'shanda hali haqiqatan yaxshi nimadir bor edi; o'shanda quvnoqlik bor edi; o'shanda do'stlik bor edi; o'shanda umidlar bor edi. Lekin yuqori sinflarda bu yaxshi lahzalar allaqachon kamayib borardi. Keyin, xizmat hayotining birinchi davrida, gubernatorning huzurida yaxshi lahzalar paydo bo'ldi; lekin hammasi aralash edi va yaxshisi tobora kamroq edi. Keyinroq yaxshisi yanada kamroq edi va qanchalik uzoqqa borsa, yaxshisi shunchalik kam edi.

paras.en: His marriage⁠ ⁠… as gratuitous as the disillusion of it and the smell of his wife’s breath and the sensuality, the hypocrisy! And that deadly official life, and anxiety about money, and so for one year, and two, and ten, and twenty, and always the same thing. And the further he went, the more deadly it became. “As though I had been going steadily downhill, imagining that I was going uphill. So it was in fact. In public opinion I was going uphill, and steadily as I got up it life was ebbing away from me.⁠ ⁠… And now the work’s done, there’s only to die.”
paras.uz: Uylanishi… uning ko'ngil qolishi kabi bexosdan, xotinining nafasining hidi, nafs, ikkiyuzlamachilik! Va o'sha o'likdek xizmat hayoti, pul tashvishi, va shunday bir yil, ikki yil, o'n yil, yigirma yil, va doim o'sha-o'sha. Va qanchalik uzoqqa borsa, shunchalik o'likroq bo'ldi. «Go'yo men tepaga ko'tarilyapman, deb tasavvur qilib, to'xtovsiz pastga tushib borgandekman. Aslida shunday bo'lgan. Jamoatchilik fikrida men tepaga ko'tarilardim va ko'tarilganim sari hayot mendan oqib ketardi… Endi esa ish tugadi, faqat o'lish qoldi.»

paras.en: “But what is this? What for? It cannot be! It cannot be that life has been so senseless, so loathsome? And if it really was so loathsome and senseless, then why die, and die in agony? There’s something wrong.”
paras.uz: «Lekin bu nima? Nima uchun? Bo'lishi mumkin emas! Bo'lishi mumkin emas, hayot shunchalik ma'nosiz, shunchalik jirkanch bo'lgan bo'lsa! Agar u haqiqatan shunchalik jirkanch va ma'nosiz bo'lgan bo'lsa, unda nega o'lish kerak, azob ichida o'lish kerak? Nimadir noto'g'ri.»

paras.en: “Can it be I have not lived as one ought?” suddenly came into his head. “But how not so, when I’ve done everything as it should be done?” he said, and at once dismissed this only solution of all the enigma of life and death as something utterly out of the question.
paras.uz: «Nahotki men qanday yashash kerak bo'lsa, shunday yashamagan bo'lsam?» — birdan xayoliga keldi. «Lekin qanday qilib bunday bo'lmasin, axir men hamma narsani qanday qilish kerak bo'lsa, shunday qilgan bo'lsam?» — dedi u va hayot va o'limning butun jumbog'ining bu yagona yechimini mutlaqo imkonsiz narsa sifatida darhol chetga surdi.

paras.en: “What do you want now? To live? Live how? Live as you live at the courts when the usher booms out: ‘The judge is coming!’⁠ ⁠… The judge is coming, the judge is coming,” he repeated to himself. “Here he is, the judge! But I’m not to blame!” he shrieked in fury. “What’s it for?” And he left off crying, and turning with his face to the wall, fell to pondering always on the same question, “What for, why all this horror?”
paras.uz: «Endi senga nima kerak? Yashashmi? Qanday yashash? Sud ijrochisi «Sud keladi!» deb baqirganda sudda qanday yashasang, shundaymi?… Sud keladi, sud keladi», deb takrorladi u o'ziga. «Mana u, sud! Lekin men aybdor emasman!» — deb qichqirdi u g'azab bilan. «Nima uchun?» Va u yig'idan to'xtab, yuzini devorga o'girib, doim o'sha bitta savol ustida o'ylay boshladi: «Nima uchun, nega bu dahshat?»

paras.en: But however much he pondered, he could not find an answer. And whenever the idea struck him, as it often did, that it all came of his never having lived as he ought, he thought of all the correctness of his life and dismissed this strange idea.
paras.uz: Lekin qanchalik o'ylamasin, javob topa olmadi. Va xayoliga, tez-tez kelganidek, hammasi u qanday yashash kerak bo'lsa, shunday yashamaganidan kelib chiqqan, degan fikr kelganida, u hayotining butun to'g'riligini eslar va bu g'alati fikrni haydardi.

chapters.title: X. The falling stone

paras.en: Another fortnight had passed. Ivan Ilyitch could not now get up from the sofa. He did not like lying in bed, and lay on the sofa. And lying almost all the time facing the wall, in loneliness he suffered all the inexplicable agonies, and in loneliness pondered always that inexplicable question. What is it? Can it be true that it’s death? And an inner voice answered, “Yes, it is true.” “Why these agonies?” and a voice answered, “For no reason.” Beyond and besides this there was nothing.
paras.uz: Yana ikki hafta o'tdi. Ivan Ilich endi divandan tura olmasdi. U to'shakda yotishni yoqtirmasdi va divanda yotardi. Va deyarli butun vaqt yuzini devorga qaratib yotib, yolg'izlikda tushunib bo'lmas barcha azoblarni chekar va yolg'izlikda doim o'sha tushunib bo'lmas savol ustida o'ylardi. Bu nima? Nahotki bu haqiqatan o'lim bo'lsa? Va ichki ovoz javob berardi: «Ha, bu haqiqat.» «Nega bu azoblar?» Va ovoz javob berardi: «Hech sababsiz.» Bundan narida va bundan tashqari hech narsa yo'q edi.

paras.en: From the very beginning of his illness, ever since Ivan Ilyitch first went to the doctors, his life had been split up into two contradictory moods, which were continually alternating⁠—one was despair and the anticipation of an uncomprehended and awful death; the other was hope and an absorbed watching over the actual condition of his body. First there was nothing confronting him but a kidney or intestine which had temporarily declined to perform their duties, then there was nothing but unknown awful death, which there was no escaping.
paras.uz: Kasalligining eng boshidan, Ivan Ilich doktorlarga birinchi marta borgan paytdan beri uning hayoti tinimsiz almashinib turgan ikki qarama-qarshi kayfiyatga bo'linib ketgan edi — biri umidsizlik va tushunilmagan, dahshatli o'limni kutish; ikkinchisi umid va tanasining haqiqiy holatini berilib kuzatish. Goh uning oldida faqat vaqtincha o'z vazifasini bajarishdan bosh tortgan buyrak yoki ichak turardi, goh esa qochib qutulib bo'lmaydigan noma'lum, dahshatli o'limdan boshqa hech narsa yo'q edi.

paras.en: These two moods had alternated from the very beginning of the illness; but the further the illness progressed, the more doubtful and fantastic became the conception of the kidney, and the more real the sense of approaching death.
paras.uz: Bu ikki kayfiyat kasallikning eng boshidan almashinib turardi; lekin kasallik qanchalik rivojlansa, buyrak haqidagi tasavvur shunchalik shubhali va xayoliy, yaqinlashib kelayotgan o'lim hissi esa shunchalik haqiqiy bo'lib bordi.

paras.en: He had but to reflect on what he had been three months before and what he was now, to reflect how steadily he had been going downhill, for every possibility of hope to be shattered.
paras.uz: Uch oy oldin qanday bo'lganini va hozir qanday ekanini, qanchalik to'xtovsiz pastga tushib borganini o'ylashi kifoya edi — umidning har qanday imkoniyati chil-chil sinishi uchun.

paras.en: Of late, in the loneliness in which he found himself, lying with his face to the back of the sofa, a loneliness in the middle of a populous town and of his numerous acquaintances and his family, a loneliness than which none more complete could be found anywhere⁠—not at the bottom of the sea, not deep down in the earth;⁠—of late in this fearful loneliness Ivan Ilyitch had lived only in imagination in the past. One by one the pictures of his past rose up before him. It always began from what was nearest in time and went back to the most remote, to childhood, and rested there. If Ivan Ilyitch thought of the stewed prunes that had been offered him for dinner that day, his mind went back to the damp, wrinkled French plum of his childhood, of its peculiar taste and the flow of saliva when the stone was sucked; and along with this memory of a taste there rose up a whole series of memories of that period⁠—his nurse, his brother, his playthings. “I mustn’t⁠ ⁠… it’s too painful,” Ivan Ilyitch said to himself, and he brought himself back to the present. The button on the back of the sofa and the creases in the morocco. “Morocco’s dear, and doesn’t wear well; there was a quarrel over it. But the morocco was different, and different too the quarrel when we tore father’s portfolio and were punished, and mamma bought us the tarts.” And again his mind rested on his childhood, and again it was painful, and he tried to drive it away and think of something else.
paras.uz: So'nggi paytlarda, o'zi tushib qolgan yolg'izlikda, yuzini divan suyanchig'iga qaratib yotarkan — gavjum shahar, ko'p sonli tanishlari va oilasi orasidagi yolg'izlik, undan to'liqroq yolg'izlikni hech qayerda — na dengiz tubida, na yer qa'rida — topib bo'lmasdi — so'nggi paytlarda bu dahshatli yolg'izlikda Ivan Ilich faqat xayolan o'tmishda yashardi. O'tmishining manzaralari birin-ketin uning ko'z oldida paydo bo'lardi. Bu doim vaqt jihatidan eng yaqin narsadan boshlanib, eng uzoqqa, bolalikka qaytib borar va o'sha yerda to'xtardi. Agar Ivan Ilich o'sha kuni tushlikka taklif qilingan qaynatilgan olxo'ri haqida o'ylasa, xayoli bolaligidagi nam, burishgan fransuz olxo'risiga, uning o'ziga xos ta'miga va danagini so'rganda og'izdan oqadigan so'lakka qaytardi; va ta'mning bu xotirasi bilan birga o'sha davrning butun bir xotiralar qatori — enagasi, akasi, o'yinchoqlari — ko'tarilardi. «Kerak emas… bu juda og'riqli», derdi Ivan Ilich o'ziga va o'zini hozirgi kunga qaytarardi. Divan suyanchig'idagi tugma va saxtiyondagi burmalar. «Saxtiyon qimmat va chidamsiz; u tufayli janjal bo'lgan edi. Lekin saxtiyon ham boshqa edi, janjal ham boshqa edi — otamizning portfelini yirtib, jazolanganimizda, onam esa bizga pirog olib kelganida.» Va yana xayoli bolaligida to'xtardi va yana og'riqli bo'lardi va u uni haydab, boshqa narsa haqida o'ylashga urinardi.

paras.en: And again at that point, together with that chain of associations, quite another chain of memories came into his heart, of how his illness had grown up and become more acute. It was the same there, the further back the more life there had been. There had been both more that was good in life and more of life itself. And the two began to melt into one. “Just as the pain goes on getting worse and worse, so has my whole life gone on getting worse and worse,” he thought. One light spot was there at the back, at the beginning of life, and then it kept getting blacker and blacker, and going faster and faster. “In inverse ratio to the square of the distance from death,” thought Ivan Ilyitch. And the image of a stone falling downwards with increasing velocity sank into his soul. Life, a series of increasing sufferings, falls more and more swiftly to the end, the most fearful sufferings. “I am falling.” He shuddered, shifted himself, would have resisted, but he knew beforehand that he could not resist; and again, with eyes weary with gazing at it, but unable not to gaze at what was before him, he stared at the back of the sofa and waited, waited expecting that fearful fall and shock and dissolution. “Resistance is impossible,” he said to himself. “But if one could at least comprehend what it’s for? Even that’s impossible. It could be explained if one were to say that I hadn’t lived as I ought. But that can’t be alleged,” he said to himself, thinking of all the regularity, correctness, and propriety of his life. “That really can’t be admitted,” he said to himself, his lips smiling ironically as though someone could see his smile and be deceived by it. “No explanation! Agony, death.⁠ ⁠… What for?”
paras.uz: Va yana shu yerda, o'sha xotiralar zanjiri bilan birga, uning qalbiga butunlay boshqa xotiralar zanjiri — kasalligi qanday o'sib, qanday kuchaygani haqidagi xotiralar kelardi. U yerda ham xuddi shunday edi: qanchalik orqaga borsa, shunchalik ko'p hayot bor edi. Hayotda yaxshi narsa ham ko'proq, hayotning o'zi ham ko'proq bo'lgan. Va ikkalasi birlashib, bitta bo'la boshladi. «Og'riq tobora yomonlashib borayotganidek, butun hayotim ham tobora yomonlashib borgan», deb o'yladi u. Orqada, hayotning boshida bitta yorug' nuqta bor edi, keyin u tobora qorayib, tobora tezlashib borardi. «O'limgacha bo'lgan masofaning kvadratiga teskari proporsional», deb o'yladi Ivan Ilich. Va tobora ortib borayotgan tezlik bilan pastga qulayotgan tosh obrazi uning qalbiga cho'kdi. Tobora kuchayib boradigan azoblar qatori bo'lgan hayot oxirga, eng dahshatli azoblarga tobora tezroq qulaydi. «Men qulayapman.» U seskanib ketdi, qimirladi, qarshilik qilmoqchi bo'ldi, lekin qarshilik qila olmasligini oldindan bilardi; va yana unga tikilishdan charchagan, lekin oldidagi narsaga tikilmaslikka qodir bo'lmagan ko'zlari bilan divan suyanchig'iga tikilib, o'sha dahshatli qulash, zarba va parchalanishni kutib turdi. «Qarshilik qilish imkonsiz, — dedi u o'ziga. — Lekin hech bo'lmasa bu nima uchun ekanini tushunsa bo'lardi-ku? Hatto bu ham imkonsiz. Agar men qanday yashash kerak bo'lsa, shunday yashamaganman, desa, buni tushuntirish mumkin bo'lardi. Lekin buni da'vo qilib bo'lmaydi», dedi u o'ziga hayotining butun muntazamligi, to'g'riligi va odobini eslab. «Buni haqiqatan ham tan olib bo'lmaydi», dedi u o'ziga, lablari kinoyali jilmayib — go'yo kimdir uning jilmayishini ko'rib, aldanishi mumkindek. «Izoh yo'q! Azob, o'lim… Nima uchun?»

chapters.recap_uz: Divanga qarab yotgan Ivan Ilich faqat o'tmishda yashaydi: qaynatilgan olxo'ri bolalikdagi fransuz olxo'risini eslatadi. Hayoti og'riq kabi tobora yomonlashib borgan: boshida bitta yorug' nuqta, keyin tobora qora va tobora tez — tezligi oshib borayotgan qulayotgan tosh kabi.

chapters.title: XI. Not the right thing

paras.en: So passed a fortnight. During that fortnight an event occurred that had been desired by Ivan Ilyitch and his wife. Petrishtchev made a formal proposal. This took place in the evening. Next day Praskovya Fyodorovna went in to her husband, revolving in her mind how to inform him of Fyodor Dmitryevitch’s proposal, but that night there had been a change for the worse in Ivan Ilyitch. Praskovya Fyodorovna found him on the same sofa, but in a different position. He was lying on his face, groaning, and staring straight before him with a fixed gaze.
paras.uz: Shunday qilib ikki hafta o'tdi. O'sha ikki hafta ichida Ivan Ilich va uning xotini istagan voqea yuz berdi. Petrishchev rasman sovchi qo'ydi. Bu kechqurun bo'ldi. Ertasi kuni Praskovya Fyodorovna Fyodor Dmitriyevichning taklifi haqida unga qanday xabar berishni o'ylab, erining oldiga kirdi, lekin o'sha tunda Ivan Ilichning ahvoli yomonlashgan edi. Praskovya Fyodorovna uni o'sha divanda, lekin boshqa holatda topdi. U yuztuban yotib, ingrar va qotib qolgan nigoh bilan to'g'ri oldiga tikilib turardi.

paras.en: She began talking of remedies. He turned his stare on her. She did not finish what she had begun saying; such hatred of her in particular was expressed in that stare.
paras.uz: U dori-darmonlar haqida gapira boshladi. U nigohini unga qaratdi. U boshlagan gapini tugatmadi; o'sha nigohda aynan unga nisbatan shunday nafrat ifodalangan edi.

paras.en: “For Christ’s sake, let me die in peace,” he said.
paras.uz: — Xudo haqqi, meni tinch o'lishga qo'ying, — dedi u.

paras.en: She would have gone away, but at that moment the daughter came in and went up to say good morning to him. He looked at his daughter just as at his wife, and to her inquiries how he was, he told her drily that they would soon all be rid of him. Both were silent, sat a little while, and went out.
paras.uz: U chiqib ketmoqchi edi, lekin shu payt qizi kirdi va unga salom berish uchun yaqin keldi. U qiziga ham xuddi xotiniga qaragandek qaradi va ahvolini so'raganiga quruqqina tez orada hammalari undan qutulishlarini aytdi. Ikkalasi jim bo'lib, biroz o'tirishdi va chiqib ketishdi.

paras.en: “How are we to blame?” said Liza to her mother. “As though we had done it! I’m sorry for papa, but why punish us?”
paras.uz: — Bizning nima aybimiz bor? — dedi Liza onasiga. — Go'yo biz qilgandek! Dadamga achinaman, lekin nega bizni jazolaydi?

paras.en: At the usual hour the doctor came. Ivan Ilyitch answered, “Yes, no,” never taking his exasperated stare from him, and towards the end he said, “Why, you know that you can do nothing, so let me be.”
paras.uz: Odatdagi soatda doktor keldi. Ivan Ilich g'azablangan nigohini undan uzmay, «Ha, yo'q», deb javob berdi, oxirida esa dedi: — Axir, hech narsa qila olmasligingizni bilasiz-ku, meni tinch qo'ying.

paras.en: “We can relieve your suffering,” said the doctor.
paras.uz: — Biz azobingizni yengillashtira olamiz, — dedi doktor.

paras.en: “Even that you can’t do; let me be.”
paras.uz: — Hatto buni ham qila olmaysiz; meni tinch qo'ying.

paras.en: The doctor went into the drawing-room and told Praskovya Fyodorovna that it was very serious, and that the only resource left them was opium to relieve his sufferings, which must be terrible. The doctor said his physical sufferings were terrible, and that was true; but even more terrible than his physical sufferings were his mental sufferings, and in that lay his chief misery.
paras.uz: Doktor mehmonxonaga chiqib, Praskovya Fyodorovnaga ahvol juda jiddiy ekanini va ularga qolgan yagona chora — dahshatli bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan azoblarini yengillashtirish uchun afyun ekanini aytdi. Doktor uning jismoniy azoblari dahshatli ekanini aytdi va bu rost edi; lekin jismoniy azoblaridan ham dahshatliroq uning ruhiy azoblari edi va uning asosiy iztirobi aynan shunda edi.

paras.en: His moral sufferings were due to the fact that during that night, as he looked at the sleepy, good-natured, broad-cheeked face of Gerasim, the thought had suddenly come into his head, “What if in reality all my life, my conscious life, has been not the right thing?” The thought struck him that what he had regarded before as an utter impossibility, that he had spent his life not as he ought, might be the truth. It struck him that those scarcely detected impulses of struggle within him against what was considered good by persons of higher position, scarcely detected impulses which he had dismissed, that they might be the real thing, and everything else might be not the right thing. And his official work, and his ordering of his daily life and of his family, and these social and official interests⁠—all that might be not the right thing. He tried to defend it all to himself. And suddenly he felt all the weakness of what he was defending. And it was useless to defend it.
paras.uz: Uning ruhiy azoblari shundan ediki, o'sha tunda Gerasimning uyqusiragan, xushfe'l, keng yonoqli yuziga qararkan, birdan xayoliga shu fikr kelgan edi: «Agar aslida butun hayotim, ongli hayotim, to'g'ri narsa bo'lmagan bo'lsa-chi?» Ilgari mutlaqo imkonsiz deb hisoblagan narsa — hayotini qanday yashash kerak bo'lsa, shunday o'tkazmagani — haqiqat bo'lishi mumkin, degan fikr uni hayratga soldi. Yuqori mavqedagi odamlar yaxshi deb hisoblagan narsaga qarshi ichidagi zo'rg'a sezilgan kurash intilishlari, u chetga surib qo'ygan zo'rg'a sezilgan intilishlar — aynan ular haqiqiy narsa bo'lishi, qolgan hamma narsa esa to'g'ri narsa bo'lmasligi mumkin, degan fikr uni hayratga soldi. Uning xizmat ishi ham, kundalik hayoti va oilasini tartibga solishi ham, bu ijtimoiy va xizmat qiziqishlari ham — bularning hammasi to'g'ri narsa bo'lmasligi mumkin edi. U o'z oldida bularning hammasini himoya qilishga urindi. Va birdan u himoya qilayotgan narsasining butun zaifligini his qildi. Uni himoya qilishdan foyda yo'q edi.

paras.en: “But if it’s so,” he said to himself, “and I am leaving life with the consciousness that I have lost all that was given me, and there’s no correcting it, then what?” He lay on his back and began going over his whole life entirely anew. When he saw the footman in the morning, then his wife, then his daughter, then the doctor, every movement they made, every word they uttered, confirmed for him the terrible truth that had been revealed to him in the night. In them he saw himself, saw all in which he had lived, and saw distinctly that it was all not the right thing; it was a horrible, vast deception that concealed both life and death. This consciousness intensified his physical agonies, multiplied them tenfold. He groaned and tossed from side to side and pulled at the covering over him. It seemed to him that it was stifling him and weighing him down. And for that he hated them.
paras.uz: «Lekin agar shunday bo'lsa, — dedi u o'ziga, — va men menga berilgan hamma narsani yo'qotganimni va uni tuzatib bo'lmasligini anglab hayotdan ketayotgan bo'lsam, unda nima?» U chalqancha yotib, butun hayotini butunlay yangidan ko'zdan kechira boshladi. Ertalab malayni, keyin xotinini, keyin qizini, keyin doktorni ko'rganida, ularning har bir harakati, aytgan har bir so'zi unga tunda ochilgan dahshatli haqiqatni tasdiqladi. Ularda u o'zini ko'rdi, o'zi yashagan hamma narsani ko'rdi va hammasi to'g'ri narsa emasligini aniq ko'rdi; bu ham hayotni, ham o'limni yashirib turgan dahshatli, ulkan aldov edi. Bu anglash uning jismoniy azoblarini kuchaytirdi, ularni o'n baravar ko'paytirdi. U ingradi, u yonidan bu yoniga ag'darildi va ustidagi ko'rpani tortqiladi. Unga ko'rpa uni bo'g'ayotgandek va ezayotgandek tuyuldi. Va buning uchun u ularni yomon ko'rdi.

paras.en: They gave him a big dose of opium; he sank into unconsciousness; but at dinnertime the same thing began again. He drove them all away, and tossed from side to side.
paras.uz: Unga katta doza afyun berishdi; u hushsizlikka cho'mdi; lekin tushlik paytida xuddi shu narsa yana boshlandi. U hammasini haydab chiqardi va u yonidan bu yoniga ag'darildi.

paras.en: His wife came to him and said, “Jean, darling, do this for my sake” (for my sake?). “It can’t do harm, and it often does good. Why, it’s nothing. And often in health people⁠—”
paras.uz: Xotini uning oldiga kelib dedi: — Jean, jonim, buni men uchun qiling (men uchun?). Bu zarar qilmaydi, ko'pincha foyda beradi. Axir, bu hech narsa emas. Ko'pincha sog'lom odamlar ham…

paras.en: He opened his eyes wide.
paras.uz: U ko'zlarini katta ochdi.

paras.en: “What? Take the sacrament? What for? No. Besides⁠ ⁠…”
paras.uz: — Nima? Muqaddas tabarruk olishmi? Nima uchun? Yo'q. Buning ustiga…

paras.en: She began to cry.
paras.uz: U yig'lay boshladi.

paras.en: “Yes, my dear? I’ll send for our priest, he’s so nice.”
paras.uz: — Ha, jonim? Ruhoniyimizni chaqirtiraman, u shunday yoqimli.

paras.en: “All right, very well,” he said.
paras.uz: — Mayli, yaxshi, — dedi u.

paras.en: When the priest came and confessed him he was softened, felt as it were a relief from his doubts, and consequently from his sufferings, and there came a moment of hope. He began once more thinking of the intestinal appendix and the possibility of curing it. He took the sacrament with tears in his eyes.
paras.uz: Ruhoniy kelib, uning tavbasini tinglaganida, u yumshadi, go'yo shubhalaridan va natijada azoblaridan yengillik his qildi va bir lahzalik umid paydo bo'ldi. U yana ko'richak va uni davolash imkoniyati haqida o'ylay boshladi. U ko'zlarida yosh bilan tabarrukni qabul qildi.

paras.en: When they laid him down again after the sacrament for a minute, he felt comfortable, and again the hope of life sprang up. He began to think about the operation which had been suggested to him. “To live, I want to live,” he said to himself. His wife came in to congratulate him; she uttered the customary words and added⁠—
paras.uz: Tabarrukdan keyin uni yana yotqizishganida, bir daqiqa o'zini yaxshi his qildi va yana yashash umidi tug'ildi. U unga taklif qilingan operatsiya haqida o'ylay boshladi. «Yashash, yashashni istayman», dedi u o'ziga. Xotini uni tabriklash uchun kirdi; u odatiy so'zlarni aytdi va qo'shib qo'ydi:

paras.en: “It’s quite true, isn’t it, that you’re better?”
paras.uz: — Rostdan ham yaxshiroqsiz, a?

paras.en: Without looking at her, he said, “Yes.”
paras.uz: Unga qaramay, u: «Ha», dedi.

paras.en: Her dress, her figure, the expression of her face, the tone of her voice⁠—all told him the same: “Not the right thing. All that in which you lived and are living is lying, deceit, hiding life and death away from you.” And as soon as he had formed that thought, hatred sprang up in him, and with that hatred agonising physical sufferings, and with these sufferings the sense of inevitable, approaching ruin. Something new was happening; there were screwing and shooting pains, and a tightness in his breathing.
paras.uz: Uning ko'ylagi, qomati, yuzidagi ifoda, ovozining ohangi — hammasi unga bir xil narsani aytardi: «To'g'ri narsa emas. Sen yashagan va yashayotgan hamma narsa — yolg'on, aldov, hayotni ham, o'limni ham sendan yashiradi.» Va u bu fikrni shakllantirishi bilanoq, unda nafrat qo'zg'aldi, nafrat bilan birga azobli jismoniy qiynoqlar, bu qiynoqlar bilan birga esa muqarrar, yaqinlashib kelayotgan halokat hissi qo'zg'aldi. Yangi nimadir sodir bo'layotgan edi: buraluvchi va otiluvchi og'riqlar, nafasida siqilish paydo bo'ldi.

paras.en: The expression of his face as he uttered that “Yes” was terrible. After uttering that “Yes,” looking her straight in the face, he turned on to his face, with a rapidity extraordinary in his weakness, and shrieked⁠—
paras.uz: U o'sha «Ha»ni aytayotgandagi yuz ifodasi dahshatli edi. O'sha «Ha»ni aytib, unga to'g'ri yuziga qarab, u zaifligiga nisbatan g'ayrioddiy tezlik bilan yuztuban o'girildi va qichqirdi:

paras.en: “Go away, go away, let me be!”
paras.uz: — Ket, ket, meni tinch qo'y!

chapters.title: XII. Light

paras.en: From that moment there began the scream that never ceased for three days, and was so awful that through two closed doors one could not hear it without horror. At the moment when he answered his wife he grasped that he had fallen, that there was no return, that the end had come, quite the end, while doubt was still as unsolved, still remained doubt.
paras.uz: O'sha lahzadan boshlab uch kun to'xtamagan va shunchalik dahshatli bo'lgan qichqiriq boshlandiki, uni ikkita yopiq eshik orqali ham dahshatsiz eshitib bo'lmasdi. Xotiniga javob bergan lahzada u yiqilganini, qaytish yo'qligini, oxir kelganini, butunlay oxir kelganini angladi, shubha esa hamon hal bo'lmagan, hamon shubhaligicha qolgan edi.

paras.en: “Oo! Oo⁠—o! Oo!” he screamed in varying intonations. He had begun screaming, “I don’t want to!” and so had gone on screaming on the same vowel sound⁠—oo!
paras.uz: — U! U-u! U! — deb qichqirardi u turli ohanglarda. U «Istamayman!» deb qichqira boshlagan va shu tarzda o'sha unli tovushda — u! — qichqirishda davom etgan edi.

paras.en: All those three days, during which time did not exist for him, he was struggling in that black sack into which he was being thrust by an unseen resistless force. He struggled as the man condemned to death struggles in the hands of the executioner, knowing that he cannot save himself. And every moment he felt that in spite of all his efforts to struggle against it, he was getting nearer and nearer to what terrified him. He felt that his agony was due both to his being thrust into this black hole and still more to his not being able to get right into it. What hindered him from getting into it was the claim that his life had been good. That justification of his life held him fast and would not let him get forward, and it caused him more agony than all.
paras.uz: O'sha uch kun davomida, u uchun vaqt mavjud bo'lmagan o'sha kunlarda, u ko'rinmas, qarshilik qilib bo'lmas kuch uni itarayotgan o'sha qora qopda tipirchilardi. U o'limga hukm qilingan odam o'zini qutqara olmasligini bilib, jallodning qo'lida tipirchilaganidek tipirchilardi. Va har lahza u unga qarshi kurashish uchun barcha urinishlariga qaramay, uni dahshatga solayotgan narsaga tobora yaqinlashib borayotganini his qilardi. U azobi ham bu qora tuynukka itarilayotganidan, ham undan ko'ra ko'proq unga to'liq kira olmayotganidan ekanini his qilardi. Unga kirishga xalaqit berayotgan narsa — hayoti yaxshi bo'lgan, degan da'vo edi. Hayotining bu oqlanishi uni mahkam ushlab turardi, oldinga o'tishga qo'ymasdi va unga hammasidan ko'proq azob berardi.

paras.en: All at once some force struck him in the chest, in the side, and stifled his breathing more than ever; he rolled forward into the hole, and there at the end there was some sort of light. It had happened with him, as it had sometimes happened to him in a railway carriage, when he had thought he was going forward while he was going back, and all of a sudden recognised his real direction.
paras.uz: Birdan qandaydir kuch uni ko'kragiga, biqiniga urdi va nafasini yanada ko'proq bo'g'di; u tuynukka qulab tushdi va u yerda, oxirida qandaydir yorug'lik bor edi. Unda xuddi ba'zan temir yo'l vagonida bo'lganidek bo'ldi: u oldinga ketyapman deb o'ylagan, aslida esa orqaga ketayotgan va birdan haqiqiy yo'nalishini tanigan paytdagidek.

paras.en: “Yes, it has all been not the right thing,” he said to himself, “but that’s no matter.” He could, he could do the right thing. “What is the right thing?” he asked himself, and suddenly he became quiet.
paras.uz: «Ha, hammasi to'g'ri narsa bo'lmagan, — dedi u o'ziga, — lekin bu muhim emas.» U to'g'ri narsani qila olardi, qila olardi. «To'g'ri narsa nima?» — deb so'radi u o'zidan va birdan tinchib qoldi.

paras.en: This was at the end of the third day, two hours before his death. At that very moment the schoolboy had stealthily crept into his father’s room and gone up to his bedside. The dying man was screaming and waving his arms. His hand fell on the schoolboy’s head. The boy snatched it, pressed it to his lips, and burst into tears.
paras.uz: Bu uchinchi kunning oxirida, o'limidan ikki soat oldin edi. Aynan o'sha lahzada gimnazist o'g'il otasining xonasiga sekin sudralib kirib, karavoti yoniga borgan edi. O'layotgan odam qichqirar va qo'llarini silkitardi. Uning qo'li gimnazistning boshiga tushdi. Bola uni ushlab oldi, lablariga bosdi va yig'lab yubordi.

paras.en: At that very moment Ivan Ilyitch had rolled into the hole, and caught sight of the light, and it was revealed to him that his life had not been what it ought to have been, but that that could still be set right. He asked himself, “What is the right thing?”⁠—and became quiet, listening. Then he felt someone was kissing his hand. He opened his eyes and glanced at his son. He felt sorry for him. His wife went up to him. He glanced at her. She was gazing at him with open mouth, the tears unwiped streaming over her nose and cheeks, a look of despair on her face. He felt sorry for her.
paras.uz: Aynan o'sha lahzada Ivan Ilich tuynukka qulab tushgan va yorug'likni ko'rgan edi, va unga hayoti qanday bo'lishi kerak bo'lsa, shunday bo'lmagani, lekin buni hali tuzatish mumkinligi ayon bo'ldi. U o'zidan so'radi: «To'g'ri narsa nima?» — va tinglab, tinchib qoldi. Keyin kimdir qo'lini o'payotganini his qildi. U ko'zlarini ochib, o'g'liga qaradi. Unga achindi. Xotini uning oldiga keldi. U unga qaradi. Xotini og'zini ochib, burni va yonoqlari bo'ylab artilmagan ko'z yoshlari oqib, yuzida umidsizlik ifodasi bilan unga tikilib turardi. Unga achindi.

paras.en: “Yes, I’m making them miserable,” he thought. “They’re sorry, but it will be better for them when I die.” He would have said this, but had not the strength to utter it. “Besides, why speak, I must act,” he thought. With a glance to his wife he pointed to his son and said⁠—
paras.uz: «Ha, men ularni baxtsiz qilyapman, — deb o'yladi u. — Ularga achinarli, lekin men o'lsam, ular uchun yaxshiroq bo'ladi.» U buni aytmoqchi edi, lekin aytishga kuchi yetmadi. «Buning ustiga, nega gapirish kerak, harakat qilishim kerak», deb o'yladi u. Xotiniga nigoh tashlab, o'g'liga ishora qildi va dedi:

paras.en: “Take away⁠ ⁠… sorry for him.⁠ ⁠… And you too⁠ ⁠…” He tried to say “forgive,” but said “forgo”⁠ ⁠… and too weak to correct himself, shook his hand, knowing that He would understand whose understanding mattered.
paras.uz: — Olib chiq… achinarli… Senga ham… — U «kechir» demoqchi bo'ldi, lekin «ketir» dedi… va o'zini tuzatishga kuchi yetmay, qo'lini siltadi — tushunishi muhim bo'lgan Zot tushunishini bilib.

paras.en: And all at once it became clear to him that what had tortured him and would not leave him was suddenly dropping away all at once on both sides and on ten sides and on all sides. He was sorry for them, must act so that they might not suffer. Set them free and be free himself of those agonies. “How right and how simple!” he thought. “And the pain?” he asked himself. “Where’s it gone? Eh, where are you, pain?”
paras.uz: Va birdan unga ravshan bo'ldiki, uni qiynagan va tark etmagan narsa birdaniga ikki tomondan, o'n tomondan, har tomondan tushib ketyapti. U ularga achinardi, ular azob chekmasligi uchun harakat qilishi kerak edi. Ularni ozod qilish va o'zi ham bu azoblardan ozod bo'lish. «Naqadar to'g'ri va naqadar oddiy!» deb o'yladi u. «Og'riq-chi? — so'radi u o'zidan. — U qayerga ketdi? Hoy, qayerdasan, og'riq?»

paras.en: He began to watch for it.
paras.uz: U uni kuta boshladi.

paras.en: “Yes, here it is. Well what of it, let the pain be.”
paras.uz: «Ha, mana u. Xo'sh, nima bo'pti, og'riq bo'laversin.»

paras.en: “And death. Where is it?”
paras.uz: «O'lim-chi? U qayerda?»

paras.en: He looked for his old accustomed terror of death, and did not find it. “Where is it? What death?” There was no terror, because death was not either.
paras.uz: U o'zining eski, odatiy o'lim qo'rquvini izladi va uni topmadi. «U qayerda? Qanday o'lim?» Qo'rquv yo'q edi, chunki o'lim ham yo'q edi.

paras.en: In the place of death there was light.
paras.uz: O'limning o'rnida yorug'lik bor edi.

paras.en: “So this is it!” he suddenly exclaimed aloud.
paras.uz: — Demak, mana u! — dedi u birdan ovoz chiqarib.

paras.en: “What joy!”
paras.uz: — Naqadar quvonch!

paras.en: To him all this passed in a single instant, and the meaning of that instant suffered no change after. For those present his agony lasted another two hours. There was a rattle in his throat, a twitching in his wasted body. Then the rattle and the gasping came at longer and longer intervals.
paras.uz: Uning uchun bularning hammasi bir lahzada o'tdi va bu lahzaning ma'nosi keyin hech qanday o'zgarmadi. Hozir bo'lganlar uchun uning jon talvasasi yana ikki soat davom etdi. Uning tomog'ida xirillash bor edi, ozib ketgan tanasida tortishish bor edi. Keyin xirillash va hansirash tobora uzoqroq oraliqlar bilan keldi.

paras.en: “It is over!” someone said over him.
paras.uz: — Tugadi! — dedi kimdir uning ustida.

paras.en: He caught those words and repeated them in his soul.
paras.uz: U bu so'zlarni ilg'ab oldi va qalbida takrorladi.

paras.en: “Death is over,” he said to himself. “It’s no more.”
paras.uz: «O'lim tugadi, — dedi u o'ziga. — U endi yo'q.»

paras.en: He drew in a breath, stopped midway in the breath, stretched and died.
paras.uz: U nafas oldi, nafasning yarmida to'xtadi, cho'zildi va o'ldi.

chapters.recap_uz: Uch kun qichqiriq. U qora tuynukka kira olmaydi, chunki hayotini «yaxshi» deb oqlab turadi. Oxirida u tuynukka quladi va yorug'likni ko'radi: hayoti to'g'ri bo'lmagan, lekin buni hali tuzatish mumkin. O'g'li qo'lini o'padi, u xotini va o'g'liga achinadi. Og'riq qoladi, lekin o'lim qo'rquvi yo'qoladi: o'lim o'rnida yorug'lik. «O'lim tugadi.»
